author: ALR Editors
title: Announcing Asian Labour School Oct-Nov 2026 Semester
content:
Dear friends,


We are back with an amazing list of new and returning courses for the Asian Labour School. If you are interested in

acquiring democratic facilitation skills, navigating conflicts and taking collective care, working cooperatively, strengthening a union core or leading your own radical walking tours

, please check out the course information below and study with Asian Labour School.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Chie Matsumoto


We all have attended meetings where decisions were made by only a few members, most outspoken ones or someone at the top. We may have once thought, “Why am I even here?” and left without saying a word. Democracy starts in the smallest conversations, dialogues and meetings by raking in most diverse opinions and ideas, piecing them together to create something new and meaningful to all participants.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Facilitators: Emi Do and Matt Noyes


Worker cooperatives are enterprises that are owned and governed by workers. When all of our working experiences have been in profit-maximizing enterprises, or in workplaces that are structured hierarchically, it is no wonder that we can encounter challenges when attempting to work together cooperatively. In this course we will explore the challenges and tensions when there are no bosses to hate!


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Facilitator: Nash Tysmans


Movements are built through relationships. Yet the pressures of organizing (urgency, conflict, exhaustion, political disagreement, and unequal power) can strain those relationships and undermine our collective capacity. How can we build movements that are both effective in challenging injustice and caring in how we work together?


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Sithar Chhim


In order to win any campaign at workplace, unions need to be strong enough to pressure the company. Building a strong and representative committee is the only way to win over the bosses who have well organized structure at workplace compare to workers.


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)


Facilitator: Kevin Lin


Have you ever thought about leading your own radical walking tour to share with friends the significance of places and histories in your city? Leading and participating in a radical walking tour is not only educational but fun and always memorable. A walking tour provides a concrete sense of places, people, and histories. This course will walk you through the conceptualisation, research and logistics of a radical walking tour, and hear ideas and experiences from other participants across Asia.


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)

author: karapatan
title: Primer on Desaparecidos
content: ANG SAPILITANG PAGKAWALA O ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCE ay isa sa pinakamalubhang paglabag sa karapatang pantao. Hindi ito simpleng pagkawala ng tao – ito ay sistematikong pagdukot, pagpapahirap at pagtatago sa isang indibidwal, na isinasagawa ng mga ahente ng gobyerno o mga grupong kumikilos na may basbas ng gobyerno. Layunin nitong patahimikin ang biktima, pigilan ang kanyang adbokasiya, at maghasik ng takot sa kanyang pamilya at mas malawak na mamamayan.

author: John David Parol
title: US bases noon, Pax Silica ngayon; kabataan, nagprotesta kontra panghihimasok ng US
content:
Nagsagawa ng kilos-protesta ang iba’t ibang grupo ng mga kabataang estudyante mula sa UP Manila patungong US Embassy upang gunitain ang makasaysayang desisyon ng Senado ng Pilipinas na tanggihan ang renewal ng US Military Bases Agreement (MBA) at ratipikasyon ng RP-U.S. Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation, and Security noong 1991.

Bitbit nila ang samu’t saring panawagan kabilang ang pagbasura sa Pax Silica, pagbuwag sa Luzon Economic Corridor, at pagpapalayas sa mga tropang Amerikano at kanilang mga base-militar sa bansa sa ilalim ng Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA).

Bagamat hindi nakalapit sa mismong tarangkahan ng embahada ang mga nagpoprotesta, ipinagpatuloy ng grupo ang kanilang maikling programa sa Kalaw Avenue sa Maynila.

Ayon sa mga nagprotesta, hindi hiwalay sa pang-araw-araw na kalagayan ng mamamayan at kabataan sa Metro Manila ang krisis dulot ng patuloy na pagyuko at pagsuko ng administrasyong Marcos Jr. ng soberanya sa malalaking dayuhan tulad ng US. Anila, sa halip na tunay na pambansang industriyalisasyon, nagpapatuloy ang banta sa likas-yaman at batayang serbisyo gaya ng kuryente at tubig na lalong magpapabigat sa gastusin ng ordinaryong pamilya.

“Ngayon pa lang, sobrang taas na ng singil sa kuryente. What more kung magkakaroon ng Pax Silica? Tayo ang magbabayad ng kuryente na ginagamit ng US,” diin ni Carla Espera mula sa Liga ng mga Kabataang Propagandista (LKP).

Kinakailangang mag-supply ng 3 Gigawatt (GW) na kuryente para gumana ang itatayong industrial at manufacturing hub sa ilalim ng Pax Silica Initiative. Katumbas ito ng 16% kabuuang current grid capacity ng Luzon. Ani Espera, hindi na nga natutugunan ng gobyerno ang pangangailangan at mas murang kuryente para sa mamamayan, may pangamba pang balikatin ng mamamayan ang posibleng kasalatan sa kuryente o mataas na singil sa kuryente kaugnay sa pagpapatayo at pagpapagana sa Pax Silica.

Bahagi rin sa isinusulong ng administrasyong Marcos Jr. ang nuclear energy at liquefied natural gas (LNG) upang tugunan ang lumalaking pangangailangan sa kuryente. Gayunman, ang pagpapalawak ng mga energy at industrial infrastructure ay may usapin din sa paggamit ng lupa. Sa ilalim ng Special Economic Zone Act o Republic Act No. 7916, maaaring ma-convert ang agricultural lands para sa ilang industrial at economic-zone developments, habang may mga probisyon para sa compensation sa mga residenteng maaaring ma-displace.

Pinalawig naman ni Zamann Milagrosa ng Kabataan Partylist (KPL) ang epekto ng Pax Silica sa New Clark City sa Tarlac, na siyang sentro ng proyektong digital sa ilalim ng Luzon Economic Corridor na nagdurugtong mula Subic, Clark, Maynila, hanggang Batangas.

“Hindi dahil malayo ang (Metro Manila) sa Tarlac, ay hindi na tayo maaapektuhan, kasi connected siya sa Luzon Economic Corridor. Papunta siya sa Pax Silica, marami tayong proyekto na patungo sa Pax Silica, may ginagawang highway na maapektuhan yung pagputol ng puno at malakihang pagputol ng puno, at yung mga tubigan natin na mawawalan tayo ng malinis na tubigan,” ani Milagrosa.

Noong 2024, naglatag ang National Economic and Development Authority ng 21 proyektong isinasaalang-alang sa pagtataguyod ng LEC. Aabot sa trilyong piso ang halaga ng mga proyektong ito. Lima sa mga ito ang may direktang koneksyon sa Metro Manila. Kabilang dito ang North-South Commuter Railway, Laguna Lakeshore Road Network, North Luzon East Expressway, Manila Bay–Pasig River–Laguna Lake Ferry System, at ang Subic-Clark-Manila-Batangas Railway.

“’Yong mga magsasaka natin mawawalan ng tirahan at papalayasin sila sa lupang ninuno nila. Imbes na ‘yung tubig na napupunta sa irigasyon—dahil magkakaroon pa tayo ng super El Niño, mawawalan sila ng malinis na tubig. ‘Yong kuryente na dapat napupunta sa mga taong bayan sa Gitnang Luzon, sobrang laki ang mapupunta sa Pax Silica. Tatlong gigawatts ang kukunin nila,” dagdag pa ni Milagrosa.

Bukod sa banta sa kabuhayan ng mga katutubo at magsasaka, iginiit ng mga nagpoprotesta na ang panghihimasok ng US sa bansa sa pamamagitan LEC, Pax Silica at iba pang mga hindi pantay na kasunduan ay tahasang naglalagay sa Pilipinas sa umiigting na girian ng mga makapangyarihang bansa, partikular ang US at Tsina sa rehiyon.

“Gagamitin ang Pax Silica bilang pagawaan ng materyales pandigmaan. Ibig sabihin, gagamitin tayo bilang base ng US para madali na silang makapag-atake ng karatig-bansa na umaatake sa kanila. Kumbaga, gagawin tayong base for war dahil nandito sa atin ang siyam na …

author: Rojava IC
title: Sleeper-Cell Report July 2026 – Global Coalition reports 0 confirmed ISIS attacks
content:
An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside


 


Key Points


– Six sleeper-cell attacks recorded by RIC, but the Global Coalition claims 0 attacks were officially claimed by ISIS


– One military personnel was killed, and a further five injured


– A minimum of seven alleged ISIS members were arrested


– A total of 36 civilians were injured, two killed


– An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in Deir ez-Zor


–

Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS mercenaries repatriated from Roj camp


 


In-Depth


In July of 2026, RIC

recorded six sleeper-cell attacks which some publications have attributed to ISIS, according to


North Press Agency

 one of these attacks was claimed by ISIS whereas the


Global Coalition


reported that July was the first month since the territorial defeat of ISIS in 2019, where they claimed 0 attacks. Also this month at least 7 members of ISIS cells were arrested.


On July 7, Bombings struck central Damascus near the Ministry of Tourism and the Four Seasons Hotel, during the visit of Macron the president of France to Syria. Ministry of Interior has attributed the attack to ISIS, the bombing resulted in the killing of one civilian and injury of 36.


On July 8, three attacks happened during the same day and the are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.

Unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle used machine guns to target an oil truck in Abrahyah town in eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, killing the driver.


Similarly, unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle, attacked a checkpoint of the Internal Security Forces near al-Baserah city bridge.


According to North Press Agency, also on July 8 ISIS

claimed responsibility for the killing of Rashad Khalaf al-Ghurair in the northern countryside of Deir ez-Zor.


On July 15,

unknown gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire on a member of the 72nd Division on the road linking al-Arimah and Manbij in eastern Aleppo countryside, injuring the him.


On July 18,

two unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire directly on member of the Defence Ministry


near al-Awsajli junction in eastern Manbij city.


On July 9,

Syria’s Interior Ministry announced its security forces had dismantled several ISIS cells in southern Syria, arresting a senior leader and several members accused of involvement in assassinations and financing terror.


On July 28,

Syrian Internal Security Forces and the General Intelligence Service in Aleppo announced the arrest of individuals allegedly affiliated with the ISIS, during a security operation in Aleppo and its surrounding countryside.


An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, in an incident that sparked widespread concern among residents.


During July, Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS were repatriated from


Roj Camp, which houses families of ISIS members, and returned to Tunisia. Additionally, Tunisian citizen Bilal Chawachi was sentenced to 55 years in prison after being convicted on terrorism-related charges, specifically traveling to Syria and fighting alongside the extremist organization.


Germany sentenced an Iraqi man to life imprisonment and his former wife to nine years and six months in prison after convicting them of enslaving and torturing two Yazidi girls while they were members of ISIS in Syria and Iraq between 2015 and 2017.


Three U.S. citizens pleaded guilty to terror charges, prosecutors said the defendants communicated through encrypted messaging applications between July and November 2025 and planned to travel to Turkey before crossing into Syria to join ISIS. 


* Due to the low rate of confirmed ISIS attacks RIC has decided to stop publishing monthly sleeper-cell reports and instead share a bi-annual summary of ISIS activity throughout Syria.

author: Unknown
title: PJAK member remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after arrest by Iranian intelligence
content:
Sirwan Habibi, a member of the Kurdistan Free Life Party (PJAK), remains forcibly disappeared 13 days after Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested him in Kamyaran, Kurdistan Province.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has learned that Habibi’s family has repeatedly visited Ministry of Intelligence offices and courts in Kamyaran and Sanandaj in recent days, seeking information about his situation. However, the authorities have continued to deny any knowledge of his arrest.


Habibi, from Sanandaj, is known within PJAK by the organisational name Aram Sine. The continued lack of information about his fate, together with the absence of any judicial case registered in his name at the courts in either city, has heightened concerns about his condition and whereabouts.


KHRN has spoken to several residents of Kamyaran’s Besat neighbourhood who witnessed his arrest, obtaining further details about the circumstances.


According to witnesses, dozens of civilian vehicles with tinted windows used by the Ministry of Intelligence agents surrounded several streets in the neighbourhood on the evening of 8 September. At about 01:00 local time on 9 September, agents began pursuing Habibi as he rode a motorcycle.


Witnesses said one of the vehicles struck his motorcycle at high speed, causing it to overturn, before agents used violence to arrest him.


Bystanders called the police emergency number, 110, and approached to help him after the motorcycle overturned. Plainclothes forces fired into the air to disperse them.


One witness said: “A few minutes later, a police patrol responding to the 110 call arrived, unaware of what was happening. But security forces blocked its path, said it was a security matter and forced the officers to leave.”


The witnesses said Habibi resisted arrest, but agents beat him, covered his face with a cloth and put him in a Samand car before taking him away.


In a statement issued on 14 September, PJAK said Habibi had been carrying out an organisational mission and was unarmed when Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested him. The party said his fate remained unknown.


KHRN’s findings show that, before the US-Israeli war with Iran, most people arrested by the Ministry of Intelligence and the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in Kurdistan Province were taken to the two agencies’ detention facilities in Sanandaj, where they were held and interrogated.


Following US and Israeli air strikes on those facilities, security agents have been holding detainees in secret detention facilities operated by the Ministry of Intelligence and in solitary confinement in prisons in the cities concerned.

author: groundxero
title: ‘ডিটেক্ট-ডিলিট-ডিপোর্ট’-অস্ত্রে কায়েম সন্ত্রাসের শাসন; মুর্শিদাবাদের সুতি অঞ্চলে করা তথ্যানুসন্ধানের প্রতিবেদন
content:
কঠিন পরিস্থিতির সঙ্গে প্রতিনিয়ত যুঝতে-যুঝতে বেঁচে থাকা এই মানুষগুলোর মধ্যে সংখ্যাগরিষ্ঠ মুসলমান গরিব মানুষরা হঠাৎই কেবলমাত্র বাংলাভাষী মুসলমান হওয়ার কারণেই এক ভয়ঙ্কর রাষ্ট্রীয় সন্ত্রাসের কবলে পড়েছেন এ রাজ্যে হিন্দুত্ববাদী সরকার কায়েম হওয়ার পর থেকে। সুতি ব্লকের কিছু গ্রাম ঘুরে এই ভয়ঙ্কর সন্ত্রাসের যে নিদর্শন আমরা চাক্ষুষ করেছি, তা নিয়ে এই প্রতিবেদন।


 


বিপ্লব নায়ক


 


[মুর্শিদাবাদের বিভিন্ন গ্রাম থেকে বাংলাদেশী সন্দেহে পুলিশ তুলে নিয়ে যাচ্ছে এমন বেশ কিছু বাঙালি মুসলমানদের যারা দীর্ঘদিন ধরে, এমনকি কয়েক পুরুষ ধরে ভারতের বাসিন্দা এবং ভারতের নাগরিক হওয়ার বৈধ নানা প্রমাণপত্রও যাঁদের আছে। বি.এস.এফ.-এর অধীন হোল্ডিং সেন্টার/ ডিটেইনশন সেন্টার-এ প্রাথমিকভাবে তাঁদের আটকে রাখা হচ্ছে, তারপর তাঁরা কর্পূরের মতো উবে যাচ্ছেন। বলা হচ্ছে যে তাদের বাংলাদেশে ডিপোর্ট করে দেওয়া হয়েছে, কিন্তু বাংলাদেশের কোথায় তাঁদের ঠেলে ঢুকিয়ে দেওয়া হলো তা নিয়ে কোনোকিছুই তাঁদের পরিবাররা জানতে পারছেন না। এইরকম কয়েকটি ঘটনার কথা আমরা ‘পুবের কলম’ নামক সংবাদপত্রে প্রকাশিত খবর এবং গণতান্ত্রিক অধিকার রক্ষা সমিতি-র জঙ্গীপুর শাখার একটি তথ্যানুসন্ধান রিপোর্ট পড়ে জানতে পারি। হঠাৎ করে উবে যাওয়া মানুষদের সহনাগরিক হিসেবে উদ্বিগ্ন হয়ে উঠে আমরা সেখানে নিজেরা গিয়ে সরেজমিনে পরিস্থিতি বোঝার চেষ্টা করার ও সম্ভাব্য প্রতিরোধের পথ খোঁজার প্রয়োজন অনুভব করি। সেই মোতাবেক আমরা চারজন — কিরীটী রায় (মানবাধিকার সুরক্ষা মঞ্চের আহ্বায়ক), বিপ্লব নায়ক (‘মাতৃভাষা’ পত্রিকার অন্যতম সম্পাদক), সঞ্জয় ভট্টাচার্য (কেন্ট বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের সহযোগী অধ্যাপক) এবং অন্তরা স্বর্ণকার (স্বাধীন সাংবাদিক) — মুর্শিদাবাদের সুতি অঞ্চলে গিয়ে ১৪-ই সেপ্টেম্বর বেশ কয়েকটি গ্রাম ঘুরে সাধারণ মানুষ, সরকারি আধিকারিক ও জনপ্রতিনিধিদের সঙ্গে কথা বলি। সেখানে আমরা যা দেখেছি, শুনেছি ও অনুভব করেছি, তা নিয়ে এই প্রতিবেদন।]


 


মুর্শিদাবাদ জেলার রাঢ় অঞ্চলে গঙ্গা ও পদ্মা নদীর মাঝের এলাকার নাম সুতি, প্রায় ২৫৫ বর্গ কিলোমিটার জুড়ে তা বিস্তৃত। পদ্মা নদী অনেকাংশেই এখানে আন্তর্জাতিক সীমানা হিসেবে কাজ করছে: এপারে ভারত, ওপারে বাংলাদেশ। প্রশাসনিকভাবে এই অঞ্চল দুটি সমষ্টি উন্নয়ন ব্লকে বিভক্ত: সুতি-১ ও সুতি-২। সুতি-১ ব্লকের জনসংখ্যা ১ লাখ ৮০ হাজারের কাছাকাছি, যার মধ্যে ধর্মীয় বিশ্বাসের ভিত্তিতে ৫৮.১ শতাংশ মুসলমান ও ৪১.৬ শতাংশ হিন্দু; আর সুতি-২ ব্লকের জনসংখ্যা ২ লাখ ৭৯ হাজারের কাছাকাছি, যার মধ্যে ধর্মীয় বিশ্বাসের ভিত্তিতে ৭২.৫ শতাংশ মুসলমান ও ২৭.২ শতাংশ হিন্দু (২০১১ জনগণনার প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী)। প্রায় আশিটি গ্রামে এই মানুষরা বাস করেন। গ্রামগুলি অধিকাংশই ঘনবসতিপূর্ণ। এখানকার মাটি ল্যাটেরাইটযুক্ত এঁটেল মাটি, কৃষিকর্মের সহায়ক। ধান ও পাট দুটি প্রধান ফসল, এছাড়াও ডাল, সবজির ফলন হয়। গ্রামগুলোর প্রধান কাজ এই কৃষিকাজই। কিন্তু তা  মানুষের জীবনকে সচ্ছলতা দিতে পারে না। কারণ, এখানকার সিংহভাগ মানুষই ভূমিহীন কৃষক বা প্রান্তিক চাষী। কৃষির সঙ্গে যুক্ত মানুষদের মধ্যে সুতি-১ ব্লকে ৪৮ শতাংশ ও সুতি-২ ব্লকে ৫৩ শতাংশ মানুষদের কোনো জমি নেই, তাই চাষের মরশুমে অন্যের জমিতে কৃষিমজুর হিসেবে খাটার মধ্য দিয়েই তাঁদের যা রোজগার। সেই মজুরির প্রকৃত মূল্যও দিন-কে-দিন কমছে। বাকিদের সিংহভাগও ১ বা ২ হেক্টরের কম কৃষিজমির মালিক। কৃষিকাজের খরচ বাড়তে থাকার সঙ্গে সঙ্গে এঁদের অনেকেই নিজেরা চাষ করার ক্ষমতাটুকু হারাচ্ছেন, ঋণ-বন্ধকী-কর্জ-এর পাকে পড়ে ধনীদের কাছে জমি লিজ দিয়ে কোনোমতে টিকে থাকার চেষ্টা করছেন। তাই গঙ্গা-পদ্মার আশীর্বাদে মাটি উর্বর হলেও চাষের কাজ দিয়ে বেশিরভাগ মানুষের পেট চালানো দুষ্কর হয়ে উঠেছে অনেকদিন। এই সুযোগে বিড়ি-বাঁধার শ্রম সেঁধিয়েছে ঘরে-ঘরে। বিড়ি কোম্পানিগুলোর মালিকরা বিশাল ধনী ও প্রভাবশালী। বিস্তৃত কন্ট্রাক্টর-জালিকার মধ্য দিয়ে বিড়ির পাতা ও মশলা পৌঁছে যাচ্ছে ঘরে-ঘরে, কন্ট্রাক্টররা দিন-প্রতি কতগুলো বিড়ি বেঁধে দিতে হবে তার লক্ষ্যমাত্রা ঠিক করে দিচ্ছেন, অতি কম পিস-রেট মজুরী, লক্ষ্যমাত্রা পূরণ না করতে পারলে সে মজুরীতেও কোপ পড়বে, তাই প্রায় প্রতিটি বাড়ির দরজার সামনে, উঠোনে বা রাস্তার ধারে, একা বা কয়েকজন একসাথে, মহিলারা মশলা ও বিড়িপাতার কুলো কোলে নিয়ে বিড়ি বেঁধে চলেছেন একটানা। সুতি-১ ব্লকে মোট শ্রমিকদের মধ্যে প্রায় ৩৬ শতাংশ এবং সুতি-২ ব্লকে মোট শ্রমিকদের মধ্যে প্রায় ৬৩ শতাংশ এমন বিড়ি-বাঁধা শ্রমিক (২০১১ জনগণনা প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী)। হ্যাঁ, এই বিড়ি-বাঁধা শ্রমিকদের প্রায় আশি শতাংশই গেরস্থ মহিলা। তবু তো দিন চলে না। তাই দূরের শহরে বা অন্য রাজ্যের শহরে পাহারাদার-মিস্ত্রি-মজুর-ফেরিওয়ালা-র কাজের সন্ধান যখন আসে আড়কাঠিদের মারফত, তখন ঘর ছেড়ে শক্ত-সমর্থরা পাড়ি দেয় খাটনি-করার শক্তির শেষ বিন্দুটিকেও নিঙড়ে করকরে কিছু টাকা রোজগারের জন্য, সে টাকা তারা ঘরে পাঠায়, বাড়িটা হয়তো পাকা হয়, দেওয়ালে নতুন রঙের পোঁচ পড়ে, আর সেই পরিযায়ী শ্রমিকটির দূর প্রবাসে গতর-নিঙড়ানো খাটনি আর ক্লান্তি-অবসাদে মোবাইলের নীল আলোর মধ্যে ডুব-সাঁতার, এভাবেই দিন কাটে। এঁদের সংখ্যা বেশ কয়েক লাখ হবে।


 


কঠিন পরিস্থিতির সঙ্গে প্রতিনিয়ত যুঝতে-যুঝতে বেঁচে থাকা এই মানুষগুলোর মধ্যে সংখ্যাগরিষ্ঠ মুসলমান গরিব মানুষরা হঠাৎই কেবলমাত্র বাংলাভাষী মুসলমান হওয়ার কারণেই এক ভয়ঙ্কর রাষ্ট্রীয় সন্ত্রাসের কবলে পড়েছেন এ রাজ্যে হিন্দুত্ববাদী সরকার …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Will New Changes Improve Taiwan’s Image on Migrant Work?
content:
A NUMBER OF changes are set to occur in the migrant work landscape in Taiwan going forward.

For one, the first batch of migrant workers in the hospitality field has arrived, consisting of 35 Indonesians. These 35 workers arrived in Taiwan as part of the new Multinational Skilled Worker Enhancement Program and are classified as skilled labor, rather than blue-collar migrant workers. The 35 workers previously conducted internships in Taiwan of at least one year in length and are required to reach A-2 level listening and speaking within three years, per the requirements of the program.

Their employer, Regent Taipei, previously hired them as interns, and it approached them individually under the new program. The 35 workers are mostly in their twenties and will return to the departments they worked in. The terms of the new program specify that hospitality industry businesses can hire a new migrant worker if they increase the salary of their lowest-paid Taiwanese worker by 2,000 NT, though hiring of migrant workers is still capped at 10% of the workforce.

The hospitality industry, which has a shortfall of 6,000 workers annually, has long clamored for hiring migrant workers to take up positions that Taiwanese are no longer interested in working. At the same time, it had already gradually been the case that what were technically internships had become a means of hiring migrant workers in the hospitality industry. The government seems to now be making moves at regulation, which hopefully can provide workers with stronger protections.

One notes that the new batch of workers will not pay recruitment fees, as instituting zero-fee recruitment practices as Taiwan has long been called on to do. Likewise, Taiwan is set to open a direct hiring desk in the Philippines in the near future, as another means of instituting recruitment that routes around the brokers that traditionally have imposed heavy fees on migrant workers to arrange for their transportation to and from Taiwan and their employment after arriving. The direct hiring desk mandates that employers cover travel to and from Taiwan.

Clearly, Taiwan is aiming to clean up its international image, given increased scrutiny on migrant worker abuses. The pressure to institute zero-fee recruitment is largely external and is a direct result of Taiwan agreeing to such terms in trade negotiations with the US.

Indeed, similarly, Taiwan has built new facilities for migrant workers in the Cianjhen Fishing Port to the tune of 8.2 billion NT. Such facilities are intended to provide showers, laundry, WiFi, and hotel services for migrant workers, especially as labor abuses against migrant fishermen and the poor working conditions they face have increasingly seen scrutiny in past years. But despite the expenditure, the facility has been criticized, as migrant workers in many cases cannot afford the hotel facilities, which require 1,000 NT per day. Likewise, the facility has insufficient showers and laundry machines, often leading migrant workers to go elsewhere. It is to be seen whether the government’s recent actions on the migrant work front prove to be simply an attempt to whitewash their poor treatment, then, with token gestures done for the sake of appearance that mean little in terms of concrete change.

author: Eleanor Morley
title: The problems of AI are the problems of capitalism
content:
Recent revelations about artificial intelligence models “going rogue” have raised serious concerns that the technology could soon cause great damage to human society. Already, the production and application of AI is wreaking havoc on the environment, amplifying existing social problems and expanding the powers of the surveillance state. While further regulation of the industry is necessary, the fundamental problem with AI is that capitalists control it and it is subject to the system’s prevailing conditions of profit maximisation, competition, imperial rivalry and more.

“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade”, Jacob Coxon, a former researcher at Anthropic and OpenAI, the world’s leading frontier AI model developers, wrote on X in early September. Anthropic’s chief safety researcher Evan Hubinger later responded similarly. “We do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans”, he wrote. “I personally think it is >10 percent within the next decade.”

Amid the myriad other doomsday scenarios the world faces—catastrophic weather and mass extinction events from climate change, the threat of inter-imperialist nuclear war, economic collapse and mass starvation and so on—this latest warning of impending catastrophe could get lost. But it’s worth pausing to think about what exactly has just been said by people working at the frontier of this new technology: it might pose an existential risk to humanity. It’s like an automotive engineer warning that the latest car model has a >10 percent chance of killing everyone on the roads, yet constructing and releasing it anyway.

Some people are understandably sceptical. Outrageous claims have been a key part of the hype machine that has attracted trillions of dollars in investment into leading AI firms and the associated ecosystem of tech companies that provide the chips and memory needed to run the models. “My AI is the biggest and scariest” is another way of saying “my AI is the best to invest in”. There are also debates about the technical capabilities/limitations of various forms of AI, debates about what counts as “intelligence” and whether it is possible to replicate it through binary code, and more. 

But if there is even a tiny possibility that AI could hijack autonomous weapons and rain them down on humanity (something Coxon, in an interview with the

New York Times

, claimed is a potential future scenario), then we should immediately halt the development and deployment of AI models until proper safeguards are in place. Under capitalism, profits always trump human life. We have enough evidence for this in the form of tobacco companies fighting against lung cancer science, DuPont’s knowing deployment of cancerous forever chemicals, the fossil fuel industry’s war on climate science and the very existence of the military-industrial complex. So we certainly should not trust AI titans to regulate themselves, as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has implored us to do.

The problems with AI

AI doomsday predictions are not new—they have been discussed in tech circles for decades and entered the public domain with the launch of ChatGPT nearly four years ago. But the recent warning cut through in a way others haven’t, partly because it coincides with growing hostility to AI and the companies producing it, and partly because anxieties are rising about the pace of AI’s development. 

The hostility is multifaceted. AI data centres are popping up seemingly everywhere, chewing through energy, guzzling water and emitting a constant, loud hum that is reportedly unbearable for nearby residents. AI slop has degraded online spaces, and deepfakes have created a new dystopian category of sexual harassment. And there are fears about what AI will do to the labour market and the education system—no one is buying Silicon Valley’s techno-optimist line that our labour time will be replaced by leisure time funded by a universal basic income. 

Early AI models now seem almost quaint as we move from general chatbots that could churn out a basic essay or a maid of honour speech to AI agents designed to undertake tasks on our behalf and make their own decisions about how to complete them. Take a recent incident in Australia. An AI assistant, asked by its instructor to bump him to the top of the waitlist for a gym class, hacked the gym’s website and booted someone else off the waitlist entirely.

This was a relatively benign example of AI’s capabilities, though …

author: AWSM
title: Why I Won’t Vote ~ A SYMPOSIUM #1
content:
Anarchy 37, March 1964, Why I Won’t Vote

Voting : “The instrument and symbol of a freeman’s power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country”

The saying that ” only a fool would put a loaded gun into the hands of an idiot ” is an especially apt analogy of government. An idiot (usually well-meaning) considers himself clever enough to run the affairs of a large number of people by taking a seat in parliament. A large number of people, acting like fools, vote for his party’s policy then spend the next few years grumbling about the results. The error in approach is that the voter thinks that he will get what he voted for. If he could vote for those who in fact control the country, say the Governors of the Bank of England, the directors of the industrial corporations and those behind the ministries, the illusion of democracy would be more understandable.

The real centres of power lie far beyond the people’s influence at elections. These remain constant whatever Party is ” in power “. In the terms of centralised ” democracy ” the only possible argument to justify voting is that marginal benefits may be gained. The state only incidentally attends to the well-being of its subjects. Its main concern is its power relation to other states, of which the most perfect expression is in war.

I am on the side of people anywhere who are prepared neither to live nor die for something that in the long run can only militate against survival and the conditions that make life worth living. Our immediate action must, by its nature, be to oppose that pathetic gesture, voting. It must be direct and direction. We can learn to live as free men and women only by organising against the condition we are in.

The Tenants Association, Consumers Association, and Direct Action in industry all provide opportunities for people to experience directing their own lives in positive ways towards positive ends.

Only by direct involvement in society can the individual hope to transform himself and his world. Freedom cannot be given, it must be taken; and the free society can only grow from experiments in the problems (ethical and organisational) of community.

Voting does not, and cannot, mean government by consent. By voting, one acts on the assumptions that certain men are fit to govern, and that a majority is necessarily right. Also should the state, acting in the name of a (frequently fictitious) majority, declare war, the individual loses the right to live, if he ever had it.

To me, voting is complicity with the State and a negative action, therefore I do not vote.

author: Ruby Healer
title: Labor doubles down on US military alliance
content:
“American force posture in Australia is growing”, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles declared on his visit to Washington, DC, this month. “Since we’ve come to government”, Marles said, standing alongside US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, “you can see a through line there of growing American force posture in Australia”.

It was a fairly straightforward summary of the Albanese Labor government’s attitude, followed up with promises of further integration between the Australian and US militaries. A shifting “force posture” will mean more American troop rotations, more US air and naval operations and more pre-positioning of military equipment like warplanes, fuel and munitions in Australia.

Agreements made by the Albanese government will ramp up co-operation on all fronts, with a newly

revitalised

 HMAS Stirling base near Perth set to host American nuclear-powered submarines and an estimated 2,300 US troops within five years. As America’s military machine looks ahead to an era of aggressive contest with China in the Asia-Pacific, Australia’s ruling class is desperate to make itself an indispensable part of US war planning.

Weapons trade regulations have also been

loosened

 under a bilateral agreement to help both countries access shared research to develop arms and surveillance systems. And, Marles promised ominously, “you will hear more from us ... in the coming months” about further arrangements to increase co-operation.

Of course, there’s nothing new about the Australian ruling class throwing itself into a military alliance with the United States. This is a long-standing arrangement pursued by every Australian government since the Second World War. Permanent joint intelligence and communications programs have run out of Pine Gap in the Northern Territory and the Harold Holt naval station in Western Australia since the 1960s.

Data

published

 by the

Guardian

 in early September revealed that American forces and weapons corporations control or make use of over 100 military facilities across the country. And Australia is one of the biggest recipients of US arms in the world, with around 85 percent of weapons purchased in 2021-25 coming from the US,

according

 to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute’s arms transfers database.

Hegseth himself

recalled

 during a separate love-in event with Marles last year: “We [the Australian and US militaries] fought shoulder to shoulder in every major conflict since World War One—from the Western Front, to Guadalcanal, to Vietnam, to Afghanistan”.

“During my time in Afghanistan”, he reminisced, “I served with members of the Australian military who were some of the finest”. We can only imagine the sorts of unconvicted war criminals who consorted with Pete Hegseth during the joint twenty-year occupation of Afghanistan.

The US alliance has long been a pillar of Australia’s foreign policy, but the current Labor government seems particularly eager to grovel to America. Just one month after Donald Trump’s inauguration, and before the current Australian and US defence ministers had even met for the first time, the Australian government arranged a

payment

 of US$500 million towards the Trump administration’s military budget.

“We’re really pleased that the first payment ... we’ve been able to make in the first couple of weeks of the Trump administration”, Marles told Hegseth ahead of their first formal meeting in February 2025. “We’re really pleased to make it in the first week of your tenure as the secretary of defence.”

In the meeting that followed, Marles

explained

 that Hegseth’s enthusiasm for military ties with Australia made sense, since “the whole idea of a free and open Indo-Pacific really has its origins during the first Trump Administration”.

You wouldn’t be wrong to interpret this behaviour as pathetic bootlicking. The Australian government is a simpering bunch of pro-American lowlifes. But the problem isn’t that our leaders are “weak” or being strong-armed into subservience. They run the twelfth largest economy in the world. Their armed forces outstrip those of any oceanic neighbours by a wide margin. The reality is that Australian capitalism is a willing and culpable participant in the world’s most powerful military coalition alongside America.

As former Labor Prime Minister Kevin Rudd recently

stated

, the “alliance with the United States remains a force multiplier for Australia’s defence needs”. With the help of its powerful …

author: AWSM
title: Errico Malatesta – Vote? What For?
content:
George: This beer’s not too bad, is it?

Jack: Yes, it’s alright, but what a price!

George: Shocking – especially when you remember what things used to cost. Still, you can’t wonder with all these taxes. It costs you twice as much to live as it used to. They put up the price of some things, and say you can do without them. But you can’t do without bread, and food, and clothes – you have to pay the rent all the same, and then there are the taxes on this and the rates – on our wages too! What a life! And it’s our own fault! If we wanted to we could alter things. The working class has the remedy in its own hands.

George: Easy enough! You’ve got a vote?

Jack: What’s that got to do with it?

George: Have you, or haven’t you?

Jack: Well, I’m entitled to a vote – but I never make use of it.

George: There you are! You’ve got a vote, but you just won’t take the trouble to use it, and then you wonder why things are so bad. You deserve all you get, honestly! People like you are responsible for all the trouble in the world!

Jack: Alright, alright, keep your hair on! Just tell me what’s the good of voting?

George: It’s obvious. Who makes the laws? The M.P.’s. Elect good M.P.’s and you get good laws.

Jack: Good councillors and good M.P.’s? We’ve heard that for a long time. But you’d have to be deaf, dumb, and blind not to notice it’s the same stooges that always get in. Oh, it’s wonderful to hear them when they’re after votes at election time. They pat you on the back, ask after the wife and kids, kiss the baby, promise you railways, bridges, work, cheap bread, less taxes, higher wages, protection – absolutely everything! And once they get in, they’re no better than anyone else. Goodbye promises! The wife and kids may starve, there’s no more or less work than before, the whole town can be falling to pieces for all they care. They’ve other things to think about than your troubles! Then a few years later they start the ballyhoo again. It doesn’t matter what colour the party is: they’re all the same. As soon as they’re elected, they forget all about you. They’re in their clubs and at their select dinners, and they don’t even trouble to come and have a look at you until the next election.

George: That’s correct! But why elect the rich? Don’t you know that the rich only live on the work of the masses? So how do you expect them to worry about the masses? All they think of is getting as much out of the ordinary man as they can.

Jack: Now you’re talking! But it’s not only the rich. There’s the other type, who want to get elected so they can become rich.

George: That’s true. So don’t let’s vote for them. Let’s elect workers, experienced friends of ours, as you might say, and then we won’t be fooled.

Jack: Oh, we’ve got some of your “experienced friends” in now, and they’re no different from our acknowledged enemies! Anyhow, what do you mean, “let’s elect – let’s elect.” As if we – you and me – could do as we like!

George: But it’s not only us two. If each one of us tried to convert other people and they would do the same, labour would have a majority, and we could elect whoever we liked. And that’s when we could form a government of the workers, and then . . .

Jack: And then it would be a paradise – I mean for those who were in Parliament! You’re arranging things a bit too quickly! Those in command always have the majority. The rich are always in power. Just imagine a poor worker, perhaps with an ill wife and four hungry kids, and you tell him to risk his job and get thrown out of his house to starve; just to give his vote to a candidate his master doesn’t like. Just try and convince those poor devils who can be thrown out of work by their boss whenever he likes. They’re never free; if they want to be free, they don’t want to waste their time voting – just take what they need.

George: But if we didn’t do that, no-one would vote. We couldn’t go to the workers and ask them to vote for our party, and say at the same time that votes were useless.

Jack: That’s just it! And on top of that you have to make election promises you know you can’t keep. And then you have to stand in with the Government, and mix with the well-to-do, and all the rest of it. As soon as any of your men are elected they have to kow-tow to the people you admit are the opponents of the workers. So why the hell talk about propaganda when the first thing you do is to counteract propaganda?

George: But you must admit, it’s an advantage to have our own men with …

author: Susan Price
title: ‘Ecological crisis creates a challenge and an opportunity for the left’
content:
Ayesha Ahmad, a Pakistani socialist-feminist activist, researcher, educator, and labour rights practitioner with the Haqooq-e-Khalq Party, was one of the guest speakers at the Ecosocialism 2026 conference in Magan-djin/Brisbane, September 11–13. She spoke to Green Left’s Peter Boyle about the impact of the mounting global ecological crisis on politics in Pakistan.

The catastrophic flash floods in Nepal as a result of global warming and the melting of the Himalayan glaciers were a warning to the world, but does it have a special significance for Pakistan, which also borders the Himalayas?

The catastrophic flash floods in Nepal are a profound warning for Pakistan. For years, Pakistan has been among the countries most exposed to the climate crisis in South Asia, and we have already witnessed what a warming Himalaya can do — from the catastrophic 2022 floods, to increasingly frequent glacial lake outburst floods in Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Nepal disaster tells us that we may be entering an even more dangerous phase of the Himalayan climate crisis.

But for me, there is a much deeper question here. South Asia shares a history. We share the history of colonial extraction, of loot and plunder, of resources being taken from our lands to build wealth elsewhere. Political decolonisation did not necessarily mean economic decolonisation. The geography of extraction has changed, the language has changed, but the underlying relationship can remain remarkably familiar.

Today, we are being told that the answer is development, investment, critical minerals, energy security and even the green transition. But we have to ask: whose development, whose energy security and whose transition?

Climate change cannot be reduced to mining alone. But it would be deeply irresponsible to pursue accelerated extraction in an already climate-vulnerable Himalayan region without asking what extraction does to fragile ecosystems, watersheds, communities and the cumulative resilience of the region.

And this is where the history of colonialism matters. We cannot keep repeating the old colonial bargain under a new vocabulary: our mountains provide the minerals, our communities bear the ecological and social costs and the value is extracted into global markets elsewhere.

If the Global North needs minerals for its energy transition, then the question must be: Who owns them? Who decides? Who benefits? Who bears the environmental costs? And what happens to the people and ecosystems from which these resources are extracted?

We cannot continue with an economic model that treats our mountains, minerals, rivers and land as commodities.

We cannot call it a green transition if the transition is built on another round of extraction from the Global South. We cannot decolonise our politics while continuing to colonise our resources. And we cannot keep asking the people of Pakistan to pay the climate price for a development model from which they receive so little of the wealth.

For Pakistan, the lesson from Nepal is therefore not simply to prepare better for floods.

If extraction continues without ecological limits, democratic control and justice — and if the old unequal relationship between the Global North and resource-rich countries of the Global South continues under the language of “green development” — then the next disaster will not be a surprise. It will be a consequence of choices we already made.

Many years ago, we took part in an international campaign for the release of Baba Jan from Gilgit-Baltistan, who was dubbed the “first climate justice political prisoner”. How does the mounting ecological crisis impact repression and human rights?

The struggle is not only about environmental protection, but about who has the right to speak, whose land is protected, whose losses are recognised, and whether climate-affected communities are allowed to demand justice.

For me, the story of Baba Jan is one of the clearest examples of what climate politics looks like in Pakistan when it becomes a question of justice, rather than simply a question of climate change. And this tells us something very important about the space available to the left in Pakistan.

We are allowed to talk about climate change. We are allowed to talk about floods, melting glaciers, carbon emissions and resilience. But when we start talking about climate justice — about land, ownership, displacement, workers’ rights, resource extraction, reparations and who is …

author: James McVicar
title: Why do the Greens always chicken out?
content:
When Larissa Waters was elected leader of the Australian Greens, she said she was there to “

get shit done

”.

True to her word, Waters did something last week—and it was, indeed, shit. Greens MPs gave

crucial support

 in the Senate to the roll-out of a carbon emissions offset scheme so bad that the term “greenwashing” seems generous.

Under the scheme, state governments will now be able to take publicly owned forest, promise not to deforest it, and then convert that promise into “carbon credits”. These credits can then be sold to greenhouse gas emitters to subtract from their overall carbon emissions count.

In NSW, the scheme is being tied to the establishment of a 476,000-hectare koala reserve the state government had already promised back in 2015. This move, according to Larissa Waters, put the Greens in an “

impossible position

” and forced them to support Labor’s carbon credit scam.

So now, in exchange for doing something it had already said it would do, the NSW Labor government can continue to do

nothing

 to trees that were

already there

 and, in turn, magically generate permits for carbon emitters to carry on emitting carbon.

The Greens are now trying to sell this as a step forward for the planet, Waters describing it as the “first chink in the armour of coal and gas”.

Cartoonist First Dog on the Moon found a

visual metaphor

 much nearer the mark, depicting a Labor MP holding a cuddly koala at gunpoint and threatening the Greens leader: “vote for climate change or the koala gets it”.

Richard Denniss of the Australia Institute—hardly a radical left outfit—likened the Greens decision to “

fiddling while the forest burns

”. He went on: “In voting with Labor, the Greens ... have tied the protection of trees and koalas to the expansion of gas and coal”.

Labor’s actions come as no surprise, given the party’s longstanding support for Australia’s fossil fuel industry. But why the hell have the Greens gone along with it?

Prominent left-wing Greens figure Jonathan Sriranganathan criticised his party but suggested it was simply a problem of accountability. In a recent

Facebook post

 about the carbon credit vote, he wrote:

“Despite having plenty of time and capacity to do so, the three federal Greens politicians in Queensland didn’t bother seeking out the views of all the people who helped get them elected.”

To be sure, in a party whose sole purpose is to accrue seats in parliament, MPs usually dominate decision-making with little rank-and-file oversight. But internal democracy within the Australian Greens, however scant it may be, is not the real problem.

For one thing, there’s no evidence that Greens members overwhelmingly oppose the way their MPs voted in the Senate, though undoubtedly many do. Even Sriranganathan didn’t venture to say in his post that the Greens MPs who did so were wrong to support the bill.

What it comes down to is politics.

The Greens are a pro-capitalist party. They may not like some of its worst aspects, but the party has never been for overturning the system. They are committed to working within it.

The contradictions of such a project are perhaps most obvious on the question that is so core to the party’s political identity: climate change.

The Greens insist the climate crisis can be tackled without any radical change to the way our society operates. Rejecting any fundamental alternative to the profit-driven logic of capitalism, they instead throw their support behind farcical “market solutions” that shield the fossil fuel industry from real action.

And even when the Greens are critical of greenwashing scams, they aren’t willing to put up a fight lest they be accused of obstructing or “letting the perfect be the enemy of the good”. This isn’t just poor strategy; it stems from wanting to be seen as responsible partners in government.

These endless acrobatics of compromise also send the wrong message to Greens supporters and left-wing people more broadly. Party leaders have to run PR for every shoddy deal they stitch up with Labor, no matter how bad, and sell it as progress. Anyone who disagrees is a helpless idealist, a useful idiot for the side of “perfect” against the side of “good”.

Socialist politics offers an alternative. Socialists never limit our demands to what is palatable to the rich parasites who run this country and their defenders in parliament.

We know that radical social change is possible and that it doesn’t come from parliamentary manoeuvring …

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Students walk out of class again to protest Hanson’s racism and bigotry
content:
Thousands of high school and university students again walked out of class a second time to protest Pauline Hanson’s racism and bigotry on September 17. Rallies were held in 18 cities and towns across the country.

Students highlighted Hanson’s racist comments towards First Nations people and immigrants, her anti-LGBTIQ stance, her claim that domestic violence is a “two-way street” and her denial of the climate crisis.

Many pointed out that Hanson’s claim to be representing “ordinary Australians” is shown to be a lie because she is backed by Gina Rinehart, Australia’s richest person, and has consistently voted against pay rises and improved workers’ rights.

Students at the rally in Gadigal Country/Sydney told Green Left they did not support the vision for the country that Hanson is putting forward. “We’re the next generation of voters and we don’t want to see people like Pauline Hanson and One Nation who spread bigotry and hate in power,” one student said.

A year-12 student told Green Left he attended the protest to oppose Hanson’s racist rhetoric, and its adoption by Labor and the Coalition. “I’m here to stand in solidarity with women, immigrants, Palestinians, Indigenous people and queer people.”

Another student said they want politicians who are “for the people and not for billionaires”. “My mum is a person of colour and we don’t want someone who’s going to be racist.”

Atlas, an 18-year-old, said he came to the rally “because I am queer and people who I care about are in danger”.

Another told GL: “It’s hard to think that we could grow up in a future where someone like that could be deciding what happens in Australia. I think Pauline Hanson stands for racism, and I hate racism!”

Layla, from Newtown High, said she joined the rally to “stand against a monocultural Australia”.

“Australia is so much more interesting and multicultural, and to strip us of that would be to strip away everything good about this country.”

Grace Street, president of the University of Sydney Student Representative Council, told GL “high school and university students reject Hanson’s far-right politics”. “This is also a student issue — she just announced her plan to reduce the number of international students who come to the country and how many would be able to stay after they finish their degree.”

Rachel Evans, Socialist Alliance candidate for Heffron in the NSW elections in March, said it was exciting to see so many students campaigning against Hanson’s politics. “She is anti-refugee, anti-migrant, anti-trans and anti-woman, and it’s excellent to see young people start to organise.”

Another group of students told GL that Hanson’s beliefs are “destructive”. “Australia thrives off its multiculturalism and we’ll become the next laughing stock, after the US, if this continues.”

About 100 students joined the rally in Muloobinba/Newcastle. One student told GL they “don’t support what Hanson says about LGBTIQ people and people from other countries … this is a country that should be for everyone.

“She has no idea what she is doing and no idea what is right for the country or what we wants — she is totally out of touch.”

Another said Hanson was following the script of US President Donald Trump and his “Make America Great Again” movement.

[Join the speak-out against racism and bigotry in Glebe on September 26.]

author: Lance Selfa
title: Away from the cameras, Trump’s mass deportation campaign grinds on
content:
In the opening days of 2026, the Trump administration’s mass deportation operation faced a crisis, thanks to the brave resistance of ordinary people in Minnesota’s Twin Cities area. After Trump’s armed thugs murdered Renée Goode and Alex Pretti in broad daylight, when hundreds of cell phone videos refuted the Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem’s bald-faced slanders of the dead, the administration reset.

Trump fired Noem and cashiered Greg Bovino, a white supremacist Customs and Border Protection commander. Both Noem and Bovino had revelled in displays of immigration cops’ brutality and degradation of immigrants caught in their dragnets. They brought camera crews with them to create “content” of the terror campaign against immigrants for MAGA-aligned media.

Trump put “border czar” Tom Homan in charge of operations in Minnesota and then appointed Senator Markwayne Mullin to take over for Noem. These two dullards are no less committed to Trump’s anti-immigration agenda than were Noem and Bovino. But they have the good sense to keep themselves out of the limelight.

Trump suffered a political defeat in Minnesota. But in the months since, the mass deportation campaign has ground on. In fact, it may be achieving its aims more successfully while minimising social media images of armed goons terrorising neighbourhoods.

Let’s take note of the sheer breadth of the deportation machine. According to the latest figures the 

Vera Institute of Justice

 compiled (current as of August 2026), Immigration and Customs Enforcement detains around 70,000 people per day in more than 1,400 facilities across the US and its territories. Detentions peaked in January (73,000 per day), fell sharply to about 55,000 in mid-May, and climbed again to 68,000 per day by early August.

These patterns suggest the Department of Homeland Security pulled back from the high-profile mass raids that hit a wall of opposition in Minnesota. But that step back looks like a temporary regrouping of forces before ramping up arrests again. DHS is on pace to “remove” (aka deport) about 460,000 people this year, according to 

Open Immigration

, a database of US immigration court records.

These numbers also reflect Congress opening the floodgates of money earmarked for immigration roundups and creating a gulag archipelago of “detention centres” (perhaps more accurately described as concentration camps). The enormous budget passed in 2025, authorising $170 billion for immigration enforcement over most of Trump’s term, represents a five-fold increase in ICE’s and CBP’s pre-Trump budgets.

In June, Republicans used “budget reconciliation”, a legislative tactic that lets Congress pass budget-related bills by simple majority (end-running the Senate filibuster), to add another $70 billion to ICE and CBP through the end of Trump’s term.

One of the most effective uses of these vast sums is to recruit local law enforcement agencies as deputies in the mass deportation machine. Homeland Security’s “287(g)” program, created by Democratic President Bill Clinton’s administration in 1996, helps law enforcement agencies that sign up to collaborate with Immigration and Customs Enforcement and CBP.

To DHS, agreements with locals are a “force multiplier” because immigrants who might have an encounter with a cop over a trivial traffic violation might quickly find themselves being turned over to ICE. The symbiotic relationship between the Feds and the locals is clear. Police agencies receive millions in federal assistance, and the Feds receive bodies to feed into the deportation maw—without facing the political blowback that armed goons snatching people off the streets generates.

In January 2025, at the beginning of the Trump administration, 139 local agencies, representing areas covering about 15 million people, had 287(g) agreements with the Feds. In September 2026, that number has ballooned to 2,054 agencies covering 56 million people (or one-sixth of the US population), according 

to 287(g) Watch.

DHS agreements with local law enforcement extend to contracts turning city and county jails into immigration jails.

“As of August 5, ICE has detained 104,800 people across 303 jails in 2026. Compared to the same period in 2024 under the Biden administration, this reflects an 84 percent increase in the number of local jails used for ICE detention and triple the number of people held by ICE in local jails”, the 

Vera Institute reported

.

author: Amir Khafagy
title: NYC Announces Largest Food Delivery Worker Settlement Ever Reached in US
content:
DoorDash reached a $131.5 million settlement agreement for underpaying nearly 260,000 delivery workers.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Immigrant delivery workers have long alleged that DoorDash has shortchanged them out of their hard-earned wages. Now, the city has announced a historic settlement that aims to make them square — and then some.

On Tuesday, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) Commissioner Samuel Levine announced a $131.5 million settlement agreement with DoorDash for underpaying nearly 260,000 delivery workers.

The settlement follows a years-long DCWP investigation that found DoorDash failed to pay thousands of workers for all the time they worked, and failed to pay thousands more workers on time. DCWP will contact the affected workers directly, and said they expect workers will receive compensation equivalent to approximately 200% of the amount they were initially underpaid.

Additionally, DCWP found that DoorDash violated the city’s delivery worker Minimum Pay Rate law, which is currently set at $22.13 per hour for time spent on active delivery, regardless of a worker’s immigration status. And although DoorDash increased hourly pay for its workers in December 2023, the company still found ways to exclude some delivery workers from receiving the minimum hourly wage.

As per the terms of the agreement, over $115 million will go directly into delivery workers’ pockets, and DoorDash will be forced to pay more than $16 million in additional civil penalties. The city estimates that since at least 2022, more than 260,000 workers were underpaid by DoorDash, including workers who were not paid at all or were paid late by days and, in some cases, weeks.

According to the city, this is the largest labor enforcement action in New York City history as well as the largest food delivery worker settlement ever reached in the entire country.

“When a worker earns a wage, they deserve to be paid that wage — not tomorrow, not after a lawsuit, but on time and in full,” said Mayor Mamdani in a statement shared with Documented. “No corporation is above the law, and this administration will keep fighting until every worker gets the pay and protections they deserve.”

DoorDash spokesperson Samantha Ramirez acknowledged that the company had failed to pay some workers, but stressed that it was not deliberate, but merely a mistake.

“Simply put, we screwed up,” she told Documented in a statement. “Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late. While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them okay. We pride ourselves on operational excellence at DoorDash, and this was not excellent, nor was it acceptable.”

Ramirez said less than 1% of all payments to delivery workers were affected, with around $6.6 million in wages withheld from workers. Another $5.7 million in wages arrived days or, in some cases, weeks late. Overall, Ramirez says, 65% of impacted workers were underpaid by $1 or less.

“We’re making things right by paying every impacted Dasher what they are owed and fixing what caused this so it doesn’t happen again,” said Ramirez.

The settlement goes beyond compensating for past violations. Going forward, as part of the settlement, DoorDash must submit detailed data reports to DCWP every month for three years, which the agency will use to monitor the company’s compliance with the law and the terms of the settlement.

The case was first brought to the city’s attention by The Workers’ Justice Project (WJP) in 2023 after they found that 200 DoorDash workers had had their wages stolen beginning in 2022. Since then, they have continued to put pressure on the city to act. Now the city has finally delivered.

“This historic settlement is a major victory for thousands of Deliveristas across New York City who have been organizing for basic rights and building their own union, Los Deliveristas Unidos,” said Ligia Guallpa, executive director of WJP, in a statement shared with Documented. “For too long, DoorDash treated workers as disposable, stealing their wages and deactivating them, leaving families without the income they rely on. This settlement puts money back in workers’ pockets and holds DoorDash accountable.”

For workers like Rosendo Tacam, who first brought this case to light in 2023, the settlement announcement is a vindication …

author: Unknown
title: Eskişehir’de Eğitim Sen’den okul saldırısı tepkisi: Okullarda şiddeti sona erdirecek somut adımlar acilen atılmalıdır
content:
Eskişehir – Eğitim Sen Eskişehir Şubesi, Manisa’nın Turgutlu ilçesinde İnci Üzmez Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi önünde öğrencileri hedef alan silahlı saldırıya tepki göstermek amacıyla Köprübaşı’nda basın açıklaması yaptı. Açıklamayı Eğitim Sen Eskişehir Şube Başkanı Özkan Demirkol okudu.

Manisa’nın Turgutlu ilçesinde sabah saatlerinde okul önünde gerçekleşen silahlı saldırıda 11 öğrencinin yaralanmasına dikkat çeken Demirkol, okullarda her geçen gün tırmanan şiddet olaylarının ve öğrencilerin yaşam hakkını tehdit eden saldırıların münferit vakalarla geçiştirilemeyeceğini söyledi.

Okullarda yaşananların eğitim sisteminin içine sürüklendiği yapısal krizin, derinleşen toplumsal şiddet ikliminin ve öğrencilerin can güvenliğini yok sayan ihmaller zincirinin doğrudan sonucu olduğunu belirten Demirkol, “Okullarda şiddeti sona erdirecek somut adımlar acilen atılmalıdır” dedi.

Milli Eğitim Bakanlığının eğitim alanındaki temel sorunlara çözüm üretmek yerine “önlük” gibi şekilci dayatmalarla ve öğretmenlerin giyim kuşamıyla gündem oluşturduğunu söyleyen Demirkol, Bakanlığın bu yaklaşımından vazgeçmesi gerektiğini ifade etti.

Demirkol, “Okullarda ve okul çevrelerinde öğrenciler saldırıların hedefi olurken, eğitim emekçileri her gün şiddet riskiyle yüz yüze çalışırken, Bakanlığın eğitimin asıl ve hayati sorunu olan ‘güvenli okul, güvenli gelecek’ talebini görmezden gelmesi ve kamuoyunu tamamen şekilci meselelerle meşgul etmesi kabul edilemez” diye konuştu.

Öğrencilerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin yaşam hakkını ve güvenliğini tehdit eden sorunların görmezden gelindiğini belirten Demirkol, giderek derinleşen şiddet ikliminin halı altına süpürüldüğünü söyledi. Demirkol, bunun MEB’in eğitimin gerçek ihtiyaçlarından ve sahadaki yakıcı gerçeklerden ne kadar kopuk olduğunu gösterdiğini ifade etti.

Okulların aşırı güvenlikçi denetim alanlarına dönüştürülmesinin eğitim kurumlarının toplumsal ve demokratik dokusunu zedelediğini söyleyen Demirkol, öğrencilerin potansiyel birer “suç öznesi” olarak görülmesine dayanan yaklaşımların çözümsüzlüğü derinleştirdiğini belirtti.

Kalıcı çözümün okulları yalnızca güvenlikçi bir anlayışa teslim etmekten geçmediğini vurgulayan Demirkol, Psikolojik Danışmanlık ve Rehberlik (PDR) hizmetleri ile sosyal hizmet uzmanlarının eğitim sürecinin merkezine alınması gerektiğini söyledi.

Demirkol, “Okullarda psikolojik danışman, rehber öğretmen ve sosyal hizmet uzmanlarının görevlendirilmesi sıradan kontenjan hesaplarına ya da masa başında belirlenen sayılara göre değil; her okulun bulunduğu çevrenin sosyo-ekonomik koşulları, öğrencilerin ihtiyaçları ve somut riskler dikkate alınarak planlanmalıdır” dedi.

MEB’in eğitim ortamlarında yaşanan sorunlara şekilci ve polisiye yöntemlerle yaklaşmaktan vazgeçmesi gerektiğini belirten Demirkol, önleyici, koruyucu, pedagojik ve sosyal destek mekanizmalarının güçlendirilmesini istedi.

Eğitim sisteminin uzun süredir devam eden temel sorunlarından birinin kalabalık sınıflar olduğunu ifade eden Demirkol, sınıf mevcutlarının derhal azaltılması gerektiğini söyledi. Öğrenciler ve eğitim emekçileri açısından daha sağlıklı ve güvenli eğitim ortamlarının oluşturulması gerektiğini belirtti.

Müfredatın yalnızca sınava odaklı eleme ve yarıştırma mantığından çıkarılması gerektiğini söyleyen Demirkol, öfke kontrolü ve akran zorbalığıyla mücadele gibi konuların yanı sıra kültür, sanat ve sporla desteklenen güçlü bir pedagojik yapının oluşturulması gerektiğini ifade etti.

Demirkol, okulların güvenliğinin yalnızca polisiye yöntemlerle sağlanmaya çalışılmaması gerektiğini belirterek öğrencilerin sosyal, duygusal ve pedagojik ihtiyaçlarına yanıt verecek yeterli sayıda psikolojik danışman, rehber öğretmen ve sosyal hizmet uzmanının istihdam edilmesini istedi.

Eğitim Sen olarak Milli Eğitim Bakanlığına çağrıda bulunan Demirkol, öğrencilerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin can güvenliğinin sağlandığı, güçlü pedagojik bağların kurulduğu nitelikli ve demokratik bir okul ikliminin oluşturulması gerektiğini söyledi.

Demirkol, “Yeni saldırıların önüne geçilmesi için gereken önlemler vakit geçirmeksizin alınmalıdır” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: CNT Santander
title: Comunicado Anti-Galerna Fest
content:
El fin de semana del 25 y 26 de septiembre tendrá lugar en Santander un festival de música de ideología neofascista, organizado por la Asociación Alfonso I. Las bandas anunciadas tienen causas abiertas en diferentes países europeos por la presencia de homofobia, xenofobia, racismo y violencia en sus letras. Un año más se celebrará sin que el Gobierno de Cantabria lo impida, estando avisado con mucho tiempo de antelación, año tras año.


Desde CNT Santander,

reclamamos que se garantice el cumplimiento de la legislación vigente

, especialmente en materia de igualdad, prevención de la discriminación, seguridad y protección de los derechos fundamentales, y que actúen dentro de sus competencias ante cualquier conducta que pudiera vulnerarla.


Desde CNT Santander, mostramos

nuestra total oposición a la realización de este festival

, ya que consideramos que la normalización y la difusión de ideologías que promueven el odio, la discriminación y la exclusión de determinados colectivos son incompatibles con una sociedad democrática y con los principios de igualdad y dignidad que nosotras defendemos como sindicato de clase.


Esta celebración lo único que genera es más oleadas de racismo, odio y violencia en nuestras calles. Por ello,

no podemos permanecer indiferentes

 ante iniciativas que utilicen la música y los espacios como vehículo de propaganda de ideologías totalitarias y de odio.


Como personas que rechazan cualquier tipo de discriminación y violencia sobre cualquier ser humano no podemos quedarnos calladas frente a esta impunidad de actuación que poseen este tipo de grupúsculos y núcleos. No se pueden ni se deben normalizar los discursos que promulgan estas asociaciones y bandas europeas con ideología de extrema derecha.


Desde CNT Santander,

reivindicamos que los espacios de ocio sean lugares de encuentro, libertad y convivencia entre todas las personas

 y no plataformas para la difusión de mensajes que puedan incitar a la discriminación y a la violencia.


Nuestra oposición a la celebración del festival Galerna no supone un rechazo a la libertad de expresión o a la cultura musical, como muchas personas vitorean. Precisamente porque

defendemos una sociedad libre, plural y diversa, consideramos necesario establecer unas líneas rojas frente a la propaganda de odio y frente a cualquier intento de convertir la intolerancia en algo socialmente aceptable

. Hay líneas que no pueden ni deben traspasarse. Cuando se vulneran los derechos humanos de todas las personas hay acciones y opiniones que dejan de ser aceptables, y es algo que como sociedad deberíamos tener muy presente.


Como dijo Buenaventura Durruti:

¡Al fascismo no se le discute, se le destruye!

, y todas

juntas debemos destruirlo, alzando la voz y no permaneciendo impasibles

. Tenemos que gritar bien alto que no permitiremos que campen a sus anchas con sus ideas racistas y fascistas entre nuestros barrios. Cantabria es, y será siempre, antifascista. Queremos paz y libertad en nuestras calles y que cualquier persona pueda habitarlas sin miedo a ocupar los espacios.


Desde CNT Santander, hacemos un llamamiento a la

unidad de clase, a la solidaridad, al apoyo mutuo y a la convivencia

, y animamos a la ciudadanía y a las organizaciones sociales y sindicales a expresar de manera pacífica su oposición a la normalización de la ideología nazi y fascista.


Tomaremos las calles en la manifestación creada por Cantabria Antifascista que se celebrará el 26 de septiembre a las 12:00 horas en la plaza de los «Derechos Humanos», (C/Alta) de Santander.


¡¡No permitiremos ni el odio ni la discriminación!!


¡Solidaridad, fraternidad, salud y libertad!


La entrada

La manifestación, que comenzó en la Plaza Congreso y avanzó a lo largo de la Avenida de Mayo, tuvo su eje en el rechazo a las políticas económicas y de ajuste implementadas por el gobierno de ultraderecha de Javier Milei.


Estuvo impulsada principalmente por el Frente de Izquierda y de los Trabajadores Unidad (FIT-U) y contó con la adhesión de un amplio arco de organizaciones.


En el discurso de cierre, se sostuvo: “Esta es la bronca de quienes trabajamos y estamos lejos de llegar a fin de mes. La bronca de las y los jubilados que trabajaron toda la vida y hoy tienen que elegir entre comer o comprar sus remedios”.


El economista y militante Eduardo Lucita, integrante de Economistas de Izquierda (EDI), escribió un análisis sobre la jornada que compartimos a continuación:


Apuntes rápidos sobre la Marcha de la Bronca


“Para que nadie se quede peleando solo” MB.


Este sábado 19 de septiembre en horas de la tarde se llevó a delante la Marcha de la Bronca. Convocada hace poco más de dos meses atrás por la diputada nacional Myriam Bregman, la principal figura de la izquierda anticapitalista en el país, que desde hace 4 meses está a la cabeza de los políticos con mayor imagen positiva y que las encuestas le asignan una intención de votos del orden del 10%.


Desde aquella primera convocatoria a hoy fueron más de 350 organizaciones sociales, sindicales, políticas, y muchos grupos con distintas identidades (jubilados, ambientalistas, feministas, en defensa de las libertades democráticas, originarios, artistas y científicos…), que se sumaron a la convocatoria, cuya organización tuvo dos puntos culminantes. Una primera reunión, transformada en Asamblea, que se definió como Autoconvocatoria y luego una Asamblea a cielo abierto en Parque Lezama que definió el itinerario de la marcha, de Plaza Congreso a Plaza de Mayo, y sus objetivos. Entre esas reuniones hubo dos virtuales que conectaron organizaciones de todo el país. Así la Autoconvocatoria rápidamente se federalizó y tuvo sus réplicas (desiguales en cuanto a la cantidad de participantes pero importantes en términos políticos) en más de 50 ciudades de casi todas las provincias del país.

En lo que constituye “un plan de guerra contra el pueblo trabajador al servició de los capitalistas”.


En un período histórico en que el capital concentra, centraliza y homogeiniza por arriba mientras divide, escinde y heterogeiniza por abajo la Autoconvocatoria a Marchar juntos en la diversidad es el primer intento serio de unificar las diversas luchas que recorren el país, dándoles centralidad y una perspectiva política: “Tirar abajo el gobierno Milei, su plan y sus cómplices con una huelga general” (política). author: Luis Feliz Leon
title: AutoZone Workers Are Trying to Form the Company’s First-Ever Union
content:
When workers file for a union election, it’s like a Bat-Signal goes off: a column of light cuts through the night sky, summoning not Bruce Wayne but a swarm of anti-union managers and consultants who reap tens of thousands of dollars from sowing fear and doubt.


A new calculator from workers’ rights watchdog LaborLab

estimates

 that the parts retailer AutoZone has paid $210,696 to managers and lawyers to crush a union drive by 11 workers in one store in White Plains, New York. The workers went public in July with their drive to join United Auto Workers Local 259.


“It’s like hitting a fly with a mallet,” said Michael DiGuiseppe, vice president of Local 259. “At the first whiff of a union, they had their corporate executives in the store the next day. They’ve been camped out at a hotel around the corner since, and it’s been going on for two months.”


Managers have been pulling workers into meetings for antiunion propaganda and closely surveilling them to assess union support and chill the organizing. “They’ve had more corporate executive union-busters in the store than workers,” said DiGiuseppe.


The Economic Policy Institute estimates that U.S. employers

spend

 $1.7 billion annually on union-busting consultants and law firms.


“If you understand the corporate structure in America, then you understand they’re spending the money with expectations to make more money,” said AutoZone worker David Valencia. “And where is that money going to come from? It’s going to come from us!”


INVITATION TO FIRE YOU


The election is on September 25. Workers are seeking to become the first of the company’s 111,000 U.S. employees across 6,863 stores to form a union.


AutoZone management is pulling out all the stops to ensure this effort ends in defeat just like in 1992, when the Teamsters tried to organize a distribution center employing 200 workers. No workers have filed for an election at an AutoZone store or warehouse since.


The company has also pushed hard to exclude one of the key worker-organizers, Nathan DuCongé, from the bargaining unit, claiming he is a supervisor.


“If you don’t stop, we will accept your invitation to fire you,” Tammy Hamilton, a regional manager, told DuCongé on an August 28 recording shared with

Labor Notes

. DuCongé and his co-workers presented management with a demand letter in July calling for fair wages, regular raises, reliable scheduling, and affordable health insurance.


Hamilton admitted to monitoring his social media and organizing activities.


AutoZone CEO Phil Daniele III has also been skulking around DuCongé’s Instagram posts, screenshots shared with

Labor Notes

 indicate. Daniele’s total compensation last year was $9.64 million, 331 times the median salary of an AutoZone worker, which is just $29,017.


Federal labor law

protects

 workers’ right to organize a union and talk with co-workers about it, and prohibits employers from surveilling this activity, as well as from threatening to discipline or fire workers for exercising their rights. Supervisors, however, do not have these protections.


CARVED OUT FROM UNION


Workers and a UAW organizer said management succeeded in carving DuCongé out of the bargaining unit, claiming that he was a supervisor, even though he has no hiring or firing authority and other workers with the same title and responsibilities are eligible to vote.


“They wanted them to vote because these are people that already swung to the no side,” said DiGuiseppe. “It has nothing to do with who’s the supervisor and who’s not.”


But it could have delayed the election and cost Local 259 tens of thousands of dollars to challenge his exclusion in court. Instead, DuCongé and the union agreed to accept it.


“The guy fell on his sword,” DiGuiseppe said. “He’s like, ‘If this is what it takes to at least have a vote and let people know what’s going on here, then I’ll let them pull me out of it.’”


STUCK AT MINIMUM WAGE


Juan Accostupa, another White Plains worker, has worked for AutoZone for 10 years, earning $17 an hour. During that time, his wage has increased only to keep up with New York’s minimum wage.


“We don’t just cash people out,” said Accostupa. “We do extra work physically. We do the unloading of trucks. We do installations of wiper blades, headlights, and batteries.”


Workers say the company generates a lot of sales from these installation services, and it compels them to upsell washer fluid when customers purchase wiper blades, or grease when …

title: Kurdish shopkeepers face arrests, shop closures over general strike in Rojhilat
content:
Iranian security agencies have summoned and arrested dozens of Kurdish shopkeepers and market traders for joining a strike across cities in Kurdistan on 16 September, marking the fourth anniversary of Jina Amini’s state killing and the “Jin, Jiyan, Azadi” (Woman, Life, Freedom) uprising.


The agencies involved include the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Ministry of Intelligence.


Authorities have also temporarily sealed businesses under judicial orders and forced some shopkeepers and traders to sign written pledges not to join future strikes.


A shopkeeper in Kamyaran told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) that, on the evening of 16 September, following a widespread strike on Toubrehriz Street, IRGC Intelligence telephoned several shopkeepers and market traders who had closed their businesses that day, summoning them to its local office.


The source said officers ordered them to report within hours or face the closure of their businesses. Several traders went to the office late that night following the threats.


Once there, officers threatened to open judicial cases against them. An elderly shopkeeper who objected was beaten and insulted in front of the others. Those summoned were then made to sign written pledges not to take part in similar strikes in future.


As the pressure on traders in Kamyaran continued, Ministry of Intelligence forces violently arrested at least six shopkeepers. KHRN knows their identities but is withholding their names.


Two were released from Kamyaran Prison on 19 September, while the other four remain in detention and despite their families’ efforts to obtain information, their whereabouts and condition remain unknown.


A source in Sanandaj said Ministry of Intelligence forces arrested at least four market traders during the 16 September strike for taking part.


Other shopkeepers were summoned to the police department responsible for supervising business premises, where they were threatened and forced to sign written pledges.


KHRN has learned that dozens of shops in Sanandaj and Saqqez were sealed under judicial orders following the strike.


On 15 September, the day before the strike, websites and Telegram channels affiliated with security agencies in various cities across Kurdistan published a notice attributed to those agencies, threatening shopkeepers and market traders against taking part.


The notice stated: “Any support or cooperation by shopkeepers and trade associations with counter-revolutionary elements during the recent calls for action will result in their shops being sealed for six months and judicial action against the shop owners.”
