author: Sophia Sheera
title: Labour Could Win Over 80% of Green and Lib Dem Voters With Progressive Policies, Poll Suggests
content:
Eight in ten Green and Liberal Democrat voters would be open to switching allegiances, depending on Labour’s future choices.


A wealth tax on people worth more than £10 million could convince 37% of respondents who currently support the Greens or Lib Dems to vote for Andy Burnham’s party, according to a new poll carried out for

Zeteo UK

. 


Where former chancellor Rachel Reeves ruled out a wealth tax under Keir Starmer’s premiership, Andy Burnham has hinted that his government might

“ask for a little more”

 from rich taxpayers.  The Greens have backed an annual 1% tax on personal wealth of more than £10m – and double that for people with assets of more than £1bn.


Some 36% of respondents to the poll said they would be tempted to vote Labour if the party raised the personal tax-free allowance to £15,000 or higher. Reform UK has also promised to raise this threshold if voted in. 


The polling figures come three weeks before the Holborn and St Pancras byelection triggered by former prime minister Keir Starmer’s resignation as an MP. Green party leader Zack Polanski will stand against Labour’s Camden council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali and Patrick Stillman, the outgoing chair of the Camden Liberal Democrats. 


Other policies that could tempt progressive voters towards Labour include bringing water companies into public ownership, with 31% of Green and Lib Dem voters saying they’d consider changing allegiances if Burnham’s government pushed for nationalisation. Suspending all arms exports licences to Israel would tempt 27% of respondents towards Labour, the poll also showed.

title: On this day, 29 August 1997, workers at the Lusty Lady Club in San Francisco voted to join the…
content:
workingclasshistory

:

On this day, 29 August 1997, workers at the Lusty Lady Club in San Francisco voted to join the Exotic Dancers Union, part of a local of the Service Employees International Union (SEIU).

Following a campaign of organising and direct action, which included the women deciding to dance only with their legs closed in protest, they won significant improvements.

Their achievements included guaranteed work shifts, pay increases, removal of one-way mirrors (which enabled clients to film them), and protection from arbitrary discipline and firing. Management also agreed to abolish a racist scheduling practice, under which only one dancer of colour could be on stage at any one time.

The workers later took over the club and ran it as a workers’ co-operative, with elected management.

Three former workers tell their story in our podcast episode 20 about the union:

author: C.J. Polychroniou
title: This Rising Leftist Party Hopes to Turn Back Germany’s Fascist Wave
content:
The leftist Die Linke party won the most votes in Berlin, even as the far right AfD won a state election in the north.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Germany is now facing the same systemic crisis that its leaders once diagnosed in other European countries, such as Greece, Portugal, and Spain, in the early 2010s. Economic woes and anti-immigrant sentiment have given rise to anti-establishment politics, which in turn is reshaping the country’s political landscape. Indeed, after the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party achieved a historic result in the Saxony-Anhalt state in eastern Germany, the fascists have just won another state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and also made significant gains in the election held in the city-state of Berlin. But it was the radical left Die Linke (the Left), the successor to the ruling Socialist Unity Party (SED) of the former German Democratic Republic, that won the most votes in Berlin.

In the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural state in Germany’s former communist east where unemployment stands at nearly 8 percent, well above the national average, the AfD took first place by winning 38.2 percent of the vote on September 20, while the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) came second with 35.5 percent. Chancellor Merz’s center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) got routed as it failed to cross the 5 percent threshold, thus not winning a single seat in the state parliament for the first time anywhere in Germany. Merz described the result as “a disaster” for his party but vowed to stay in office and press ahead with his unpopular reforms to the German economy, which consist of imposing austerity measures and do not touch the rich. The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) also failed to clear the 5 percent threshold, while Die Linke took just 6.5 percent and the Greens took 5.7 percent.

The state election in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania was another resounding victory for the AfD and represented something of a rebuke of the SPD-Die Linke coalition that has governed in the state capital of Schwerin for the past five years. Indeed, what is most unexpected about the result in this German state election is that, unlike Saxony-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania was not considered an AfD stronghold. Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania has the lowest proportion of immigrants among all of Germany’s 16 federal states.

In the Berlin state election, Die Linke finished first with 25.3 percent of the vote, ahead of the CDU which got 19 percent, while the AfD won 16 percent, up 6.9 points from the last election.

Die Linke more than doubled the vote percentage it received in the previous Berlin state election in 2023, when it won 12.2 percent of the vote. The party cannot form a government alone, but is clearly in a position to lead a coalition government with the Social Democrats and the Greens and could see its mayoral candidate Elif Eralp become the first leftist mayor of Berlin.

Housing was at the center of the Berlin election and is undoubtedly the key factor behind Die Linke’s surge in popularity. Led by the charismatic 45-year-old Eralp — the daughter of Turkish exiles and a human rights advocate who has served in the Berlin House of Representatives since 2021 and is often called “Berlin’s Mamdani” — Die Linke focused its campaign on rent controls and more social housing, including support for implementing Berlin’s 2021 housing referendum, in which nearly 60 percent of voters backed a legal process to expropriate properties from big landlords. In Berlin, major housing and financial corporations own hundreds of thousands of apartments and thus have major influence over rents in the neighborhoods in which they own properties.

Bringing large private housing stocks under public ownership is a truly radical solution to the housing problem facing Berlin. The 2021 referendum is not legally binding but has nonetheless found massive support among the young people of Berlin in particular, who voted overwhelmingly for Die Linke. Yet, it could potentially become law if the parties in control of the Berlin Senate choose to make it so, although such a move would face various judicial challenges. A far less radical measure, a Berlin rent cap law, was declared unlawful by the German Federal Constitutional Court.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: El fascismo en el Estado español: un genocidio de clase que no se puede maquillar
content:
El príncipe Juan Carlos de Bourbon y el dictador Francisco Franco en Madrid, Reino de España. Fuente: Wikimedia


Un genocidio ideológico y de clase.


El fascismo, o falangismo, en España significó un genocidio ideológico y de clase. Fueron asesinados y torturados hombres, mujeres y niños inocentes. Fue un castigo a quienes defendieron la legalidad vigente, a quienes se atrevieron a soñar con un mundo mejor, a pensar y a cuestionar los privilegios de la oligarquía. No fue un exceso ni un error: fue un proyecto para aplastar al pueblo trabajador y devolverle el poder a quien nunca lo quiso soltar.


Un golpe de Estado traidor y cobarde.


La República sufrió un golpe de Estado, un golpe traidor y cobarde. Se convirtió en guerra civil porque el pueblo resistió. Y ese pueblo trabajador, con las manos y con la dignidad, tuvo que plantar cara a unos golpistas que contaron con la ayuda necesaria del nazismo alemán y del fascismo italiano para vencer esa resistencia. Conviene no olvidarlo: no se ganó aquella guerra con razones; se ganó con aviones extranjeros y con terror.


Quien piensa diferente no es fascista.


Quien piensa diferente y defiende su postura con argumentos, que podemos compartir o no, no es un fascista. El fascismo no utiliza argumentos porque no los tiene. Su argumento es la mentira, la fuerza y la violencia. Llamar fascista a cualquiera que discrepe es un error, pero mucho peor es lo contrario: blanquear lo que fue el fascismo real, el que fusiló, encarceló y torturó.


Ni comparaciones interesadas ni olvido.


Quienes comparan el fascismo español con el comunismo lo hacen por ignorancia o, peor, de forma intencionada, para lanzar bulos y prostituir la historia. Y quien lo compara con los defensores de la independencia, del derecho de autodeterminación de los pueblos o de otro modelo de Estado se equivoca, casi siempre a propósito y otras veces ejerciendo de mamporrero del poder. Defender que un pueblo decida su futuro es un derecho democrático, no una ideología del odio.


Memoria para no repetir.


Mirar hacia atrás no es quedarse anclado en el pasado. Es entender por qué hoy la ultraderecha avanza con la bandera falsa de lo antisistema, cuando nadie es más sistémico que ella. Es entender por qué no podremos construir una sociedad más justa sin superar el régimen del 78, que se edificó sin ajustar cuentas con aquel pasado. Y es entender que la respuesta a los herederos de aquel golpe no está en la moderación ni en las medias tintas, sino en la unidad de la clase trabajadora.


Porque la memoria es también una herramienta de lucha. Quien olvida quién asesinó a nuestros abuelos acaba aceptando que los nietos de los verdugos sigan mandando.


Até a vitoria sempre!


André Abeledo Fernández

author: dev
title: Le sacrifice du ciel
content:
Le philosophe Mohamed Amer Meziane publie son troisième livre,

Le Sacrifice du ciel. Une autre histoire de la raison

, qui vient rouvrir, reprendre et poursuivre le cycle ouvert par

Des empires sous la terre

 (2021) et

Au bord des mondes

 (2023).


Le thème du « sacrifice du ciel » fait écho à ceux de la sécularisation, de la mort de Dieu et du « désenchantement du monde ». Ces lieux communs, au sein de l'attirail des pensées critiques, ressemblent à des enjeux à la fois familiers et méconnus.


À voir lundi 21 septembre à partir de 20h


Les « statuaires de la pensée », expression du livre renvoyant au panthéon fatigué des « grands auteurs » européens, ne nous ont légué que peu d'outils pour y faire face. Il se pourrait, en plus, que ces thèmes « biens connus » (c'est-à-dire peut-être totalement impensés) aient obscurci la compréhension qu'on a de ces grands auteurs eux-mêmes. C'est la conséquence d'un des points principaux du livre : l'

orientalisme

, sous la forme de la critique historique des textes sacrés, a joué un rôle matriciel pour la production du savoir occidentalisé.


À partir de là, l'enquête donne lieu à une autre histoire de la philosophie : au prisme de l'orientalisme, Spinoza, Kant et Hegel apparaissent sous un autre jour. Leurs façons de penser la religion, ses rapports à la pensée et à la politique, est très loin cependant de s'être cantonnée au seul domaine de la philosophie. Elles participent de mouvements qui les précèdent et leur survivent, et qui constituent le sol sur lequel se sont déployées les sciences humaines et sociales « modernes ». Un ensemble de mythes vivaces s'ancrent dans cette histoire : le christianisme comme seule religion de la sortie de la religion, le protestantisme comme religion du monde moderne, le monothéisme comme origine de la violence, le fanatisme comme caractéristique des « religions de la Loi »…


Le Sacrifice du ciel

 se présente comme une critique des savoirs, une « histoire souterraine » de la connaissance. Celle-ci ne se contente pas d'en exhumer les marges, mais entend ressaisir l'héritage d'un centre occulté en montrant que la raison n'est pas « occidentale ». Se pose alors une question simple, mais trop souvent ignorée (y compris par la critique décoloniale) : comment les « orientaux » ont-ils eux-mêmes pensé l'orientalisme ? La philosophie d'Afghāni et la « métaphysique insurrectionnelle » de l'émir Abdelkader ont été les lieux d'une résistance formulée au nom du savoir et d'une « critique traditionnelle de la tradition », et deviennent ici ceux de l'élaboration d'une « pensée-autre » (comme le disait Abdelkébir Khatibi, en partant de Fanon).


« La tâche de cet anti-impérialisme philosophique a surtout été de montrer la profonde irrationalité de tout ce système militaro-fossile qui, avec un fracas et une morgue confinant à la folie, s'est targué d'être la seule Raison qui soit. »

title: Apocalypse Now: Naomi Klein y Astra Taylor investigan la alianza del «Fin de los Tiempos»
content:
¿Qué impulsa a los fundamentalistas religiosos, aceleradores tecnológicos y etnonacionalistas antiinmigrantes a provocar el fin del mundo? La lucha por el futuro se está desarrollando rápidamente ante nuestros ojos. Con debates agitando Washington por las llamadas a frenar la inteligencia artificial antes de que sea demasiado tarde, mientras Estados Unidos continúa librando guerras oficiales y no oficiales en todo el mundo. Sí, hay destrucción por todas partes. Pero estos actores han ideado cuidadosamente un plan: acelerar una visión que combine imágenes bíblicas, militantes y futuristas del fin de los tiempos para poder salvarse a sí mismos. Por the Intercept


Esta semana en The Intercept Briefing, la presentadora Akela Lacy entrevista a las autoras y documentalistas galardonadas

Naomi Klein

 y

Astra Taylor

, cuyo nuevo libro, «

Fin de los tiempos, el fascismo y la lucha por el mundo vivo

«, traza a los actores que quieren acelerar el fin del mundo.


«No sentíamos que las viejas formas de entender quién es Trump, lo que intenta lograr — incluso lo que es el fascismo — capturaran completamente lo que estábamos viendo. Aquí estamos pensando en invadir Groenlandia, declarar Canadá el estado número 51, crear un ejército ICE, la relación con las prisiones de máxima seguridad de El Salvador. Así que estamos intentando mapear esto», dice Klein. Parecía ser «un fascismo que no tenía visión de que nuestro mundo continuara. Siempre hay una cualidad apocalíptica en el fascismo, pero hay un horizonte para el grupo interno tras el cataclismo, y no veíamos eso en esta política. Se trataba mucho más de refugiarse y dar por sentado la avería.»


«El fascismo de los tiempos finales es una alianza de tres componentes principales», dice Taylor. Los fundamentalistas religiosos que ayudaron a elegir a Donald Trump, queriendo acelerar un violento Armagedón para que Jesús regrese. Los aceleradores tecnológicos «exaltan la posibilidad de que algún tipo de superinteligencia, algún tipo de ser digital, pueda tomar el control.» Los etnonacionalistas ven la inmigración como una amenaza existencial, así que fortalezcan la frontera y acaparan recursos. «Estas diferentes partes encuentran una especie de alianza incómoda en su convicción de que este mundo va al garete y que su grupo sobrevivirá a los escombros», dice Taylor.


Puede sonar extraño. Y lo es. Pero eso no significa que debamos ignorarlo, dice Klein. «Este es un patrón de pensamiento realmente peligroso: que de las peores cosas posibles surge la hermosa y gloriosa ciudad dorada. Y ese es el modelo de todas estas películas de acción y videojuegos, y lleva a abrazar lo peor y a no temer lo que deberíamos temer», dice Klein. «Cuando Trump comparte un vídeo de una Gaza remodelada con una Trump Tower, está haciendo una versión de esa historia. Cuando Sam Altman dice que está invocando a un dios digital, y que vamos a tener utopía con IA, y sí, déjame cubrir el mundo entero con centros de datos y acelerar la crisis climática porque va a ser utopía… Él está haciendo la historia. Así que tenemos que ser capaces de identificarlo — porque todos estamos viviendo con las consecuencias de esta terrible historia y necesitamos mejores historias.»


«En este momento, nos enfrentamos a un fascismo que, de alguna manera, está en contra

de todos

 los humanos. Citamos a Kelly Hayes, una activista con base en Chicago, y ella dice: ‘Todo fascismo tiene sus subhumanos, y para los tecnofascistas, son los humanos en general.’ Esto abre una lucha mayor más allá de ‘soy un hombre’ para simplemente decir, esto es

la vida contra las máquinas

, y hay algo muy sin precedentes en eso y potencialmente muy unificador», dice Taylor, señalando que el levantamiento colectivo, a lo largo del espectro político, contra los centros de datos muestra a personas liberándose de un supuesto futuro inevitable.

author: groundxero
title: The Fury of the Pipers Is Telling
content:
Gabriel Rockhill’s book

 Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism

 (2025) is a lot more than what its critics are saying.


 


Shyamoli Jana


 


Gabriel Rockhill’s book

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism

 has ruffled a lot of lefty feathers. The Jacobin Magazine, which describes itself as a “leading voice of the American left”, published a critique of it titled

No, Western Marxism Wasn’t a CIA Plot

. The piece begins with warnings against the return of “the class line”, and continues with accusations of assigning “guilt by association”. The journal

Historical Materialism

, affiliated with the SOAS University of London, published a four-part review, out of which about three parts are criticism of “Stalinism”.


 


As good a researcher as Rockhill might be, he is not the most engaging writer. It isn’t until the middle of the book that one gets to the facts that can refute the lazy “guilt by association” charges levelled by the

Jacobin

 and the

HM

 reviewers. So in the following paragraphs, I’ll try to very briefly summarise Rockhill’s description of the anticommunist propaganda machinery and the three Frankfurt scholars’ – Theodor Adorno, Max Horkheimer and Herbert Marcuse – role in it. If you are new to the topic and do not have the time to read the 400-odd-page book, I’d recommend you read the chapter

Imperial Intellectual Apparatus

. At the end, I will engage with parts of

HM

’s critiques. The facts I cite here are only a small subset of the facts Rockhill mentions in his book.


 


A ‘left’ for the Empire 


 


To give an idea about how the anticommunist propaganda apparatus operates, we will discuss two examples, the Information Research Department (IRD) and the Congress for Cultural Freedom (CCF).


 


After World War II was over, the ‘red scare’ propaganda phase began anew, overtly and covertly. British Labour MP Christopher Mayhew drew up a proposal to create a “Third Force” propaganda campaign that “would attack capitalism as well as Communism and promote the Social Democratic values associated with the Labour government”

1

. In Mayhew’s words, the creation of this Third Force would be “purely tactical – a cover designed to undermine any left-wing opposition”

2

. And from this proposal was born the Information Research Department (IRD), an outgrowth of the British propaganda agencies of wartime, becoming “one of the largest and best-funded departments in the Foreign Office”.

3


 


How did the IRD operate? It used a network of academics and journalists, many of whom were given material from the IRD that they passed off as their own work. Journalists in its web worked for “the Observer, the Guardian, the Financial Times, the Times, the Daily Mirror, the Daily Mail, the Telegraph and the Sunday Express.” This network included “freelance journalists and journalists working for ITN and Reuters.”

4


 


“The BBC was completely controlled at multiple levels, and MI5 – the UK’s domestic Security Service – vetted “its staff for ‘subversives’ from the 1930s until the practice was revealed in 1985.””

5

 The list of agencies that the IRD “established, penetrated, subsidized, collaborated with, or took control of” included Reuters, Foreign News Service and Arab News Agency, among many others.

6

 It was involved in the production of TV programmes, supported NGOs, and founded the Institute for the Study of Conflict (ISC) with funding from Shell, British Petroleum and the oligarch Richard Mellon Scaife. The ISC became one of the IRD’s propaganda outlets.

7


 


The IRD had a very solid distribution strategy for its propaganda material. It would publish and promote books that suited its purpose, sometimes bulk order prints in order to subsidize production, distribute them widely and translated them in multiple languages.

8

 One such author the IRD favoured was George Orwell, who made a list of suspected communists and gave it to the IRD. The IRD had “the foreign rights to a significant portion of Orwell’s literary output, and it spent years distributing his anticommunist literature all over the world, translating it into at least twenty languages, creating an animated film version of Animal Farm, and collaborating with the CIA on a feature-length film based on the same book”.

9

 A famous IRD academic was Robert Conquest, who was in the IRD and used the IRD files for his book

The Great Terror: Stalin’s Purge of the Thirties

 (1968).

10


 


This is just scratching the surface of …

title: Murat Çakır: Germany is openly playing a dangerous game
content:
Should Germany’s state elections and the rise of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) be seen merely as a temporary shift in voting patterns? Or are they a direct consequence of the political establishment, Germany’s militarist turn and the deepening crisis of capitalism? Murat Çakır, a researcher at the Rosa Luxemburg Foundation, said mainstream parties are legitimising fascist rhetoric by resorting to anti-refugee demagoguery, while the reformist left has deepened this political vacuum by moving away from genuine class politics. Caught between economic decline, deindustrialisation and growing hostility towards Russia, Germany is putting increasing pressure on workers at home while pursuing a dangerous course of militarism abroad that could open the door to nuclear catastrophe.


Writer and researcher Murat Çakır said the only way to confront the growing threats of fascism and war in Germany in particular and Europe more broadly is for migrants and workers to strengthen a common social struggle along anti-capitalist and anti-militarist lines.


I would like to ask about the elections in Germany, the possible scenarios and their potential short-, medium- and long-term implications. First, there was an election in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD made a strong showing. This was followed by elections in Lower Saxony, where the mainstream parties lost votes while the AfD increased its share. Berlin will hold its state election next Sunday. Although the Left Party appears to be ahead, the AfD is also seeing an increase in support there.


How would you define the AfD: as radical right, populist right, or explicitly fascist? How should the growing support for the party and the forces around it be interpreted?


The state elections in Germany and the AfD’s growing share of the vote are not merely a temporary shift in electoral preferences; they are a direct consequence of the deepening crisis of the political establishment and the capitalist system. As for how the party should be defined, it would be wrong to soften its character by describing the AfD merely as “populist” or “far right”. This party is directly racist and fascist in character. The real question, however, is what is fuelling this fascist force. Mainstream parties, the Social Democratic Party of Germany (SPD), the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), the Greens and others, appear on the one hand to complain about the rise of the AfD, while on the other pursuing policies that legitimise its rhetoric.


What these parties are doing collectively is promoting the lie, or rather the demagoguery, that migrants and refugees are the root cause of all these problems. The political establishment has been doing this for a long time. Whenever there is a crisis, migrants or refugees are immediately portrayed as being responsible for it.


The absence of a genuine left-wing alternative that engages in class struggle, gives voice to people’s concerns and develops realistic proposals is pushing people towards fascist parties that offer simplistic solutions while simultaneously creating enemies.


There is, on the one hand, xenophobia and racism deliberately fuelled by the political establishment. By adopting the rhetoric of fascist parties and putting similar policies into practice, the establishment is effectively strengthening them. Look, for example, at the plans to establish detention camps in the Maghreb region of North Africa. This is already one of the demands of fascist parties. Ultimately, the far right is exerting serious pressure on mainstream parties of both the right and left to pursue increasingly radical policies.


From this perspective, we can say that the rise of fascist parties in Germany and other European countries is a consequence of the crisis facing the political establishment, preparations for war, the militarist transformation and neoliberal policies. The other side of the problem is the failure of a genuine left-wing party rooted in class struggle to emerge as an alternative.


In this context, we can speak in particular of the profound failure of German reformism. Although they have recovered some support in Berlin, we will see whether they can fulfil the promises they have made if they come to power. Failing to move beyond narrow identity politics and lecturing people from ivory towers about how they should live is not left-wing politics. It does nothing but drive people towards fascist parties that, like the Pied Piper of Hamelin, offer …

title: Die Berliner AfD vor der Wahl
content:
Am 20. September soll in Berlin das Abgeordnetenhaus (AGH) und in den Bezirken die Bezirksverordnetenversammlungen (BVV) gewählt werden. Die AfD tritt mit insgesamt 222 Kandidierenden an – alle Namen und Portraits sind zu finden auf https://noafd.info. Das sind rund zehn Prozent ihrer Mitglieder in der Hauptstadt. Aktuelle Umfragen sehen für die AfD im Schnitt fast 18 Prozent der Stimmen voraus (1). Das wäre eine Verdoppelung im Vergleich zur Wiederholungswahl 2023. Damals haben sie 17 Personen ins AGH und insgesamt 64 in die zwölf Bezirksparlamente geschickt.


Die Stimmen wollen sie holen mit der Kampagnenklammer „Berlin. Stark. Machen“. Eine Mischung aus Migration, Ordnung/Sicherheit, nationale bzw. kulturelle Identität und ein Angriff auf „linke“ Politik. Sichtbar eigentlich nur auf rund 25.000 (2) Plakaten (viel dokumentiert: https://t.me/keinPlakatDerAfD): „Remigration ist nicht alles, aber ohne Remigration ist alles nichts.“ (Martin Kohler), „Berlin braucht Ordnung.“ (Marc Bernicke), „Für Sicherheit, Sauberkeit und Gerechtigkeit“ (David Eckert), „Gerne Deutsch.“ (Robert Eschricht), „m/w/d: männlich, weiß, deutsch.“ (Hendrik Pauli), „Lasst uns Berlin vor dem links-woken Wahnsinn verteidigen!“ (Marc Vallendar), „Gute Mobilität durch Verkehrsvielfalt statt Verkehrsideologie.“ (Rolf Wiedenhaupt), „Für Wissenschaftsfreiheit und gegen Cancel-Culture an unseren Unis.“ (Martin Trefzer) und auf Großplakaten „Migration braucht Grenzen“ oder „Berlin braucht Ordnung“.


Das Programm


Im Wahlprogramm finden sich diese plakativen Problembotschaften auch wieder. Wie schon in der ersten Veröffentlichung zur Berlin-Wahl auf Indy (3) und in der Analyse vom Apabiz (4) bemerkt, knüpft die AfD an bekannte Probleme an (z.B. Wohnen) und macht im Programm konkretere Vorschläge als in früheren Wahlprogrammen. Die Plakat-Kampagne ist dabei schmaler als das tatsächliche Programm – was nicht unüblich ist. Auch üblich ist, dass Parteien Versprechungen machen die sie wegen Finanzknappheit, Entscheidungskompetenzen (EU-Ebene, Bundesgesetze), Verfassungsrechtsproblemen und fehlendem Personal nicht umsetzen können. Die Kritik am AfD Programm sollte sich nicht auf die Umsetzbarkeit beziehen, sondern auf die politische Agenda. Es ist eine rassistische, nationalistische, sexistische und abelistische Politik, die die Machtverhältnisse weiter in Richtung besitzende Klasse verschieben soll und dafür vielen gesellschaftlichen Gruppen vergiftete Angebote macht.


Auf den zahlreichen Gegenveranstaltungen zu den Wahlkampfevents der AfD z.B. am Tierpark (5) oder in Charlottenburg (6) wurde das gut auseinandergenommen. Aber das reicht nicht, um die Stimmung in der Stadt zu kippen.


Die Kandidat*innen


Wer durch die Listen der Kandidierenden scrollt wird viele alte Gesichter erkennen. Der Großteil der Landesliste war schon vorher im AGH. In den BVVen haben sich viele ebenfalls länger etabliert und sind meist deckungsgleich mit den Bezirksvorständen der Partei. Ein paar neue Kuriositäten gibt es dennoch – der Tagesspiegel hat Andreas Quint (Platz 35 Landesliste und Anhänger der „Umvolkungs“-These) hervorgehoben (7). Andere sind z.B. eine Kathi Rödl aus Spandau, die als Bibliotheksleiterin der „Gedenkbibliothek zu Ehren der Opfer des Kommunismus“ auftritt und nun auf der BVV-Liste steht. Die Bilder der Kandiderenden hinterlassen den Geschmack von Consultants, Einzelunternehmer, KFZ-Mechaniker und vor allem ziemlich junge Rechte, die ebenso gut bei der Identitären Bewegung sein könnten (wo sie oft auch herkommen). Ein Teil des neuen AfD-Personals wurde bereits vor Jahren in der Jugendorganisation der Partei politisch sozialisiert und wandert nun geschlossen in die nächste Organisationsgeneration der Partei ein. Jan Streeck (JA Berlin, BVV und heutiger Platz 4 der Landesliste), David Eckert (JA-Landesvorsitz, Bezirksvorstand und ebenfalls Landesliste). Martin Kohler (erst JA/IB, aktuell Vorstand Generation Deutschland und jetzt Landesvorstand/Landesliste), Marc Bernicke (Polizist, JA, jetzt AfD-Parteiapparat und Landesliste) und Christopher Wiedenhaupt (Sohn des ehm. CDUlers und nun AfDlers Rolf Wiedenhaupt, auch JA, AfD/Bezirksstruktur und nun Landesliste). Es gibt leider bisher keine strukturierte Analyse der AfD Kandidiat*innen, mit der auch im Wahlkampf gearbeitet werden könnte. So hätte die bürgerliche Fassade den tatsächlichen innerparteilichen Netzwerken gegenübergestellt werden können. Diese analytische Schwäche ist ein Novum für Berlin aber …

author: Connor Knight
title: Anti-Hanson students strike again
content:
The second high-school student strike against Pauline Hanson in as many months took place on 17 September, with thousands of students across the country downing pens and taking to the streets, defying principals and politicians alike.

More than 3,000 marched in Melbourne, while 1,000 took to the streets in each of Sydney, Adelaide and Perth. Hundreds rallied in Brisbane, Canberra and Hobart, and more walkouts occurred in regional areas than during the previous national day of action.

The chants this time were the same but carried more urgency, given Labor’s plans to restrict immigration. They included “Migrants are welcome, racists are not!” and “Unite, unite, unite to fight the right!” The mood was irreverent. Right-wing provocateurs were taunted, and in Brisbane, protesters climbed on urban art sculptures and rode skateboards with red flags in hand. In Melbourne, far-right troll Avi Yemeni was surrounded by chanting students, against whom his bodyguards weren’t much use.

The right-wing media response to the first walkout was as patronising as it was sensational. An

Adelaide Now

headline is typical: “Teen anti-Hanson rallies: are students really thinking for themselves?” Hanson herself was furious, accusing students of “hating this country”.

The wonderfully impertinent attitude of students in light of these insults and accusations was well captured by high-school socialist Odessa, who told the Melbourne rally: “When the planet is burning, when we’re watching our world turn to dust ... They don’t get to tell us a single goddamn thing”.

The

Australian

reported that, in Sydney, “An organiser gave the crowd a moment to say how they felt about Senator Hanson after the protesters circled back to Hyde Park. Some could be heard shouting a number of profanities before dispersing”.

A striking feature of the protests was how many of the participants connected the rise of the right with capitalism. Signs and speakers consistently linked Hanson’s racist agenda to the interests of the billionaires and corporations who dominate politics and the economy.

“She is a battler for the bosses and the rich”, Queensland University of Technology student Sharon Binu argued from the platform in Brisbane. In Perth, year 10 student Esu put it this way: “When we look at the world today, who but those who grow fat off the misery of the many could doubt we need a total transformation of society?”

That total transformation will not be easy. But the high schoolers are at least giving it a shot, and showing up all those who choose to capitulate to, rather than resist, One Nation’s rise.

author: Unknown
title: Femicides in Batman and Osmaniye: Two women and three children killed
content:
Two women and three children have been killed in two cases of patriarchal violence in Batman and Osmaniye. In Batman, a 29-year-old man is suspected of stabbing his wife and their two young children to death before taking his own life. In Osmaniye, Didar Filiz, who was six months pregnant, was killed.


The first femicide occurred on Friday afternoon in the district of Kozluk in Batman. Following an emergency call, medical teams and police were dispatched to an apartment in a five-story building. Emergency responders found 29-year-old A.G. dead by hanging. His 27-year-old wife, S.G., and their two children, E.G. and M.P.G., had sustained stab wounds. The children were two and one year old, respectively. All four were pronounced dead at the scene.


According to the governor’s office, based on the evidence gathered so far, investigators believe that A.G. killed his wife and their two children before taking his own life. The bodies were taken for autopsy. Authorities are investigating a possible connection to an earlier dispute involving gold. A.G.’s brother-in-law had reportedly filed a complaint in May, stating that he had entrusted A.G. with around 2.5 kilograms of pure gold for safekeeping and was later unable to reach him. The governor’s office said it is investigating whether the dispute was connected to the killings.


Pregnant woman killed in Osmaniye


In Kadirli, in the Mediterranean province of Osmaniye, 20-year-old Didar Filiz was killed by her husband and three of his relatives. Filiz was the mother of two children and was six months pregnant. Her unborn baby also died as a result of the attack.


According to preliminary findings, an argument broke out during the night between Filiz and her 24-year-old husband, K.F., in the Yeşiltepe neighborhood. K.F. and three of his relatives are then alleged to have jointly assaulted the young woman. The attack ended only when other family members intervened.


Filiz was taken to Kadirli State Hospital with severe injuries, particularly to her head. Despite medical treatment, neither she nor her unborn baby could be saved. K.F. and three of his relatives were arrested in connection with the femicide. Investigations into the exact circumstances and the involvement of each suspect are ongoing.

author: Equality Now
title: Justice without discrimination: intersectional and grassroots perspectives on sexual violence in Mexico
content:
18th September 2026


Justice without discrimination: intersectional and grassroots perspectives on sexual violence in Mexico


9 min read


News and Insights


End sexual violence


Latin America and the Caribbean


This post is also available in:


Español

 (

Spanish

)


العربية

 (

Arabic

)

 (

French

)


Русский

 (

)


From 25 to 28 August, we held the National Meeting

Justice without discrimination: intersectional and grassroots perspectives on sexual violence

 in Mexico City, co-organized with seven partners from different states across the country:


Colectiva Ciudad y Género

,


EnIgualdad A. C.

,


Lúminas Centro de Derechos Humanos A. C.

,


Mujer Ideas Desarrollo e Investigación (MIDI)

, the


Office for the Defence of Children’s Rights (ODI)

, RAÍCES Análisis de Género para el Desarrollo, and the


Network of Indigenous Women Lawyers (RAI)

.


The gathering brought together 40 activists and defenders of women’s, children’s and Indigenous peoples’ rights, representing 25 civil society organisations, collectives and networks. It was shaped by a question that cuts across all of their work: what does advancing towards justice without discrimination for survivors of sexual violence mean in practice?


From standards to justice without discrimination


The starting point was to recognise a tension at the heart of access to justice in Mexico: the country has a broad legal framework for protection and has assumed significant international obligations, yet deep gaps remain between these standards and the lived experiences of those seeking justice. The lack of harmonisation of criminal legislation across states is compounded by territorial inequalities and structural forms of discrimination that have a particularly severe impact on Indigenous and Afro-descendant women, girls and adolescents, women and girls with disabilities, those living in rural areas, and other historically discriminated groups.


One of the key discussions at the meeting therefore focused on what it truly means to speak of justice without discrimination. In a panel featuring the National Network of Indigenous Women Lawyers (RAI) and the Network of Shelters for Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Women (CAMIA), anti-racist and intercultural perspectives were used to challenge one-size-fits-all responses to sexual violence. Drawing on the experiences and realities of Indigenous women, the discussion highlighted the need to recognise how racism, ethnic discrimination, gender and other inequalities intersect and can create specific barriers to accessing justice. From this perspective, addressing sexual violence through an anti-racist and intercultural lens means not only ensuring that rights are recognised, but also transforming institutional practices so that they respond to the diversity of women’s contexts, knowledge and experiences.


In working groups, participants also mapped the pathways that girls, adolescents and women survivors navigate when seeking access to justice, identifying barriers through an intersectional lens. In a country with more than 30 different criminal codes and deep territorial inequalities, guaranteeing the same rights requires recognising that barriers, available resources and relationships with institutions are not the same everywhere.


Changing the question: from the use of force to consent


One of the central themes of the meeting was the standard of consent. For decades, many laws on sexual violence have focused on questions such as: Was physical violence used? Did the victim resist? Did they scream? Were there injuries? International standards call for a shift in perspective and for a different question to be asked: was there free and voluntary consent?


This shift is fundamental because it recognises that sexual violence does not always involve the visible use of force. It can occur in contexts shaped by intimidation, abuse of power, dependency, coercion, vulnerability or other circumstances that make it impossible for a person to freely express their will.


However, this standard is still far from being incorporated consistently across Mexican legislation. Equality Now’s analysis,


From the paradigm of force to that of consent: towards comprehensive reform of sexual offences in Mexico

, shows that 32 of the country’s 33 criminal codes continue to define rape on the basis of the use of physical, moral or psychological violence. Oaxaca is currently the only state to have removed …

author: Unknown
title: Evrensel neden milli güvenliği tehdit etsin?
content:
Çalışma temposunun her geçen gün yükseldiği şu daralan ekonomide hayata tutunmak için çabalarken yorgun düşen bedenimi dinlendirmek için sosyal medyadan soyutlandığım bir zamandı. Her şehirde her gün kadın cinayetleri, iş cinayetleri, haklarını alamayan emekçilerin ''açım, açım'' diye haykırışları okul alışverişinden tarumar olan aklımı yememek ve biraz dinlenmek için telefonumdan uzaklaşma gereği duydum.

Gece vardiyasındaydım. Art arda dizilmiş onlarca makine arasında kırmızı ışıklar yanmasın diye mekik dokuyup duruyordum. Telefonum mesaj sesiyle titredi. Oysa ki; bankalar dışında mesaj atanım pek olmazdı. Gelen mesaj ile öfkem doruğa ulaştı.

Hemen sosyal medya haberini art arda okumaya başladım.” Böyle bir şey nasıl olabilir?” diye anlamaya çalıştım.” Evrensel Gazetesi X hesabına milli güvenlik gerekçesiyle erişim engeli getirildi!” Haber aynen buydu. Bir gazete “ülke güvenliğini nasıl tehlikeye atabilir?” diye düşünüyorum. Bir türlü cevap bulamıyorum. Emekten yana bir gazete nasıl da koskoca devlete tehlike olabilir ki?

7 Haziran 1995 tarihinden bu yana politikasından, çizgisinden hiç şaşmadan hep hakikat peşinden koşan Evrensel gazetesinin kurulmasından bir yıl sonra Gaziantep'te 20 bin dokuma işçisi insanca yaşam, kıdem ve yıllık izin ve sigortalı çalışma için direnişe başladı. Medya holdinglerinin kayıtsız kaldığı bu dönemde, Evrensel gazetesi tüm imkanlarını seferber edip dokuma işçilerinin sesini sınırların ardına kadar duyurmayı sağladı. Sadece Ünaldı Direnişini değil, 30 yıla aşkın süredir hangi şehirde, hangi fabrikada olursa olsun, emekçilerin sesi olmayı başardı.

Devlet politikalarına karşı gösterdikleri eleştiriler ile devlet kademeleri tarafından sürekli baskılar ve yargılamalarla karşılaşmasına rağmen, emekten yana olan çizgisinden gram sapmadan bu günlere gelebildi.

Devlet kurumlarından milyarlık ihaleler alan Kalyon Holdingin çalışanlarına çip takması, Yıldızlar Holding'in çalışan madencilerin haklarına çökmesi, 30 yıllığına otobanların, köprülerin özel sektöre kiralanmasını kamuoyuna duyuran yine Evrensel gazetesi olmuştur. İşte tam da bu yüzden patronlar daha rahat bir şekilde işçilerin haklarını gasp edip, kamu mallarına sessizce çökebilmek için gazetemize sipariş üzerine erişim engeli getirmeye çalışıyor.

Revize edilen enflasyon verileri, hiçbir zaman tutturulamadığı gibi, 2026'da yapılan asgari zam ile emekçilerin daha düşük ücretle çalışılması sağlandı. Orta vadeli program ile emekçilerin ücretlerinde milyarlarca kayıp yaşanırken, patronların sermayesinde ise tam tersi bir durumla karşılaşıldı. Şimdi ise 2027'de yapılması düşünülen zam ile biz emekçileri aynı şekilde yaşatılmanın önünü açıyorlar.

Evrensel gazetesinin X hesabının kısıtlanmasının güvenlik gerekçesi olma ihtimalinden uzak olduğu bilinen bir gerçek. Erişim engelinin getirilmesi tamamen sermaye sahiplerinin, patronların siparişi üzerine getirildi. Emekçilerin sesinin duyurulmasının önüne geçirilerek, alın teri olan haklarının üzerine sessizce çökmenin yollarını aradılar çünkü.

Okullarda bir öğün sağlıklı, ücretsiz yemek talep etmek mi milli güvenliği tehlikeye atıyor?

MESEM’lerde çocukların emeği sömürülüyor, çocuklar atölyelerde ölüyor demek mi milli güvenliği tehlikeye atıyor?

Sokaklarda kadınlar katlediliyor. İstanbul sözleşmesi yaşatır demek mi milli güvenliği tehlikeye atıyor?

Enflasyon her geçen gün yükseliyor. Milyonlar açlık sınırının altında ücretle geçinmeye çalışıyor demek mi milli güvenliği tehlikeye atıyor? Yoksa onurlu bir yaşamın nasıl olduğunu milyonlara anlatmak mı milli güvenliği tehlikeye atıyor?

Son söz: Patronların ve devlet mekanizmaların bilmediği bir şey var. Evrensel gazetesi, polislerce katledilen Metin Göktepe'nin mirasıdır. Her işçi, bir Evrensel gazetesi muhabiridir. Dijital mecralarda engellense bile, işçiler haberleri sözlü dahi olsa milyonlara ulaştıracaktır. Unutmayınız ki; Evrensel gazetesi susmadı, susturulamayacaktır da. Dün, bugün olduğu gibi yarınların da sesi olacaktır.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Ngozi Nwosu-Juba
title: Who profits from ‘saving’ women?
content:
During a recent dialogue convened by Liberation Alliance Africa’s

Building Knowledge Bridges Community of Practice on Recentering African Feminist Epistemologies to Prevent and Respond to Sexual Violence

, bringing together activists, writers, and independent researchers from across the continent, an important and thought-provoking conversation emerged. While participants acknowledged the significant contributions of civil society organizations, development agencies, and other actors in advancing efforts to end violence against women and girls, there was also a collective reflection on the ways in which this support is framed and delivered.

I was struck by how this discussion raised critical questions about funding priorities, whose interests are ultimately served, who benefits most from existing interventions, and whether the structures and language designed to address violence may, in some instances, inadvertently reproduce inequalities or overlook the needs and voices of those most affected. The conversation challenged me to think beyond the availability of resources and examine the political, economic, and institutional dynamics that shape responses to violence against women and girls across the continent.

In my early days in feminist activism, I often highlighted to funders how our interventions had shifted away from speaking on behalf of women to “giving them voice.” This was widely regarded as progressive, even transformative, evidence that we had moved beyond paternalistic approaches and were empowering women to speak for themselves. It became a powerful narrative, one that resonated strongly with donors and development agencies alike.

Yet, over time, this language began to lose its appeal, as I started to interrogate the assumptions that underpinned it. Were women truly without voices, or were their voices simply being ignored, dismissed, or rendered unintelligible within systems of power?

The notion of “giving voice” positioned organizations like ours as benevolent intermediaries bestowing agency on those presumed to lack it. In doing so, it risked obscuring the fact that women had always spoken, resisted, negotiated, and articulated their realities, often in ways that did not fit donor expectations or development frameworks.

What does it mean to “give” women a voice? And who has the authority to bestow something that women have always possessed?

There is a long history of women’s resistance and political agency in Africa. In Nigeria, the

Women’s War of 1929

 stands as a powerful reminder that women have never been silent. Thousands of women in eastern Nigeria organized, mobilized, challenged colonial authority, and articulated their demands with remarkable courage and clarity. Their actions were neither facilitated by development projects nor enabled by donor-funded interventions. They emerged from women’s own collective consciousness, an inherited legacy of women’s determination to resist injustice.

In the Bamenda Grassfields of Northwest Cameroon, women organized one of the most significant grassroots uprisings against colonial authority in Central and West Africa. Faced with colonial policies that threatened their farmland, the women of Kom fought back.

Using

Anlu

, a traditional practice where women collectively sanction men who violate community norms, they organized marches and used satire to name and shame colonial collaborators. Through their actions, they brought administrative and economic life in the region to a standstill for months, and their protest ultimately forced the colonial government to reverse the land policies and contributed to the broader political shifts that shaped Cameroon’s path toward independence and reunification.

In Eastern Africa, Queen Muhumuza led a movement against British and German colonialists from Southern Uganda. According to the historian

Murindwa Rutanga

, Queen Muhumuza was the first major leader to mobilize peasants in Kigezi into organized anticolonial resistance against British rule starting in 1909. Drawing on her political experience and spiritual authority, she raised consciousness about the dangers of colonialism and united a broad sector of the Bakiga and neighboring communities in armed resistance. Under her leadership, communities resisted colonial boundary demarcations, obstructed missionaries and colonial agents, and challenged the expansion of colonial authority despite violent repression. Her efforts established her as one of the …

author: Unknown
title: Ayşe Tokyaz davası: Kamu görevlileri bu davadan ne öğrenecek?
content:
12 Eylül 1980 darbesi 46 yıl önce kaldı diyoruz. Fakat bazı sabahlara öyle uyanıyoruz ki darbe kendisini hatırlatıyor. Belki yok fakat hayaleti hâlâ etrafımızda.


Bu sabah da LGBTİ+ derneklerinin hesaplarına erişim engeli getirildiğini, ardından operasyon düzenlendiğini ve çok sayıda LGBTİ+ aktivistinin gözaltına alındığını öğrendik.


Gerekçe yine bildik: “Aile ve toplum düzeni” ve benzeri ifadeler.


Burada iki noktayı hatırlatıp haftanın asıl gündemine geçmek istiyorum.


Birincisi, aileyi bozan LGBTİ+’lar değil, patriyarkanın kendisi.

bianet’in erkek şiddeti çetelesi

 de bunun verilerini her ay ortaya koyuyor. Kadınlar evlerinde, sokakta, işyerlerinde erkek şiddetiyle karşı karşıya kalıyor. Erkek şiddeti hayatlarımızın her alanında.


İkincisi, LGBTİ+’ları hedef gösteren trol hesaplara ve haberlere erişim vermemek gerekiyor. Eleştirmek amacıyla bile olsa yapılan paylaşımlar, bu içeriklerin daha fazla yayılmasına neden olabiliyor.


Gelelim asıl meseleye.


Ayşe Tokyaz davasında 9 Eylül’de karar açıklandı. Aylar süren yargılamanın ardından Cemil Koç ve ona yardım eden erkekler hakkında karar verildi. Bu dava herkes açısından zordu elbette. Ama en çok Ayşe’nin ailesi için zordu.


Patriayrkaya karşı kadınların direnci


Tokyaz ailesi, özellikle de Ayşe’nin ikiz kardeşi Esra Tokyaz, duruşmalar boyunca geri adım atmadı.


Esra’nın mücadelesini ilk duruşmadan bu yana izliyoruz. Mahkeme salonunda, adliye önünde, açıklamalarda, sosyal medyada Ayşe’nin adını yaşatmak için mücadele etti. Sanıkların ve avukatlarının sözlerine rağmen Ayşe’yi suçlayan anlatının karşısında durdu.


Esra Tokyaz bana göre bu yılın kadınlarından biri.


Bunu yalnızca kız kardeşi Ayşe için verdiği mücadele nedeniyle söylemiyorum. Esra, kadın cinayetleri davalarında ailelerin neyle karşı karşıya kaldığını, bir kadının öldürülmesinden sonra mücadelenin nasıl sürdüğünü ve erkek şiddetinin yalnızca cinayet anından ibaret olmadığını da hepimize gösterdi.


Karar duruşmasının ardından Kadın Cinayetlerine Karşı Feministler’den Feride Eralp’in söyledikleri de bu nedenle önemli.


“Cemil Koç yalnız değil”


Eralp, mahkeme salonunda aylar boyunca dinlediğimiz erkeklik halini şöyle anlattı:


“Biz aylarca süren bir yargılama sonucunda, sanıkların birbirlerini suçladığı ve birbiriyle çelişki içine düştüğü bu celsede en az iki saat boyunca profesyonel bir katilden ekimoz renkleri dinledik. Bir valizin kendinden menkul bir suç işleme iradesi olabilir gibi, Ayşe’nin bedenini valize kendisi koymamış gibi, bu valizi bir gece ve bir gün boyunca ortadan kaldırmaya çalışmamış gibi, o ekimozları ben yapmadım valiz yaptı cümlesini duyduk.


Ejegül Ovezova


‘Bavula koyma hatası olmasaydı’ diyerek bu iradi eylemi kendinden bağımsızlaştırma çabası içerisinde olan bir sanık izledik. Yapmadığı ve bahsini dahi geçirmediği ise o gün sitenin güvenliğini çağırmak, 112’yi aramak gibi Ayşe’yi yaşatmaya dair eylemlerdi.


Cemil Koç bugün duruşmada Ayşe Tokyaz’ı öldürmediğini, Ayşe Tokyaz’ın içki ve uyuşturucu etkisinde merdivenden düştüğünü iddia etti. Bu iddia ile ilk defa karşılaşmıyoruz. Daha öncesinde de Ejegül Ovezova’nın Diyarbakır’daki bir binanın 8. katından düştüğünü iddia etmişti. Bu kişinin yanındaki, hayatındaki kadınlar her ne hikmetse düzenli olarak yüksekten düşüyor.


Bunun suçlusunun da yine kadınlar olduğunu uzun uzun anlatma cüretini erkek egemenliğinden alıyor. Bu adamın bir zamanlar polis olmuş olması, kadınların karakollara gittiklerinde neyle karşı karşıya kalabildiğine dair ürkütücü bir gerçeğe işaret ediyor."


Bu sözler, aslında davanın tamamını özetliyor.


Peki, biz Ayşe Tokyaz’ı öldürmekten yargılanan Cemil Koç ve ona yardım eden sekiz erkeğin yargılandığı dava boyunca ne gördük?


Kendisinden emin, ne yaptığını bilen, gerektiğinde adli tıp uzmanı gibi konuşan bir erkek gördük. Gerektiğinde hâkime talimat verme cüretini gösteren bir sanık dinledik.


Devletin koruyucu gücünü arkasına alarak suç işleme konusunda kendisine güvenen bir erkeklik biçimiyle karşı karşıya kaldık.


Bunun karşısında ise Esra vardı.


İkiz kardeşi için bütün dünyaya seslenen, duruşmalarda geri adım atmayan, Ayşe’nin öldürülmesini yalnızca bir adli dosya olarak görmeyen Esra.


Bir yandan Ayşe’nin ölümüne ilişkin deliller, raporlar ve tanıklıklar konuşulurken diğer yandan kadın cinayeti kavramının kendisi tartışmaya açıldı. Esra’nın beyanları tekrar tekrar gündeme getirildi. Medya suçlandı. Ailenin mücadelesi tartışmanın konusu haline getirildi.


Oysa ortada öldürülmüş …

author: Piper Hutchinson
title: Professors in the South Fear Doxxing and Harassment, New Survey Shows
content:
The survey found a significant spike in the number of faculty worried about physical threats to their safety.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A survey of higher education faculty in the South found professors are concerned about the political environment around higher education, with some fearing for their physical safety.

The annual survey from the American Association of University Professors included an open-ended question that allowed faculty to detail the problems they’re facing. Compared with previous years, there was a significant spike in faculty scared not only for their careers but also for their physical safety.

“I teach a subject that is now considered ‘controversial,’” a professor in North Carolina wrote. “As a result, I have had a non-student with a gun enter my classroom to intimidate me. I have received an email death threat from a student.”

The AAUP survey polls faculty at schools in Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas and Virginia. The association received about 2,700 responses, with 41 coming from Louisiana universities.

Across the nation, state leaders have put higher education under a microscope. The scrutiny has been particularly acute in conservative Southern states, where changes to education laws have been extensive.

In Alabama, lawmakers eliminated faculty governance at its public institutions, where professors and instructors previously had a say in campus policy decisions.

In North Carolina, faculty are now required to post their course outlines publicly, which survey respondents said has led to them receiving threats.

In multiple states, legislators have passed laws banning the teaching of divisive topics and prohibiting diversity, equity and inclusion programs.

Dozens of faculty members said they had to fight back against angry alumni, political officials and student activists who attempted to get them fired or doxxed them. Doxxing is the act of publishing someone’s private information without their consent in an attempt to bring harm to them.

“I was targeted for harassment and experienced death threats,” a full professor in Virginia wrote. ”I feel less safe doing my job than in the past. I have to think through the consequences of words I write in manuscripts.”

Numerous faculty said they either self-censored or were told not to use certain “off-limits” words such as gender, racism and even transportation because it includes the word “trans.” Some faculty said administrators used AI-screening tools to review their syllabi for certain words.

Some survey respondents reported that the anti-faculty fervor has also spilled off-campus.

“I had to leave my church because the youth pastor expressed from the pulpit that academics were enemies of the faith. This impacts my work as a faculty member as an important aspect of my personal life has become inaccessible,” an assistant professor in Florida wrote.

Faculty also described fears that their students might record them and use their lectures or course materials out of context. The responses mention several incidents in which students publicized faculty comments, assignments or curricula to highlight areas of conflict with their personal beliefs.

At LSU, law professor Ken Levy was suspended in early 2025 after mentioning Gov. Jeff Landry and President Donald Trump in profane comments to his class. Levy fought that suspension in court and lost. His comments came to light when someone shared a video of his lecture with Landry, who posted it online.

The survey also found that 29% of faculty have applied to jobs in other states since 2024 and the same share are considering applying.

The top reason faculty gave for wanting to leave the South was its political climate. Other leading answers included diminished academic freedom, changes to diversity, equity and inclusion policy, low pay, limited LGBTQ+ rights and limits to reproductive healthcare.

Additional findings included 14% of faculty saying they view artificial intelligence as a threat to their academic discipline, and 13% reporting they have lost federal grants since Trump returned to office.

The Trump administration has revamped the government’s approach to academic research funding, which has included cancelling millions in grants and slashing resources for …

author: The Canadian Press
title: Ottawa opens up 15% Trans Mountain equity stake to Indigenous groups on pipeline path
content:
The Canadian government has offered Indigenous groups a collective 15 per cent ownership stake in the

Trans Mountain pipeline

, advancing a long-promised plan to give First Nations equity in the federally owned pipeline.


In a letter to a First Nation along the pipeline’s path seen by The Canadian Press on Tuesday, a federal Department of Finance official said the equity investment would be equally distributed among participating groups “through a low-cost government-provided loan.”


The letter said Ottawa will provide eligible groups with up to $100,000 for participation costs for expenses such as travel, office space and equipment through March 2028, while separately covering independent advisers to assist with due diligence.


Details of the offer will be shared during a series of in-person meetings in Vancouver, Victoria, Kamloops and Edmonton planned for late October, the letter added.


Ottawa bought the existing

Trans Mountain pipeline

, its expansion project and related assets for $4.5 billion in 2018 after Kinder Morgan investors raised concerns that regulatory uncertainty made the investment too risky.


It later committed to exploring Indigenous economic participation in the expansion with the 129 Indigenous communities potentially affected by the project.


The expansion began operations in 2024 and increased the Trans Mountain system’s capacity to about 890,000 barrels per day from roughly 300,000 barrels per day.


Finance documents released that year said Ottawa planned to provide Indigenous groups with access to capital to acquire a stake in Trans Mountain.


The documents said the Indigenous stake could be held collectively through a special-purpose vehicle, giving participating groups governance rights and a share of cash generated by the pipeline.


Until now, however, the government had not publicly specified the size of the ownership stake it was prepared to make available.


Story by Brett Bundale


The post

Ottawa opens up 15% Trans Mountain equity stake to Indigenous groups on pipeline path

 appeared first on

APTN News

.

author: Mag
title: Sorgende Städte – Strategien für feministisches Vergesellschaften
content:
Dossier


„

Das Konzept „Sorgender Städte“ entwirft einen Ausweg aus der alltäglichen Care-Krise: Die (Sorge-)Bedürfnisse aller werden demokratisch ausgehandelt und über öffentliche oder gemeinwohlorientierte Angebote abgedeckt. Eine feministisch-sozialistische Kommunalpolitik entwickelt konkrete Projekte, die einen Einstieg in den Umbau ermöglichen. Es geht um feministisches Vergesellschaften als „revolutionäre Realpolitik“. (…) Das Konzept wurde im Kontext des spanischen Munizipalismus entwickelt. Dass die Idee aus Bewegungen kommt, die die Wohnviertel als politische Handlungsfeld erst nehmen, ist kein Zufall, denn auch Sorge findet im Nahraum statt. Selbstverständlich können ähnliche Ansätze aber auch für den ländlichen Raum entwickelt werden. Gleichzeitig gibt es eine

internationale Vernetzung von munizipalistischen Bewegungen


. Denn klar ist: Was sich vor Ort als Krise im Alltag niederschlägt, hat häufig transnationale Dimensionen

… “ mehrsprachige

Themenseite der Rosa-Luxemburg-Stiftung


 und mehr darüber:


Internationale Konferenz vom 25. bis 27.09. in Bochum: Feministisch vergesellschaften – Her mit dem ganzen Leben! 


Die Internationale Konferenz ‚Feminist Futures II: Feministisch vergesellschaften – Her mit dem ganzen Leben!‘, vom 25. bis 27.09. an der RUB, möchte die Themen von Feminismus und Vergesellschaftung miteinander in Verbindung bringen. Siehe Informationen sogar auf mehreren Seiten:


https://www.rosalux.de/veranstaltung/es_detail/FL8C2

 


https://www.bo-alternativ.de/2026/08/03/feministisch-vergesellschaften-her-mit-dem-ganzen-leben/

 


https://care-revolution.org/termine/konferenz-feministisch-vergesellschaften-her-mit-dem-ganzen-leben

 


Von der Freiheit, füreinander da zu sein. Sorgende Städte: Was nötig ist, damit sich Menschen stressfrei um Kinder, Kranke und Alte kümmern können


„…

Das geschilderte Beispiel ist fiktiv. Allerdings sind Sorgende Städte längst nicht mehr nur eine Utopie. Vielmehr gibt es in vielen Städten bereits erste Schritte in diese Richtung. Damit die persönlichen Bedürfnisse und Erfahrungen von Menschen wie Anna zu ihrem Recht kommen können, braucht es strukturelle Bedingungen, die das ermöglichen. Konkret: Für eine bedürfnisorientierte Daseinsvorsorge ist die Vergesellschaftung von Sorge-Infrastrukturen nötig. Was ist damit gemeint? Es bedeutet, dass Infrastrukturen wie Kinderbetreuung oder Altenpflege kein privates, sondern öffentliches Eigentum sind und daher weder permanenten Sparzwängen noch der Profitlogik unterworfen werden – entsprechend wird die Arbeit dort auch gut entlohnt. Das bedeutet mehr als den Ausbau derzeit existierender Sozialsysteme. Denn in Annas Stadt werden diese Infrastrukturen außerdem demokratisch durch die Mitwirkung der Menschen vor Ort entwickelt und betrieben. Vergesellschaftung heißt also auch die gemeinsame Verfügung der Menschen über Gemeingüter des Lebens.


Vergesellschaftung von sozialer Infrastruktur hat aber noch einen dritten Aspekt: nämlich die Entprivatisierung der oft in der Isolation der Privathaushalte stattfindenden Sorgearbeit, die immer noch überwiegend von Frauen geleistet wird. Denn auch bei gut ausgestatteten öffentlichen Infrastrukturen werden große Teile von Sorgearbeit immer noch in Familien, WGs oder anderen sozialen Gefügen erbracht – und das ist auch gut so. Denn wenn sie von dem Druck, unter dem sie heute steht, entlastet ist, kann es etwas Schönes sein, sich umeinander zu kümmern.


Oft wird befürchtet, dass die Sorge um uns und unsere Liebsten zwangsweise in professionelle Einrichtungen übergehen muss. Das ist nicht gemeint. Wohl aber, dass gesellschaftliche Verantwortung übernommen wird, also auch Infrastrukturen geschaffen werden, die ins Zuhause hineinreichen, wie bei Anna, die ihren Vater in guten Händen weiß. Es geht um Angebote, die Sorgende und Umsorgte entlasten und sie mit ihren individuellen Bedürfnissen und Lebensmodellen in ein gesellschaftliches Netz einbetten. (…)


Tatsächlich ist ihre Geschichte längst nicht nur Utopie, sondern an vielen Orten der Welt teilweise gelebte Realität. Hier lohnt ein Blick auf ein konkretes Projekt aus Barcelona – die »Superblöcke«, die die Bewegungspartei Barcelona en Comú unter der feministischen Bürgermeisterin Ada Colau (2015–2023) in der Stadt entwickelt hat. Zunächst ging es dabei um verkehrsberuhigte Zonen, mit denen klimapolitische Ziele verfolgt und gleichzeitig öffentlicher Raum geschaffen wurde, damit sich die Nachbar*innen dort stressfrei …

author: TGEU
title: Trans Advocacy Network Meeting: Ten member representatives are invited to meet EU policymakers in Brussels.
content:
Selected participants will meet policymakers from the European Parliament and the European Commission. The programme includes one full day and approximately half a day of institutional meetings. 


Planned meetings include the LGBTI Intergroup, the Commissioner for Equality, the Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers, and supportive Members of the European Parliament. 


We aim to bring together participants from different parts of the EU, different organisational settings, racialised communities, gender identities and lived experiences, reflecting the full breadth of TGEU’s membership.


About the meeting


Date & time:

 9-11 November 2026


Location:

 Brussels


Cost:

 TGEU will organise and cover travel, accommodation, meals, local communication costs and transport within Brussels.

Language:

 The working language will be English. Unfortunately, interpretation will not be available.


Deadline to apply:

 4 October 2026, 23:59 CEST


apply here


We expect to inform applicants of the outcome by

13 October 2026

.


If you need the application form in another format or require support to complete it, please contact

farah@tgeu.org

.


Who can apply


Each organisation may nominate one participant. Applications must meet all of the following conditions:


• The organisation is a registered TGEU member.


• The organisation is based in a European Union Member State.


• The organisation has paid its membership fees or received a formal fee waiver.


• The nominated participant is available for the full meeting. This includes an introductory meeting during the week beginning 19 October, taking part in a substantive preparation meeting on 26 October and up to two further preparation sessions before the visit as well as the agreed work afterwards.


• The nominated participant has the travel documents required to travel to Belgium or can reasonably obtain them in time.


What we are looking for


Priority will be given to applicants who can demonstrate:


• Experience in advocacy at the local, national or regional level.


• Experience engaging with policymakers, public authorities, institutions, coalitions or relevant policy platforms.


• A clear understanding of key issues affecting the rights and wellbeing of trans people, such as asylum, gender equality, legal gender recognition, healthcare, housing, education or employment.


• Readiness to work with other selected members on shared messages, take an active role in meetings and contribute to the work arising from the meeting.


apply here


A note for members outside the European Union


We are sorry that this call is limited to member organisations based in European Union Member States. Unfortunately, the funding for this activity cannot support participation from outside the European Union on this occasion.


This restriction is not a reflection of the value of your work or your contribution to TGEU. We regret that we cannot accommodate a wider group for this meeting.


Your support makes change possible


We work across Europe and Central Asia to advance trans rights, build strong communities, and drive change through research, advocacy, and community-building.


Your donation helps us continue this vital work — defending trans lives, amplifying trans voices, and advocating for justice every day.

title: Συγκέντρωση – πορεία για την γυναικοκτονία στην Ηγουμενίτσα, Τρίτη 22/9, 19.00, στη πλατεία Δημαρχείου Ηγουμενίτσας
content:
“

Η ΠΑΤΡΙΑΡΧΙΑ ΔΟΛΟΦΟΝΕΙ ΚΑΙ Η ΚΟΙΝΩΝΙΑ ΕΘΕΛΟΤΥΦΛΕΙ

“


Τρίτη 22/9, 19.00, στη πλατεία Δημαρχείου Ηγουμενίτσας, κάλεσμα από τη Πρωτοβουλία Γυναικών Ηγουμενίτσας


Αφίσες/Καλέσματα:


Ποιοι θυμούνται σήμερα την Σούζαν από τα Γιάννενα, την Ελένη από την Ρόδο, την Κυριακή που δολοφονήθηκε μπροστά σε αστυνομικό τμήμα; Οι δεκάδες γυναικοκτονίες είναι κομμάτι μιας βαθιά αρρωστημένης πατριαρχικής κοινωνίας, όπου ο μέσος σεξιστής, γαλουχημένος με τα ιερά και τα όσια του αυθεντικού αρσενικού, θέτει τους όρους ύπαρξης για την κάθε γυναίκα που βρέθηκε στο δρόμο του. Όρους ζωής και θανάτου.


Για να επικρατήσει η ζωή και η πραγματική ελευθερία και χειραφέτηση υπάρχει κυρίως ένας όρος : η θανάτωση της πατριαρχίας.


Αύριο στις 7μμ θα είμαστε στην Ηγουμενίτσα, ανταποκρινόμενες-οι στο κάλεσμα της Πρωτοβουλίας Γυναικών Ηγουμενίτσας για την Πηνελόπη, ενάντια στον σεξισμό, την πατριαρχία και την παλιανθρωπιά που μεγαλώνει τέρατα, άνδρες της διπλανής πόρτας.


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


 


Αναρχική ομάδα,

A Batalha


Η ΠΑΤΡΙΑΡΧΙΑ ΔΟΛΟΦΟΝΕΙ ΚΑΙ Η ΚΟΙΝΩΝΙΑ ΕΘΕΛΟΤΥΦΛΕΙ


20 Σεπτεμβρίου 2026, η Πηνελόπη δολοφονείται στην Ηγουμενίτσα από τον πρώην σύντροφό της. Πρόσφατα προηγήθηκαν δύο ακόμη γυναικοκτονίες στα τέλη του Αυγούστου, με διαφορά τεσσάρων ημερών, η μία στη Νέα Σμύρνη και η δεύτερη στη Ροδόπη. Δολοφόνοι, και στις δύο περιπτώσεις, όχι κάποιοι άγνωστοι περαστικοί, αλλά κοντινά τους πρόσωπα που μέναν μαζί στο ίδιο σπίτι, οι σύντροφοί τους. Γυναίκες δολοφονημένες που την ίδια στιγμή πολλές βιώνουν στο σπίτι τους την έμφυλη βία. Πόσες ακόμη πρέπει να δολοφονηθούν για να αντιληφθούμε ότι κάτι πάει στραβά;


Οι γυναίκες αυτές δεν είναι απλά νούμερα σε μια στατιστική πίτα, αλλά άνθρωποι που έχασαν τις ζωές τους από την πατριαρχία. Ένα σύστημα που καθυποτάσσει τις γυναίκες και όσα άτομα δε χωρούν στην ετεροκανονικότητα του και κάνει τους άντρες να τις θεωρούν κατώτερες, ιδιοκτησία τους, που τους δίνει το δικαίωμα μέχρι και να τους αφαιρέσουν τη ζωή. Η ιδέα αυτής της δύναμης δε καλλιεργείται εν μια νυκτί, αλλά δουλεύεται συστηματικά από τη παιδική ηλικία. Οι γυναίκες μεγαλωμένες σε αυτό το περιβάλλον, πολλές φορές νιώθουν εκείνες υπεύθυνες για ό,τι συμβαίνει, αφού συμπεριφορές όπως η ζήλια, ο έλεγχος, η απομόνωση και η ανδρική επιθετικότητα κανονικοποιούνται από την κοινωνία, με αποτέλεσμα να είναι εγκλωβισμένες σε μια κακοποιητική συνθήκη, που μπορεί να οδηγήσει ακόμη και στην πιο ακραία μορφή της έμφυλης βίας, τη γυναικοκτονία.


Η συνθήκη όμως δεν είναι τωρινή, όπως αρέσκονται να λένε τα κανάλια. Συμβαίνει από τότε που η πατριαρχία όρισε τις σχέσεις των ανθρώπων, ενώ μόνη διαφορά με το παρελθόν είναι πως παλιότερα χρησιμοποιούσαν τον όρο “έγκλημα πάθους”. Το προφίλ του γυναικοκτόνου χτίζεται απευθείας, για να μπορέσουμε να αντιληφθούμε υποτίθεται τα κίνητρα του. Καλό παιδί, ήσυχο, δεν είχε δώσει ποτέ δικαιώματα άρα κάτι τον ώθησε σε αυτή την ενέργεια. Το αλκοόλ, το πάθος, ή οι δυσμενείς οικονομικές συνθήκες που βιώνουμε; Κανένα από αυτά δεν του όπλισε το χέρι, παρά η απόλυτη εξουσία που θεωρούσε ότι έχει πάνω στη σύντροφο του. Το φεμινιστικό κίνημα πολύ καιρό προσπαθεί να καθιερωθεί ο όρος γυναικοκτονία, ώστε να αναδεικνύεται η αιτία των δολοφονιών και πολεμώντας στη βάση να εξαλειφθεί.


Και τι κάνει το κράτος; Αυτό που έκανε πάντα· χρησιμοποιεί την πατριαρχία προς όφελος του για να μας διαχωρίσει με βάση το φύλο και τη σεξουαλικότητα. Από τους νόμους, τις δικαστικές αίθουσες, μέχρι τις καταγγελίες στα αστυνομικά τμήματα αποτρέπονται άτομα που έχουν δεχθεί κακοποιητική συμπεριφορά να την καταγγείλουν. Στην περίπτωση που είναι ρομά, μετανάστριες, τρανς και σεξεργάτριες τα πράγματα γίνονται ακόμη πιο δύσκολα. Από την απαξίωση της καταγγελίας μέχρι το δυσβάσταχτο κόστος της οικονομικής δίωξης, όλα αποτελούν αποτρεπτικούς παράγοντες για ένα άτομο να μιλήσει. Οπότε πέρα από το ζήτημα του φύλου, σημαντικό ρόλο παίζει και η ταξική θέση του ατόμου στη διαχείριση μιας καταγγελίας. Η κοινωνία από την άλλη, κάθε φορά δείχνει να σοκάρεται και μετά από λίγο θέτει ερωτήματα του τύπου “Γιατί δεν έφευγε τόσο καιρό;”, ξεπλένοντας τον κακοποιητή και ρίχνοντας ευθύνες στη γυναίκα που δέχθηκε την έμφυλη βία.


Και τι κάνουμε εν τέλει; Περιμένουμε μοιρολατρικά ποια θα είναι η επόμενη; Η απάντηση είναι ότι δε θα σταματήσουν να διαπράττονται γυναικοκτονίες, αν δεν αλλάξουμε ριζικά τις παγιωμένες πατριαρχικές αντιλήψεις της κοινωνίας. Μια αλλαγή που δε μπορεί να είναι μόνο ατομική αλλά και συλλογική, ώστε να μη …

author: dev
title: Contre le républicanisme LGBT+ : la normalité va craquer
content:
Ce qui devait arriver, arriva. Au seuil de la campagne présidentielle, le magazine gay

Têtu,

dans son numéro d'automne qui vient de paraître, offre une double-page au président du collectif Fiertés Citoyennes, Arnaud Abel, en livrant un portrait héroïsant le personnage et manipulant certaines vérités. Ce collectif est une émanation LGBT+ du Printemps Républicain qui n'est pas sans rappeler le rôle actuellement joué par le collectif

Nous Vivrons

 dans les rangs féministes. Sans compétence de terrain ni développement argumentatif très élaboré, le collectif a pourtant réussi à visibiliser ses discours autoritaires dans les médias ; outre Têtu, ils ont pu trouver des relais dans Marianne, Le Point ou encore CNews.


Dans cet article, paru initialement dans la revue

Trou Noir n°4

 en 2025 et légèrement actualisé

sur son substack

, Mickaël Tempête décrit la manière dont ces discours ancrent la normalisation gay dans un projet de militarisation des conduites minoritaires. Il en analyse non seulement les ressorts rhétoriques qui plaisent tant aux grands médias mais il historicise cette pensée policière en revenant sur le rôle joué par le Parti socialiste dans les années 1990 dans l'institutionnalisation des luttes LGBT+.


Alors, c'est quoi le républicanisme LGBT+ ?


1.

Dans la grande messe de normalisation des conduites, voilà qu'entre en scène les républicanistes LGBT, une bande de CSP+ drapée dans l'universalisme occidental, cette vieille lune dont la lumière blafarde éclaire surtout les couloirs des ministères et les visages des éditorialistes de salon. Une association en particulier, Fiertés Citoyennes, a retenu mon attention. Née des émois numériques et des indignations télévisées, elle n'a rien inventé. Elle recycle, à la manière de ses aînés du Printemps Républicain, la vieille rhétorique de la majorité silencieuse flouée par des minorités trop bruyantes, hystériques, idéologiques. Son Dieu ? La République façon De Gaulle au pays des Algériens. Ses prières favorites ? Le tweet cynique, la tribune outrée, la table-ronde entre amis. Tout se passe comme si Caroline Fourest, celle qui a déblayé le chemin, était en passe de devenir un modèle d'émancipation homosexuelle.


2.

 L'association trouve son origine dans la réaction à un triste fait divers survenu le 30 septembre 2021 : Yanis, 17 ans, subit insultes et tabassages par deux autres jeunes eux aussi mineurs dans un parc de Montgeron en Essonne, en raison de son orientation sexuelle supposée. Ce récit, qui aurait pu stagner longtemps dans l'indifférence générale, a été rendu viral par la circulation d'une vidéo de l'agression sur les réseaux sociaux et par le témoignage de la victime à l'émission de Cyril Hanouna sur C8. Arnaud Abel, fonctionnaire officiant dans les ministères et actuel président de Fiertés Citoyennes, trouve alors scandaleux que des militants de gauche s'inquiètent d'une lecture islamophobe de cette affaire où les coupables sont racisés. Il publie un tweet pour appeler celles et ceux qui ne se reconnaissent pas dans ce militantisme qu'il nomme « intersectionnel » et à créer un groupe. La rhétorique est en place, il s'agit d'opposer le militantisme LGBT+ à une supposée « majorité silencieuse » qui ne se sent pas représentée par elles. C'est ici que naît Fiertés Citoyennes : dans la maternité réactive et émotionnelle des réseaux sociaux. Et bien qu'elle ne soit qu'une association d'opinion sans aucune compétence de terrain, elle trouvera grâce aux yeux d'importants médias généralistes et LGBT+.


3.

À cet égard, Arnaud Abel définit ce qui va servir de paradigme au républicanisme LGBT : la gauche radicale nierait l'« homophobie endémique » qui sévirait dans « les banlieues et au-delà ».


4.

Le 27 octobre 2023,

Marianne

 publie la tribune de Fiertés Citoyennes qui la fera connaître du grand public sous le titre « LGBT pro-Hamas : autant dire les dindes qui votent pour Noël » dans laquelle le collectif s'en prend ouvertement aux actions en faveur du peuple palestinien par le militantisme queer révolutionnaire. Ils les qualifient de « chicken for KFC », les comparant ainsi à du bétail atteint du syndrome de Stockholm ne se rendant pas compte que leurs actions irréfléchies les mènent à l'abattoir islamiste.


5.

 Quelques mois plus tard, ils organisent une journée de tables rondes autour de la thématique « Universalisme et militantisme LGBT+ » dans la Mairie du 3

e
