author: C4SS
title: An Attack on Tech Freedom, an Assault on Dissent
content:
We live in a world of

surveillance states

,

militarized police

, and

crackdowns


on


dissent

. Meanwhile, corporate behemoths will often ally with the state to

shut down dissident speech

 or aid and abet

surveillance

. 


In this context, it’s important for independent groups to develop and maintain encrypted communications platforms and independent web hosting.


But the Trump administration recently

declared

 that an Italian tech collective is a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist” for doing exactly this. That Italian tech collective is Autistici/Inventati, which operates the independent web hosting service

NoBlogs

 along with other digital infrastructure projects for activists.


The State Department

claims

 that “Autistici/Inventati (A/I Collective) is an Italy-based extremist group that builds and operates the digital infrastructure for violent Antifa cells and other far-left militants across the world.”


That emphasis on

Antifa cells

 reflects the Trump administration’s ongoing attempt to crack down on dissent by demonizing “Antifa.” This has been the explicit aim of

NSPM-7

, and it has been central to prosecutions of anti-ICE activists, including the

Minneapolis 15

 and the

Prairieland defendants

.


In their obsessive desire to tie all leftist and anarchist dissent to “Antifa,” the Trump administration has made blatantly false claims. The State Department asserts: 


Oregon-based Rose City Antifa has relied on A/I Collective tools and services to organize and incite violent and criminal acts domestically, including an attack on Customs and Border Patrol helicopters that led to a federal indictment. Rose City Antifa also used A/I Collective tools and services to disseminate doxing lists and release illegally obtained personal information of Federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement, along with calls for targeted attacks on ICE agents in the streets and “in their homes.” 


However, as Torch Antifa Network

points out

, Rose City Antifa does not use A/I services and did not carry out these actions. Federal officials are instead referring to communications by Rose City Counter-Info, an entirely different group that does use A/I services. “Rose City” is a common nickname for Portland, Oregon. Not all groups that use this phrase in their name are identical. These outright falsehoods were credulously amplified by reporters at

Fox News

 and the

National Review

. 


Yet despite the incompetence this shows, designating A/I Collective as a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist” poses a very serious threat. As C4SS’s Technical Coordinator William Gillis

put it

, “This is a HUGE attack on basic free speech. Words completely fail me when addressing the potential loss to the anarchist movement of — as the US names it — 5,500 mailing lists, and 10,000 blogs.”


The State Department emphasizes users of the A/I Collective’s services that have allegedly committed crimes, including sabotage and terrorism. But many users are engaged in clearly First Amendment protected activities. These include anarchist bookfairs, antifascist researchers who study and expose far-right groups, the blog of a peer-reviewed academic journal, and an anarchist podcast and radio show. 


The “Specially Designated Global Terrorist” classification subjects Autistici/Inventati to sanctions. This means that purely based on a decree from the U.S. executive branch, anyone who engages in transactions with the A/I Collective becomes vulnerable to legal reprisal. As a result, the collective’s website has been

taken down

,

PayPal

 has blocked their account, and the Italian bank

Banca Etica

 plans to close their account. 


These sanctions have had a devastating effect on the A/I Collective. As

Sabot Media

reports

, “On September 6, eleven days after the United States placed the Italian technology collective on its terrorism sanctions list, A/I announced that the collective itself will close and that the email, blogging, hosting and communications services it has provided for a quarter century will soon be discontinued.” 


This is a chilling precedent. The executive branch can unilaterally declare that a provider of web hosting, email services, and other communications infrastructure is a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist.” By doing so, they can impose sanctions, and thereby destroy that provider. This can impose serious costs on speakers, organizers, and researchers that use the providers’ services. And …

President Donald Trump made his most openly genocidal threat yet to Iran on Tuesday, threatening to “annihilate” the country and its 92 million people with “no hope of survival.”

In his opening address to the UN General Assembly in New York City, Trump asserted again that he is facing a choice on Iran about whether to make a deal “that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country.”

“Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic, and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?” Trump said in his UN speech.

Trump has repeatedly made genocidal threats against Iran, prompting calls for impeachment and war crimes inquiries. These arresting remarks are especially alarming considering that Trump felt emboldened to make them at the highest-level gathering of world leaders, under the flag of an organization created after World War II with the mission of preventing global atrocities.

Human rights experts have previously said that Trump’s threats to wipe out Iran are genocidal. The UN’s Genocide Convention defines genocide as acts carried out “with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.”

Over the nearly seven months of his war on Iran, Trump’s genocidal threats have become commonplace. He has previously said that “a whole civilization will die tonight”; claimed numerous times that there “won’t be anything left” after he strikes the country; and, most recently, pontificated about “if and when do I blow the entire nation up?”

During his remarks at the UN, Trump said that Iran’s air force, navy, nuclear program, and defense equipment have been totally destroyed by the U.S – a dubious claim that he’s made since the first week of the war. He said that Iran’s government “slaughtered 72,000 of its citizens this year,” adding that “recently 10,000 were killed for protesting.”

It’s unclear what events Trump is referencing. Iranian human rights activists have recorded roughly 6,500 protesters killed in mass protests in December and January, far lower than Trump’s 72,000 figure. Many mass gatherings in Iran since then have cheered the government against the U.S. and Israel’s war of aggression.

A UN fact-finding mission also recently found that two U.S. strikes on Iran during the first day of the war were likely war crimes in violation of international laws of civilian protection.

After making his genocidal threat at the UN, Trump claimed “we will make a deal right after the election. It doesn’t make sense for them not to. They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election, what they don’t realize is I am not running.” He said that, once the war is over, oil prices “will come plummeting down even lower than they were at the start of the conflict.”

Analysts have said this claim attempts to manipulate voters amid the president’s record low approval ratings, driven in large part by the war and the affordability crisis that it’s worsened.

In his speech, Trump also threatened Cuba, saying that his administration is “seeking a fundamental change in the situation in Cuba,” where he said left-wing leaders have “spent decades coordinating with the left-wing radicals and communist networks here in the United States.”

title: Iraqi military delegation holds talks in Shengal
content:
A high-ranking Iraqi military delegation led by Chief of Staff Abdul Amir Rashid Yarallah traveled to Shengal on Tuesday. The delegation is expected to meet with representatives of the Yazidi community and military forces present in the region to discuss the security situation and the restructuring of security arrangements.


According to the Iraqi Ministry of Defense, the visit is intended to assess the security situation in Shengal and review the operational readiness of the forces stationed there. Yarallah also heads the high-level security commission established by the government.


The delegation also includes members of Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (Hashd al-Shaabi). According to multiple reports, meetings are planned with the military formations active in Shengal, including the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the Shengal Women’s Units (YJŞ). The talks will focus on the future security structure, the handover of weapons, and the integration of members of the units into state institutions.


The visit follows a decision by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi. Following a meeting with Yazidi organizations on September 11, he announced that the resistance units would hand over their weapons to the state. At the same time, he said that eligible members of the YBŞ and YJŞ could be integrated into Iraq’s official security institutions.


Al-Zaidi also ordered the formation of a high-level commission tasked with examining the security and humanitarian situation in Shengal, assessing the needs of the population, and developing proposals for further measures. Its mandate also includes determining the status of members of the resistance units, reconstruction, and creating the conditions necessary for displaced people to return.

title: Ferdinand Domela Nieuwenhuis - Staten och militarismen
content:
Författare

: Ferdinand Domela Nieuwenhuis

Titel

: Staten och militarismen

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #3 1917


 Staten kan icke existera utan militarismen. De som förklara sig mot militarismen men för staten ha därför icke allvarligt nog begrundat problemet. Dessa tvenne faktorer komplettera varandra.


 Vad är egentligen staten?


 Staten är, under alla sina olika former, ett instrument till förtryck, som den besittande klassen använder sig av för att hålla de besittningslösa i fattigdom och beroende.


 Ju mer man utvidgar statens makt, desto starkare är dess förtryck. Och under den senare tiden har statens makt betydligt ökats, trots alla sociala reformer. Den börda som pressar industriarbetarna (producenterna) har blivit betydligt tyngre. Och det är på dem det hela vilar. Om man tar ett samhälle på 5,000 personer, varav 1,000 producera, så underhålla dessa 1,000 arbetare de 5,000, vilket blir en producent på fem konsumenter.


 Man beräkner att i de europeiska staterna finns femton millioner män som äta ur statens krubba. De äro icke blott parasiter, men de hålla dessutom staternas öden i sina händer.


 Till denna klass hör kungarna, ministrarna, diplomaterna och generalerna, adeln och militärbefälet, alla funktionärer, de som sitta inne med de höga platserna inom industrien etc. För dessa äro kriget, även när det leder till ett nederlag, profitabelt, såväl materiellt som socialt.


 Man säger: det är just därför, som vi måste erövra statsmaskineriet för att göra det nyttigt för de besittningslösa. Tror ni på det?


 En maskin som gjorts för ett visst ändamål, kan icke benyttas till ett fullständigt motsatt ändamål. Allt det där pratet är därför bluff! Staten är en regeringsmaskin, en maktmaskin, och förutsätter alltid ett medel med vilket man kan böja de motvilliga. Den är således ett tvångsinstrument. Kalla det vad ni vill: polis, militarism, - det är sak samma, det är alltid makten som uppträder med våld. Staten är mänsklighetens mest öppna, mest skamliga och mest kompletta negation. Den bryter människornas internationella solidaritet och ersätter den med en begränsad, nationell sammanhållning, och detta just i syfte att förstöra, att erövra och underlägga sig den övriga delen.


 Det finns icke den grymhet, den våldsgärning, det helgerån, den falskhet, det bedrägeri, den nedriga sammansvärjning, den skamliga banditism, det fräcka tjuveri, det förräderi som icke har begåtts och fortfarande dagligen begås under täckmanteln av

statens intresse

.


 Machiavelli erkände det öppet.


 Ty hur betraktade staterna alltid folken? Som en livlös massa, som en för staten avlad köttmassa, tvungen att underkasta sig och betala, bestämd till en evig lydnad.


 Därför har staten behov av militarismen. Den kan icke leva och blomstra utan den. Det är således ett oförnuftigt företag, att bekämpa resultatet, utan att röra vid orsaken.


 Människorna ha blivit utestängda från sin naturliga egendom (jorden) vare sig medelst våld eller list. Och berövade alla arbetsmedel måste de sälja sina krafter och utlämna sig på nåd och onåd till de besittande. Därav kommer slaveriet för den stora massan. Ty vad är det karaktäristiska för slaveriet? Att man

arbetar för andra.

 Nå väl, den stora massan arbetar för andra. Den befinner sig i slaveri.


 Och vem beskyddar och upprätthåller detta tillstånd?


 Staten!


 Staten tjänar således kapitalismens intresse, ty från den får den liv och tillvaro.


 Militarismen utgör en integrerande beståndsdel i staten; man kan således icke klara sig utan den.


 Läs Krapotkins bok:

Den modärna staten

. Där skall man se: "Det är alltid en livlig önskan att få avsättningsmarknad för sina produkter och strävan efter att exploatera de efterblivna folken, som är orsaken till de modärna krigen. I Europa slåss man icke längre för monarkernas ära. Man kastar den ena arméen mot den andra för att skydda de mäktiga herrarna Rotchilds och Schneiders, det mycket aktade aktiebolaget d'Anzin, eller den mycket heliga katolska bankens i Rom inkomster. Kungarna räknas icke längre. Alla krig som förts i Europa sedan hundrafemtio år tillbaka ha varit krig för handelsintressen, för rätten till exploatering." I varje stat finns det en klick, en klass av män, ännu mäktigare än fabrikanterna, som söka nya avsättningsområden, nya källor till rikedom, och som tillskynda krigen. author: Sicilia Libertaria
title: Orizzonti di guerra e prospettive di lotta
content:
Corsa agli armamenti.


Orizzonti di guerra, parafrasando un celebre film, si potrebbe definire questo nostro tempo in cui i conflitti armati, agiti o minacciati, occupano lo spazio politico e mediatico e si presentano con una forza necessitante che non ammette discussioni o ripensamenti. Ma la guerra di per sé non è una novità, non è entrata in scena recentemente. La storia del XX secolo, per rimanere ad un periodo circoscritto, si è venuta svolgendo attraverso due tragicissime guerre mondiali, e anche il periodo successivo, quello della pace armata e delle armi nucleari come deterrente, ci ricordava già qualche decennio fa Eduardo Galeano in un suo straordinario libro –

A testa in giù. La scuola del mondo alla rovescia

– ha visto la morte di più di 20 milioni di persone a causa delle guerre. Dal 2001, data degli attentati alle Torri gemelle di New York, è entrata in scena la guerra permanente statunitense che si è dispiegata lungo vaste aree del pianeta contribuendo a creare quell’incertezza e quell’instabilità che appaiono i segni distintivi di questa epoca triste. Con lo scoppio del conflitto in Ucraina nel 2022 la guerra anche alle nostre latitudini è stata pienamente normalizzata, ricorrendo all’antico adagio del nemico, altro e irriducibile, da cui difendersi a tutti i costi. Così è ripartita una nuova corsa agli armamenti che vede protagonisti governi e parlamenti dei principali Stati a livello mondiale. Emblema di questa follia, come richiesto da Trump e fatto proprio da molti governi, è l’aumento del contributo alle spese della Nato fino al 5% del Pil. Corsa agli armamenti che, pur nella costanza dell’aumento delle spese militari degli ultimi decenni, si presenta oggi con una qualità differente, a causa di quella normalizzazione della guerra di cui si diceva. E così la guerra di fronte all’estrema instabilità che ci attraversa non è più un’ipotesi da scongiurare eventualmente con gli strumenti della diplomazia – che potevano “anche” fallire- ma una concreta e praticabile opzione. Una scelta legittimata già dal modo in cui vengono concepite le relazioni tra Stati e fatta diventare necessaria dalla propaganda mediatica.


Tuttavia

, oltre le particolarità di questa fase storica, le trasformazioni in atto nel sistema politico ed economico mondiale, le ragioni (o presunte tali) contingenti che hanno fatto scaturire i diversi conflitti in corso, da quello russo-ucraino, a quello in Iran, a Gaza, in Libano e ai tanti altri, persino dimenticati o poco spendibili sul piano mediatico, forse sarebbe opportuno svincolarsi dalle manifestazioni attuali della guerra, delle guerre, provando a penetrare più a fondo nelle dinamiche del sistema capitale-mondo, nelle sue perverse logiche di sopraffazione, di affarismo, e assumendo anche una posizione etica rispetto alla dominante realpolitik. Certo ci sono le famose cause delle guerre: economiche, politiche, di egemonia, culturali; a volte cause insospettate, addirittura poco convenienti da un punto di vista economico, come è avvenuto per l’imperialismo otto-novecentesco i cui risultati economici erano meno importanti della volontà d’imporsi che spingeva le potenze dell’epoca a impegnarsi in guerre dispendiose e senza senso (a proposito l’Italia ne sa qualcosa con le sue guerre coloniali, dall’Eritrea, alla Libia, alla Somalia, all’Etiopia). Figurarsi oggi se questa volontà di potenza non solletichi un Trump o un Putin! E c’è pure la geopolitica che ci spiega le relazioni tra gli Stati, come sia in corso uno scontro imperialista tra Stati Uniti e Cina, come bisognerebbe per l’Italia o l’Europa prendere parte a questa lotta e ritagliarsi uno spazio, adottando gli stessi strumenti e le stesse logiche della supremazia e del prevalere (leggere qualche numero di Limes per capire di cosa si sta parlando) e mentre ci spiega tutto questo la geopolitica ci suggerisce che oltre questo quadro dato non ci sono alternative, la realtà è questa e bisogna farci i conti.


Ma è sufficiente

 sapere di geopolitica, comprendere cause, contesti, motivazioni delle guerre, di quelle note e di quelle ignote, per far nascere forme reali, praticabili, incisive di opposizione alla guerra? Premesso che conosciamo e comprendiamo già (certo per chi vuole conoscere e comprendere) cause o origini dei conflitti del passato o del presente, il punto è che ciò non è sufficiente per spingere verso una concreta opposizione alla guerra. Anzi pare che oggi, e non solo per la guerra, più “conosciamo” e più …

author: Dr. Yvonne Würz
title: Indien: Helfen Sie Elefant Madhuri zurück in die Auffangstation
content:
Videoinhalt: © PETA India


Elefantendame

 Madhuri verbrachte jahrzehntelang angekettet und isoliert in einem Kloster (Matha) in Indien. Nach Bemühungen von PETA Indien wurde sie im Juli 2025 auf Anordnung eines Sonderausschusses des Obersten Gerichtshofs von Indien (High-Powered Committee, HPC) und des Obersten Gerichtshofs von Bombay aus ihrer tierquälerischen Haltung in das Elefanten-Rehabilitationszentrum Vantara gebracht. Dort erhielt sie tiermedizinische Versorgung, konnte erstmals Kontakt zu anderen Elefantinnen aufnehmen und begann, sich körperlich und psychisch zu erholen.  


Am 9. September 2026 ordnete das HPC jedoch an, dass die Elefantendame in dasselbe Kloster zurückkehren muss, in dem sie über Jahrzehnte unter den belastenden Haltungsbedingungen litt. 


Warum wurde Madhuri in die schlechte Haltung zurückgebracht? 

 


Dem Beschluss vom 9. September ging eine Kehrtwende Vantaras voraus. Die Organisation erklärte, Madhuris weiterer Aufenthalt in der Einrichtung liege nicht länger „im Interesse von Madhuri oder des Klosters“. Diese Kursänderung folgte einer Kampagne, die die Rückführung von Madhuri forderte und zum Boykott von Produkten aufrief, die mit dem Unternehmen hinter Vantara verbunden sind.  


Drei Monate vor der Entscheidung berichtete Vantaras Veterinärteam selbst, dass Madhuri mit schweren chronischen Erkrankungen angekommen sei. Die Folgen schlechter Haltung seien deutlich sichtbar gewesen, weshalb sie fortlaufend spezialisierte Behandlungen und regelmäßige Kontrollen benötige. 


Rückführung ins Kloster bedeutet enorme Risiken für Elefantendame Madhuri 

 


Während der jahrzehntelangen Haltung im Kloster war Madhuri gezwungen, fast regungslos auf Betonboden im Tempel zu leben. Dadurch hat sie irreversible gesundheitliche Schäden erlitten, darunter eine chronische Fußerkrankung und Arthritis. Die Rückführung birgt deshalb erhebliche Risiken für die Elefantendame. Sie benötigt weiterhin spezialisierte tiermedizinische Versorgung, die sie im Kloster nicht bekommen kann. Zudem hat sie nach 33 Jahren Isolation erstmals enge soziale Bindungen zu anderen Elefantinnen aufbauen können, die durch die Rückführung erneut zerstört wurden.  


Erst wenige Wochen zuvor hatten vom Sonderausschuss HPC eingesetzte Inspektoren das Kloster besucht. Ihr Fazit: Die Anlage sei für eine langfristige Haltung ungeeignet. Dennoch wurde Madhuri Mitte September 2026, nach nur 13 Monaten im Rehabilitationszentrum Vantara, wieder in den Tempel in Kolhapur überführt. 


PETA Indien setzt sich weiterhin dafür ein, dass Madhuri zurück in die Rehabilitationseinrichtung von Vantara gebracht wird.  


Fordern Sie jetzt Madhuris Rückkehr in die Auffangstation 

 


Elefantendame Madhuri musste zurück in eine Umgebung, die ihren Bedürfnissen als Wildtier niemals gerecht wird. Sie braucht dringend medizinische Versorgung, den Kontakt zu Artgenossen und die Möglichkeit, in einer geeigneten Umgebung zu leben. Unterstützen Sie deshalb PETA Indiens Petition und fordern Sie die Verantwortlichen auf, Madhuri dauerhaft in der Rehabilitationseinrichtung von Vantara unterzubringen. 


Jetzt Madhuri helfen (Weiterleitung auf PETA India)

author: webadmin
title: Quantock Hunt Members Charged
content:
At long last, charges have been issued against members of a stag hunt. 


Huntsman Martin Watts. Image Credit Mendip Hunt Sabs


Avon and Somerset Police have charged Quantock Staghounds hunt master Chris Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts with illegally hunting a wild mammal with dogs in relation to an incident on March 16, 2026.


Watts faces a further charge relating to a separate incident on April 23, 2026.


Both men are to appear in Taunton Magistrates’ Court on October 22, 2026 to answer the charges.


Hunt master Chris Gibbons. Image credit North Dorset Hunt Saboteurs


The charges follow what was, for a stag hunt, an ordinary day in March, when hunt saboteurs from Mendip Hunts Sabs and North Dorset Hunt Sabs were in attendance and recorded events as they unfolded.


The stag was first seen by sabs at around noon

. It would be almost six o’clock before the day was over and the stag was dead.


For more than five hours sabs documented the pursuit as the animal repeatedly fled. Quads, hunters on horseback, hounds and even motorbikes were involved as the stag attempted to escape.


It is difficult to comprehend what five hours of pursuit actually means for the animal. Deer are not endurance runners, prolonged exertion can cause severe physiological stress and overheating, and exhausted deer often enter rivers or streams during or following a pursuit.


The stag was pursued for over five-hours


Spring stag hunting takes place from early March until late April. Younger stags without the heavy antlers and greater body mass they develop later in the year, have historically been prized by stag hunters for the speed of the chase.


It is the pursuit itself, the flight of the wild animal turned into entertainment for bloodthirsty baying hunters.


Eventually after a gruelling five-hour pursuit the exhausted stag was trapped against a fence line with a sab on the other side.


The image of the stag was haunting. His jaw was bloodied and visibly deformed, his eyes bulging and blood pouring from his nose. His body was cut and gashed after hours of desperate flight across the landscape.


The haunting image of the stag moments before death, as a Mendip Hunt Sab begged for the animal to be left alone


What the sabs witnessed that day has left a mental scar, while the haunting video they managed to record has also stayed with many who have watched it.


As one sab desperately begged for the exhausted and injured stag to be left alone, hunters laughed as they raced past with the gun, demonstrating the stark contrast between the compassion of the sab pleading for mercy, and the barbarity of the hunters frothing and chewing at the bit to get their kill.


Soon after, the stag was dead.


Huntsman Martin Watts at the Quantock Staghounds’ closing meet 2026. Image Credit North Dorset Hunt Saboteurs


Watts’ second charge relates to an incident on April 23, 2026 during the Quantock Staghounds’ closing meet at Bagborough.


Hunting Act exemptions are subject to specific conditions, such as having permission to be on the land they are on.


The hunt was filmed by monitors from Wildlife Guardian hunting a young stag through Triscombe Quarry, a dangerous working quarry, which sabs say they had no permission to enter.


This time, unlike the stag pursued on March 16, he escaped alive. Eventually making his way into New Ground, a League Against Cruel Sport sanctuary.


The Quantock Staghounds are no strangers to seeing one of their huntsmen before the courts. Former QSH huntsman, Richard Down, was convicted in 2007 after

hunting a deer for more than an hour

. He was convicted again in 2010 for hunting a wild mammal with more than two dogs.


Down, who was still huntsman of the Quantock Staghounds at the time, became the first

huntsman to be convicted twice

 under the Hunting Act.


An HSA spokesperson said:


“These charges are a testament to the extraordinary dedication of the hunt saboteurs and monitors who spend countless hours in the field documenting what happens at stag hunts.


The Hunting Act must be strengthened to remove the exemptions, loopholes and excuses that hunts rely on to get away with the traditional hunting of wildlife with dogs.


This stag was chased for more than five-hours. We have been waiting 22 years for the law to catch up”.


You can support Mendip Hunt Sabs

here

 and North Dorset Hunt Sabs

here

.

Quantock Hunt Members Charged

 appeared first on

Hunt Saboteurs Association

title: Kutschpferde ohne Schutz: Vorstösse in Stadt, Kanton und Bund
content:
Anwohner:innen dokumentierten diesen Sommer in Interlaken

Kutschpferde im Dauereinsatz

: dasselbe Pferd um 14 und um 21 Uhr desselben Tages, bei 31 Grad. Das kantonale Veterinäramt erklärte zu einer Temperaturlimite, die Tierschutzgesetzgebung biete

«keine Grundlage für derartige Anordnungen»

. An dieser Lücke setzen die drei Vorstösse an.


Die

Tierschutzverordnung

 regelt, wie viel Bewegung ein Pferd mindestens braucht – nicht, wie lange es vor der Kutsche arbeiten darf. Hitzeschutz schreibt sie für Wasserbüffel, Yaks und Schweine vor, für Pferde im Geschirr fehlt jede Bestimmung. Die Motion von Nationalrätin Meret Schneider (Grüne) beauftragt den Bundesrat deshalb, die Verordnung zu ergänzen: mit einer Höchstdauer des täglichen Einsatzes und Ruhezeiten, Einsatzgrenzen bei Hitze und einem Fachkundenachweis für das gewerbliche Kutschieren.


«Die Tierschutzverordnung kennt Hitzeschutz für Wasserbüffel, Yaks und Schweine – nur für Pferde, die bei grosser Hitze Kutschen über den Asphalt ziehen, fehlt jede Regel», sagt Meret Schneider. «Diese Lücke kann der Bundesrat auf dem Verordnungsweg schliessen, ohne Gesetzesänderung.»


Wie gross die Risiken auch für Menschen sind, zeigte der

Unfall im Val Roseg

 vom 16. August: Die Bremsleistung einer Kutsche reichte nicht mehr aus, ein Pferd stürzte, das Fuhrwerk prallte gegen einen Baum. Eine 73-jährige Frau starb, zwölf Mitfahrende wurden verletzt. Wer ein Tierfuhrwerk lenkt, braucht nach Bundesrecht einzig das vollendete vierzehnte Altersjahr, eine Prüfung besteht nicht.


Im Grossen Rat verlangt Susanne Clauss (SP) mit der Interpellation «Hitzefrei für Kutschpferde?» Auskunft darüber, wie viele Pferde im Kanton Bern für gewerbliche Kutschfahrten eingesetzt werden, wie der Kanton kontrolliert und was aus den Meldungen aus der Bevölkerung wird.


«Verbindliche Regeln nehmen den sorgfältigen Betrieben nichts weg», sagt Susanne Clauss. «Sie stoppen die Betriebe, die ihr Pferd von Mittag bis Mitternacht durcharbeiten lassen.»


In der Stadt Bern fragt Tobias Sennhauser, Stadtrat von Tier im Fokus (TIF), welche Bewilligungen die Stadt für Kutschenbetriebe erteilt, welche Vorgaben für die Kutschenfahrten des städtischen Tierparks gelten und wie weit ihr Handlungsspielraum reicht – bis hin zu einem Verbot.


«Die Kutsche ist Unterhaltung auf Kosten der Tiere», sagt Tobias Sennhauser. «Wir wollen von der Stadt wissen, ob sie im 21. Jahrhundert daran festhalten will, Pferde zwischen Tram, Bussen und Menschenmengen einzuspannen.»


Andere Städte sind weiter:

Berlin

 lässt seit 2019 ab 30 Grad im Schatten keine Kutschfahrten mehr zu, Barcelona, Madrid und Málaga haben den gewerblichen Kutschenbetrieb ganz beendet.


Der Beitrag

Kutschpferde ohne Schutz: Vorstösse in Stadt, Kanton und Bund

 erschien zuerst auf

Tier im Fokus (TIF)

.

title: Chris Packham Joins Woman Living In Pig Crate During 21-Day Stand Against Factory Farming
content:
Wildlife presenter and former RSPCA president Chris Packham joined Michelle Farnham inside a pig farrowing crate outside the National Gallery today, where she has been living for over a week to highlight suffering on British factory farms.

Animal Rising campaign lead Michelle Farnham is living inside the crate 24 hours a day as part of a living art installation outside the National Gallery. She does not leave the crate at any point, day or night, from 1 to 22 September. [1]

Animal Rising campaign lead Michelle Farnham is living inside the crate 24 hours a day as part of a living art installation outside the National Gallery. She does not leave the crate at any point, day or night, from 1 to 22 September. [1]

Farrowing crates are still used in approximately 92% of indoor pig production systems, confining more than 200,000 mother pigs each year [2] - but Animal Rising says the crates are just one part of a much wider problem, and is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040.

Farrowing crates are still used in approximately 92% of indoor pig production systems, confining more than 200,000 mother pigs each year [2] - but Animal Rising says the crates are just one part of a much wider problem, and is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040.

The action follows Animal Rising’s release of hidden-camera footage documenting the life of Luna, a mother pig kept in a farrowing crate on a Suffolk factory farm. Over 19,000 people have now signed a petition calling for her release to sanctuary. [3] [4]

The action follows Animal Rising’s release of hidden-camera footage documenting the life of Luna, a mother pig kept in a farrowing crate on a Suffolk factory farm. Over 19,000 people have now signed a petition calling for her release to sanctuary. [3] [4]

Chris Packham joined Michelle in the crate today (09/09/26) on her ninth consecutive day living inside behind its bars in Trafalgar Square.

Animal Rising is now calling on the government to commit to the end of factory farming by 2040, arguing the scale of suffering in intensive farming systems can no longer be ignored.

Visiting today, Chris Packham said:

Packham stepped down as president of the RSPCA in December 2024 following Animal Rising investigations into RSPCA Assured farms and slaughterhouses, saying he had seen “no meaningful change” in response to the findings. [5] [6]

Michelle Farnham has spent years examining conditions inside British animal farms. She studied Animal Management for two years and has since reviewed hundreds of hours of undercover footage recorded inside UK pig farms, working alongside veterinary and animal welfare law experts to assess conditions, including during Animal Rising’s investigations into RSPCA Assured farms and slaughterhouses.

Farrowing crates can confine mother pigs for four to five weeks at a time around giving birth and nursing their piglets, leaving them unable to turn around or take more than a step forward or back. Sows are put through this cycle repeatedly, returning to the crates with successive litters until they are eventually culled.

Animal Rising released its investigation into Luna’s life last week, after documenting her for a month on a factory farm in Suffolk. Hidden-camera footage narrated by Michelle shows Luna giving birth and nursing her piglets while confined inside a farrowing crate, unable to turn around or freely interact with her piglets. Animal Rising is calling for Luna to be released to a sanctuary home that has been offered to her, alongside its wider call for the Government to commit to ending factory farming by 2040.

Over 19,000 people have signed the petition since Luna’s story was released.

Michelle and Animal Rising spokespeople are available for interviews and comment at the crate outside the National Gallery. Please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691 to arrange.

title: Devon And Somerset Staghounds Recreate The Horror Of The Barle Stag
content:
Thirty-two years on from the controversy of the Barle stag, the excuses may have changed, but for the hunted stag the suffering is horribly familiar.


More than three decades have passed since the death of the Barle stag became one of the most notorious episodes associated with stag hunting on Exmoor. Yet for those who witnessed what happened on Saturday 12th September 2026, the events along the River Barle carried disturbing echoes of the past – a past that, sadly, does not seem so very different from the present.


On Saturday, this magnificent stag was found quickly in the boggy woodland below Twitchen, and from there the pursuit began.


The stag was described as “a very fine up and coming stag” by a deer expert from Wildlife Guardian


A sab from North Dorset Hunt Saboteurs struggled to keep pace as the stag was chased across Molland Common and West Anstey Common. The stag crossed the road just moments before sabs arrived.


From there, the stag continued towards the River Barle at Mountsey Castle. It was there that sabs saw him bursting across a track in front of point riders and a quad bike before heading down and into the river.


By this stage the pursuit had clearly taken a terrible toll on the animal. Relays of hounds are typically deployed in pairs during stag hunting, allowing a pursuit to continue for hours. On this occasion the chase lasted around two hours before the stag was brought to bay.


Relays of pairs of hounds are used during the pursuit of the stag.


“At bay” is a hunting term to describe the point at which a hunted stag has stopped fleeing and turns to face his pursuers. It is often the culmination of an exhausting chase: an animal pushed to the point where escape is impossible, confronted by those pursuing him and facing what may come next.


The powerful wild animal who had crossed miles of difficult country was now struggling simply to continue. He was heaving for breath and, at one point appeared to be unable to even hold his head up properly. Instead of running, he was reduced to a slow walk.


And still the pursuit continued.


This is the image that cuts through the arguments used to defend stag hunting. Whatever terminology, smokescreen or justification is employed, it boils down to an exhausted, tormented animal desperately trying to keep moving.


The stag managed a final slow trot upstream before exhaustion overcomes him for the final time.


A sab entered the river after him, the Barle was shallow after a summer of drought. The river offered a moment of respite for the animal, he even managed a slow trot upstream, with the cooling water seeming to relieve him slightly, despite everything he had already endured.


A hound was also in the river, but appeared not to have picked up the scent. The sab continued to follow, the stones underfoot were slippery, making progress difficult while they also tried to protect their camera equipment and preserve the footage already recorded. The footage in stag hunting is important.


A small child was taking part in the obscene spectacle


Documenting is particularly important in stag hunting, because intervention at the final stages can be extraordinarily difficult.


During fox hunts, direct intervention by saboteurs can sometimes give a hunted animal the opportunity to escape. With an exhausted stag standing at bay, the situation is quite different.


On several occasions, sabs have managed to reach a stag standing at bay and position themselves close to the animal. Their presence may offer some protection for a limited period, but the stag is already frightened and exhausted.


Pressure continues and if the stag is frightened into moving again, even one final desperate burst can take him beyond the immediate protection of saboteurs.


If the stag cannot be saved, then at the very least what happens to him should not be hidden. People should be able to see what these animals endure and understand what the pursuit at the heart of this so-called “sport” actually looks like.


The hunts gunman, Shaun Kelloway, then dismounted from his horse, and carrying his gun, began following the stag on foot along the riverbank.


Gunman Shaun Kelloway dismounted, and carried his gun, before shooting the animal.


Sabs were hindered and obstructed by hunt supporters, while further ahead hounds could be heard being “hunted on”.


Yet despite everything – the woodland, the commons, the roads, the hills and finally the river, this extraordinary animal kept …

content:
Une enquête de L214 a filmé, en juillet et en août 2026, un élevage de canards de Barbarie de Sèvremoine (49) dont la viande est vendue sous la marque Carrefour Extra. Onze mille cinq cents oiseaux aquatiques y sont enfermés sur un caillebotis de plastique, sans litière, sans aucun dispositif leur permettant de plonger la tête dans l'eau. On les mutile pour qu'ils arrivent à survivre assez longtemps dans ces conditions ; Ils arrivent dans l'élevage le bec épointé. Leurs griffes sont coupées. Au ramassage, ils sont empoignés brutalement par le cou et balancés dans les caisses de transport.

Votre charte éthique fournisseurs engage pourtant chacun de vos fournisseurs à respecter les réglementations en matière de bien-être animal et à bannir les actes de cruauté envers les animaux.

Je vous demande d'écarter de vos rayons les produits de cet élevage et de tout élevage de canards conduit de la même façon. Et je vous demande de signer le Plant Protein Pact, pour réduire de moitié le nombre d'animaux tués pour vos approvisionnements d'ici 2030.

Ces images ont été filmées en juillet et en août 2026 dans un élevage de canards de Barbarie de Sèvremoine, dans le Maine-et-Loire. 11 500 oiseaux y sont enfermés dans un seul bâtiment fermé.

Les canards de Barbarie sont des oiseaux aquatiques de forêt marécageuse. Ici, ils vivent sur un caillebotis de plastique qui couvre toute la surface, sans un mètre carré de litière, avec environ 700 cm² pour chacun, à peine plus qu'une feuille A4. Pour toute eau, une pipette au-dessus d'une coupelle de quelques centimètres : rien qui permette de plonger, ne serait-ce que la tête.

Les canetons arrivent dans l'élevage le bec épointé. Ils ont aussi les griffes coupées. Les animaux ont le plumage souillé et les pattes couvertes de plaques brunes et croûteuses. Certains, pattes écartées, ne se déplacent plus par eux-mêmes. Des cadavres restent au sol parmi les vivants.

Au bout des 83 jours d'engraissement, les ramasseurs vident le bâtiment en une heure et demie. Les canards sont empoignés brutalement par le cou, plusieurs à la fois dans chaque main, puis balancés dans les caisses de transport, entassés les uns sur les autres.

Leur viande est vendue sous la marque Carrefour Extra. La comédienne Aure Atika, qui commente ces images, demande à l'enseigne d'écarter ces produits de ses rayons et de s'engager à signer le Plant Protein Pact.

title: Tırmanış cennetine siyanür gölgesi
content:
Eskişehir - Eskişehir Sivrihisar bölgesinde faaliyet gösteren Türk Altın İşletmeleri, Kaymaz altın ve gümüş madeni için yeni bir kapasite artış süreci başlatarak çevresel etki değerlendirme başvurusunda bulundu. Madenin açık ocak genişletmesi, flotasyon ünitesi ve ikinci atık depolama tesisinin büyütülmesini içeren proje, Karakaya köyü ile bölgenin en önemli doğa sporları merkezini doğrudan etkileyecek boyutlara ulaştı. Buna karşın hazırlanan ÇED dosyasında, her yıl binlerce sporcuyu ve kampçıyı ağırlayan Karakaya kayalıkları ile kamp alanının adının dahi anılmaması dikkat çekiyor.

Türk Altın İşletmelerinin hazırladığı kapasite artış projesi, bölgedeki maden sahasını devasa boyutlara taşıyor. Şirket, Çanakkale Karapınar ve Alpu Esence sahalarından taşıyacağı milyonlarca tonluk cevheri Kaymaz tesisinde işleyerek siyanürlü atık barajlarını genişletmeyi hedefliyor. Proje alanı Karakaya köyündeki en yakın yerleşim birimine yalnızca 1,2 kilometre mesafede yer alıyor. Maden atık depolama tesislerinin ve siyanürlü işlem sahalarının köye bu kadar yaklaşması, bölgede yaşayan vatandaşlar ile doğaseverler arasında derin bir kaygı yaratıyor.

Karakaya köyü sınırlarında yer alan granit kuleler, Türkiye'nin en popüler spor tırmanış ve kamp alanları arasında bulunuyor. Bölgede 240'tan fazla tırmanış rotası yer alıyor ve her yıl üniversite kulüpleri ile dağcılık dernekleri tarafından eğitimler, şenlikler ve kamplar düzenleniyor. Akasya koruluğuyla bozkırın ortasında doğal bir vaha niteliği taşıyan bu alan, bölgeye ekonomik ve sosyal açıdan büyük canlılık kazandırıyor. Ancak maden şirketinin sunduğu resmi ÇED dosyasında bu ulusal ölçekteki tırmanış bahçesinin, kamp ve mesire alanının varlığı tamamen görmezden geliniyor.

Kayalıkların önemini gizlemek adına perdeleme mi yapılıyor?

ÇED raporundaki bu büyük eksiklik, kamuoyunda ve çevre çevrelerinde bilinçli bir perdeleme şüphesini gündeme getiriyor. Çevre hassasiyet raporlarında alanın herhangi bir özel niteliği yokmuş gibi sunulması, maden ve atık sahalarının kayalıklara vereceği tahribatı gizleme amacı taşıdığı şeklinde yorumlanıyor.

Daha önce üçüncü atık barajı projesine karşı yürütülen hukuki mücadelelerde idare mahkemesi yürütmeyi durdurma ve iptal kararları verirken, süreç Danıştay aşamalarıyla devam ediyor. Siyanür sızıntısı, ağır metal kirliliği, toz ve gürültü tehlikesi altında kalan bölge halkı ve sivil toplum kuruluşları, doğa sporları alanlarını ve yaşam alanlarını korumak için mücadeleyi sürdürüyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Compares AI Warnings to Past Climate Fears He Wrongly Says Were a “Hoax”
content:
Millions of people have died as a direct result of the climate crisis.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump has dismissed legitimate concerns about the growth of artificial intelligence (AI), comparing them to the “hoax” of the climate crisis.

“The same people that said, ‘We’ll all be dead in twelve years because of Global Warming’ … are the people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us, that robots are going to attack us, and everything is a DISASTER,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

The president’s comments came a week after reports about the U.S. military nearly starting a war with China after relying on false information from AI, and after the world experienced its hottest month on record in August.

Trump also claimed that “nobody was dead” due to climate change, and compared AI concerns to the investigation into election interference by Russia during his first term in office, and his impeachment over withholding aid from Ukraine in order to get political “dirt” on Joe Biden, wrongly describing both of those situations as “a Hoax.”

In dismissing worries over the expansion of AI — which tech experts and developers themselves have said should be slowed down until proper safeguards are instituted — Trump made a false claim about the climate crisis: that no one has died from it.

In fact, millions of people around the world have lost their lives due to its impacts.

According to a Lancet Countdown report published last fall, which was authored by 128 experts from 71 different academic institutions, 546,000 deaths have occurred from heat exposure on average each year over the past decade. It also found that 84 percent of heatwave days in the past five years of data wouldn’t have happened without the effects of the climate crisis, and that droughts induced by the climate crisis have also led to 123.7 million more people experiencing food insecurity around the world than observed between 1981 and 2010.

“We’re seeing millions of deaths that are occurring needlessly every year because of our persistent fossil fuel dependence, because of our delay in mitigating climate change, and our delays in adaptation to the climate change that cannot be avoided,” said Marina Romanello, executive director of the Lancet Countdown at University College London.

Extreme weather events, which are becoming more numerous and severe due to climate change, have caused at least hundreds of thousands of deaths over the past 20 years.

“From 1995 to 2024, more than 832,000 lives were lost … driven by more than 9,700 extreme weather events,” reads an explainer from GermanWatch’s Climate Risk Index. “The frequency and intensity of climate-related disasters continue to rise, and these figures underscore the urgent need for climate action.”

A University of Wisconsin-Madison study published in 2022 found that eliminating air pollution from energy-related activities could reduce premature deaths in the U.S. by more than 53,000 annually. Put another way, by ending the country’s dependence on fossil fuels and shifting to renewable energy sources, the U.S. could save a number of lives nearly equivalent to the population of Madison every five years.

AI data centers will also worsen the climate crisis.

According to a 2015 analysis from Cornell University researchers, by 2030, the current rate of AI growth will add 24 to 44 million metric tons of carbon dioxide to the atmosphere every year. That amount is equal to 5 to 10 million cars added to U.S. roads annually. Water usage to cool these data centers would also equal the annual household usage of 6 to 10 million Americans per year.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Greta Thunberg Is Taking Sweden to Court Over Climate Crisis Again
content:
Greta Thunberg and Swedish youth climate organisation Aurora are suing the Swedish government over its failures to tackle the climate crisis.


While Sweden has reduced its greenhouse gas emissions at a rate faster than the EU average, the country is

not on track

 to meet its own target of net zero by 2045.  


Thunberg said on Monday that Aurora has filed a second

 lawsuit

, arguing that Sweden is failing in its legal duty to protect its citizens – especially children and the young – from the effects of climate change.


The group is demanding that Sweden take action to limit global warming to 1.5C by cutting emissions and protecting ecosystems like forests. A third demand involves accounting for emissions that it says are currently excluded from government calculations such as burning imported biomass.


“Sweden, as a rich country with high historical and current emissions, has a legal duty to lead the climate transition,”

the group wrote in its fundraiser

. “A safe and just world is still possible, but only if rich, high-emitting states like Sweden stop violating their duty to protect people from the devastation of the climate crisis, and start transforming their societies before 2030.” 


Thunberg and Aurora’s first attempt to sue Sweden into taking stronger action against climate change was

quashed in February

, when the country’s supreme court decreed it could not force the government to take action. 


However, the Swedish court did not rule out that a differently formulated claim might have better success. In 2024, the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR)

said

 that citizens can sue governments that fail to tackle climate change, on the grounds that their right to a private and family life could be violated by climate breakdown. 


Civil groups have successfully sued their governments in the

Netherlands

,

Belgium

,

Germany

 and

Switzerland

, forcing them to take more drastic measures to protect the environment. 


Thunberg and campaigners at Aurora have so far

raised more than £180k

 to fund their forthcoming lawsuit.

author: Unknown
title: Merve Asya Özgür: If Kurdish artists are free, Turkish artists also gain - Part Two
content:
Actress Merve Asya Özgür, one of the lead actresses in Pelin Esmer’s latest film And the Rest Will Follow, in which she plays the character Aliye, spoke to ANF about the relationship between art and peace.


Part one of this interview can be read

here

.


You seem to be saying that artists need freedom in order to find the courage to speak. Wouldn’t positive progress in this process help create that freedom?


We were quite critical of the artistic community earlier, but there are also people who genuinely have something to say and cannot express it because of the pressure they face. There is, first of all, a major problem of censorship. These conditions inevitably create their own artistic language. People often say, ‘Art somehow finds a way and creates a new form.’ There is some truth in that, of course. But repression and the inability to speak under that pressure eventually turn into a collective silence, beginning with the self-censorship of those who would otherwise speak out. Then a new generation emerges within that collective silence. They enter the creative process, quietly settle into a corner and fall into line with that silence. The spiral of silence expands to include the new generation, while subdued forms of artistic expression remain trapped within the same vicious cycle.


You know how popular movements are often discussed: repression creates an accumulation of discontent within people, makes contradictions visible and awakens feelings of resistance. Anger grows and accumulates until, eventually, it develops into a mass movement. There is often such an expectation in periods when conditions are particularly harsh. That accumulation can, of course, also help movements mature.


But if you look at the history of struggles, radical changes have generally taken place during more moderate periods. Change occurs in an environment where people still have some room to breathe and act, where everything has not yet become completely blocked and entrenched. So if we approach this issue with the hope that a more moderate and democratic atmosphere can emerge, then the silence I mentioned earlier will naturally begin to evolve into something different. People may find the courage to say something new rather than simply repeating the same words in muted voices.


It is quite clear. Artists in the west of the country who have acted as though an issue that has been visible in this region for years simply did not exist may perhaps turn and look at it. Maybe it will become popular; I don’t know. Something that becomes popular can suddenly have a completely different impact and acquire a certain appeal. People want to gravitate towards it. In my view, we should not separate art from the conditions in which it is produced and place it on some idealised pedestal. Art is something created by people; it is a way of seeing. It is influenced by circumstances, its surroundings and the political climate, and it takes shape accordingly. If the more moderate environment we are talking about can be created, I imagine such tendencies will emerge.


We always talk about the artist’s responsibility towards society and their role in ‘showing the way’. But how are artists themselves nourished by society, and what do they learn from it?


Everything an artist knows, sees and creates, everything that nourishes their creative work, comes from society, from the people who make up the society into which they are born and first open their eyes. Even our sense of self is established through another person, through the existence of someone else. I can only be me because I am not you, isn’t that so?


Ultimately, it is society that shapes your entire world of images. Its culture, its stories, the richness of its language, the pain behind it, its folk songs and dances… All this accumulated heritage, the conflicts within it, the political tensions, everything shapes people and the way they live. You grow up within it. You speak its language and try to tell something through that language. Everything from the words you use and the way you think to the laughter and humorous traits of the characters you portray or create comes from the society in which you live. Which sections of society all that we take is ultimately given back to is another, rather neglected question. 


Unfortunately, the art world in Turkey often operates within a closed circle. Under these economic conditions, people are already struggling simply to get through everyday …

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: News in pictures | US-wide campaign against Pax Silica launched
content:
NEW YORK – From the belly of the beast, resistance to the U.S.-initiated Pax Silica is rising.

The U.S.-wide launch of the Shut Down Pax Silica Campaign Network happened on Sunday, September 20 with over 500 people attending in New York City, online, and in watch parties all over the country. Convened by the International League of Peoples’ Struggle-US (ILPS-US), Bagong Alyansang Makabayan USA (BAYAN USA), and International Coalition for Human Rights in the Philippines-US (ICHRP-US), the network consists of 45 organizations who opposed the Pax Silica over impacts on environmental destruction and exploitation of the poor in other countries.

Speakers from Agham, Friends of the Congo, Countermapping Network PH, and Nodutdol shared about the impacts of AI and tech supply chains around the world, and the global threat of Pax Silica, with the Philippines as “ground zero” for the Initiative.

This event marked the beginning of the week of action at the UN General Assembly with the banner “No to War and Plunder, Fight for Peoples’ Rights, National Sovereignty, and Genuine Development.” (RVO)

author: Alfredo Seguel
title: Defensoras del agua en la Patagonia: La resistencia mapuche ante la expansión de data centers de IA en Argentina
content:
Mujeres mapuche en la Patagonia argentina (Puelmapu), resisten la expansión de data centers de inteligencia artificial que amenazan reservas de agua golpeadas por sequías, minería y fracking. Denuncian falta de regulación, el Súper RIGI y el proyecto Atlas GigaHub en Chubut. Llaman a defender los territorios bajo el concepto de “terricidio”, destacó un reciente reportaje de WIRED .


Guardianas mapuche resisten los data centers de IA en la Patagonia


La weychafe (“guerrera” en mapudungun) Moira Millán vive a orillas del río Corcovado, en la provincia argentina de Chubut, desde su hogar en el Lof Pillán Mahuiza.

Según recogió WIRED en un reportaje


de Ella Fernández publicado el 3 de septiembre de 2026, Millán habla del agua pura y libre, el ko, que recorre las venas del territorio Puelwillimapu en forma de ríos que no solo alimentan las cosechas y los animales, sino que son fuente de vida. “En el color del agua se puede leer el estado del alma”, dice la weychafe.


Ver también / “Los pueblos originarios hemos vivido la violencia sistemática por defender la vida y la naturaleza”: Onésima Lienqueo, candidata mapuche a Escazú


En la cosmovisión mapuche, cada elemento de la naturaleza tiene un newen, una fuerza vital. Nada puede extraerse sin pedir permiso, porque el ser humano —el che— no es dueño de la tierra, sino una parte más de un sistema interconectado. “¿Cómo es la vida cuando no tenés agua? “, pregunta Nélida Askalipe, de la comunidad Nahuelpan, en Chubut. “Salimos y sostenemos las luchas porque sabemos todas las consecuencias de la destrucción de la tierra, como si fueran nuestros cuerpos”, añade Askalipe, según WIRED .


El costo invisible de la IA


A inicios de junio, el presidente Javier Milei publicó una nota de opinión en el Financial Times titulada “Argentina invites AI to free itself”. “Con el mismo espíritu de los comerciantes holandeses que convirtieron a Ámsterdam en la capital financiera del siglo XVII, buscamos ofrecer el entorno legal y fiscal más atractivo para las empresas de Inteligencia Artificial que definirán el siglo XXI”, escribió. “La IA nos liberará de las limitaciones del cerebro humano, impulsando la productividad más allá de lo imaginable”.


Jessica Gentile, coordinadora del colectivo Red Ecosocialista , integra el texto de Milei dentro de una serie de decisiones estratégicas para “facilitar a los barones de Silicon Valley una arquitectura legal y económica” y “entregar la Patagonia —una de las reservas más importantes de agua y gas del mundo— a esta nueva infraestructura”. Entre los magnates se menciona a Peter Thiel, fundador de Palantir Technologies, quien recientemente reubicó su residencia en Argentina. En junio de 2026, el Gobierno presentó el Súper RIGI , una ampliación del RIGI orientada a megacentros de datos para IA, que ofrece arancel cero para importaciones y estabilidad tributaria por 30 años, según WIRED .


Danila Suárez Tomé, docente e investigadora del Instituto de Investigaciones Filosóficas (SADAF/CONICET) , cuestiona el relato que asocia la expansión de la IA con el progreso: “Los data centers usan mucha energía eléctrica y volúmenes gigantescos de agua dulce para refrigerar los equipos y evitar que colapsen por el calor. Esto puede agudizar el estrés hídrico de las zonas de instalación y hacer que el enfriamiento de los servidores termine siendo prioridad por sobre el derecho al agua de las comunidades y las economías regionales”. La Agencia Internacional de Energía calculó que en 2023 los data centers consumieron unos 560,000 millones de litros de agua a nivel global.


La Patagonia en emergencia hídrica


El norte de la Patagonia enfrenta desde hace al menos 15 años períodos de estrés hídrico, en territorios atravesados por décadas de conflictos por megaminería y explotación petrolera. Neuquén prorrogó la Emergencia Agraria por sequía hasta fines de 2026, con caudales en mínimos históricos. Río Negro hizo lo propio en enero de 2026. En agosto de 2026 , la Legislatura de Chubut declaró la emergencia hídrica por un año. Un mes antes, el gobernador Ignacio Torres anunció la instalación de un data center en la Zona Franca de Trelew junto a la empresa polaca Green Capital . El proyecto Atlas GigaHub , previsto para 2027, contempla aproximadamente 3,000 MW de capacidad y 10,000 MW de generación renovable, pero su demanda de agua no ha sido especificada, según consignó WIRED .


El vacío legal

author: Comunizar
title: Comuna y Estado: experiencias de resistencia colectiva en Kurdistán y México
content:
Diego Laurenti Sellers y Amara Ayney

Öcalan


Introducción


Quienes luchan en contra de las injusticias del capitalismo conocen bien la represión del Estado, que habla en nombre del Pueblo al mismo tiempo que defiende los intereses de la burguesía. El Estado-nación moderno “es el instrumento político actual del capitalismo” (Aslan, 2023), incompatible con los valores de una sociedad plural, incluyente y políticamente activa (Öcalan, 2024). Bajo el formato de la democracia representativa, este concentra los mecanismos formales de toma de decisiones en mano de representantes, sometiendo a la mayoría de las personas a un sistema de explotación que las obliga a vender su fuerza de trabajo para sobrevivir. La amenaza constante de represión y marginalización- sea de forma explícita con la cárcel y las desapariciones forzadas, o de forma indirecta a través del hambre y de la miseria- permiten a la clase capitalista apropiarse de la labor humana y de sus frutos.


Aun así, la humanidad ha logrado mantener viva la esperanza de un mundo diferente, alimentada por actos cotidianos de solidaridad que se escapan a la lógica del capital, desde las redes familiares o comunitarias de cuidado mutuo hasta las prácticas colectivas de toma de decisiones y gestión colectiva de los recursos comunes. En momentos de rebelión abierta, estas prácticas colectivas toman un sentido político más explícito, cuando son utilizadas para gestionar territorios más grandes, arrancados al control del Estado y del sistema de producción capitalista. Por ejemplo, cuando los Pueblos de la región cholulteca en México tomaron las instalaciones de la embotelladora de agua de Bonafont en 2021, sellaron los pozos, frenaron la producción y las transformaron en un espacio de lucha gestionado colectivamente. A pesar de autodefinirse con nombres diferentes, este tipo de acciones-espacios-relaciones comunitarias se pueden analizar a partir del concepto de

comuna

. La mayoría de las comunas que se han generado durante los años tuvieron un fin violento, pero marcaron la conciencia popular, porque donde hubo huerto, semillas quedan.


Las luchas populares que hoy se enfrentan con el capitalismo neoliberal y con un sistema de gobierno eufemísticamente llamado “democracia” son herederas de luchas mucho más antiguas, que durante milenios han resistido a los procesos de dominación de las masas por parte de quienes pretenden someterlas a la tiranía de unos pocos (Öcalan, 2024). Tanto el Pueblo Kurdo en Mesopotamia como los Pueblos Indígenas en México han logrado mantener sus redes comunitarias tradicionales ante los procesos que favorecen su fragmentación, y siguen construyendo comunidad a partir de luchas que apuntan no sólo a preservar su autonomía, sino a destruir todo aquello que la amenaza. Estas luchas han inspirado a otros Pueblos en otras geografías porque tienen una propuesta concreta, a partir de un modelo heterogéneo de sociedad plural libre de explotación, sea laboral, sexual o de la naturaleza. Rompiendo con la visión lineal de la historia que ve a la comunalidad rural como “primitiva” y a la especialización jerárquica del Estado como “avanzada”, las comunas representan una forma de interactuar más sostenible, incluyente y

democrática

1

.


Durante el último medio siglo bajo el capitalismo neoliberal, muchos Estados han cedido al sector privado el control de servicios públicos como la educación, la salud pública, los transportes y los medios de comunicación, así como la propiedad de bienes comunes como bosques, praderas, agua y conocimiento. Como explica la sexta declaración de la Selva Lacandona, del Ejército Zapatista de la Liberación Nacional (EZLN):


El capitalismo todo lo convierte en mercancías, hace mercancías a las personas, a la naturaleza, a la cultura, a la historia, a la conciencia. Según el capitalismo, todo se tiene que poder comprar y vender. (EZLN, 2005)


Ante esta grave emergencia para los bienes comunes y para las condiciones de vida de la gente, hay partidos políticos que buscan la solución a través del fortalecimiento del Estado, tanto desde el progresismo como en la “cuarta transformación” (4T) en México, como desde la derecha xenófoba como en “Make America Great Again” (MAGA) en los Estados Unidos. Estas propuestas se basan en la ilusión de que el Estado cuida los intereses de la ciudadanía, cuando en realidad favorece las empresas que son las mismas que lo financian. En contraste con esta promesa “desde arriba”, existen propuestas …

author: Petala Ironcloud
title: Big Tech Is Trampling Native Treaty Rights to Build Data Centers
content:
Tribal consultation isn’t optional, but the corporations building data centers in New Mexico are acting like it is.

Tribal consultation isn’t optional, but the corporations building data centers in New Mexico are acting like it is.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

In 2004, Microsoft’s future chief sustainability officer, Melanie Nakagawa, co-edited a law journal issue on Indigenous peoples’ right to prior informed consent. This month, as a data center developer routed around exactly that standard in New Mexico, she didn’t answer whether it applies to her own company’s work.

Ask Google, Amazon, and Microsoft whether they consult Native nations before building a data center, and you’ll get the same answer: silence dressed up as sustainability commitment — as if the law here were unsettled, rather than two centuries old. Chief sustainability officers operate by ESG (environment, sustainability, governance) principles that imply tribal consultation, typically executed either to pacify objecting community members or to comply with an environmental review process. ESG reports are meant to define a company’s community impact but instead serve as shields for deals structured to sidestep responsibility.

Project Jupiter, a 1,400-acre Oracle and OpenAI hyperscale data center under development in Santa Teresa, New Mexico, is leased by these tech titans from BorderPlex and Stack: two companies handling physical infrastructure, simultaneously distancing the lessees from responsibility for their environmental and tribal impacts.

ESG (environment, sustainability, governance) reports are meant to define a company’s community impact but instead serve as shields for deals structured to sidestep responsibility.

On August 23, the New Mexico Supreme Court temporarily halted construction for air quality review and ordered a state engineer to diminish water use. Oracle has forecast its use of 11 million gallons of water for an initial fill, plus roughly 168,000 gallons per year in ongoing maintenance. Sen. Melanie Stansbury has separately put the figure at “over a million gallons a day” — a gap neither company nor state officials have reconciled. Lisa Henne, general counsel for the Interstate Stream Commission, told Truthout the water used for construction is purchased from an existing water right holder, not a new appropriation, and that New Mexico’s Pueblos — all located upstream of Elephant Butte Reservoir — aren’t affected, since Jupiter sits in the Lower Rio Grande, a separate hydrological zone.

That leaves an open question: Ysleta del Sur Pueblo, based across the state line in Texas, sits in the same Lower Rio Grande stretch, closer to the site than any New Mexico Pueblo. Asked whether the Commission had been in contact with the Pueblo, Henne confirmed it had not. She added, though, that the Commission “would not expect” the project to affect it, based on the same reasoning she applied to New Mexico’s own Pueblos. In other words: no contact, but a conclusion about impact reached anyway.

Even that thin standard assumes someone’s title implies responsibility. OpenAI has no chief sustainability officer at all. The closest approximation would have been the company’s Head of Data Centers Chris Malone, who just left the company in August amid a wave of executive departures, leaving infrastructure decisions split across engineers with no explicitly named party responsible for considering environmental or community impact.

Zephyr Jaramillo of Isleta Pueblo, speaking for Youth United for Climate Crisis Action at the Santa Fe County hearing, put it plainly: “Communities are already considering considerable harm … We look forward to engaging with communities throughout this process.” Whether that engagement extends to Project Jupiter and the Pueblos with senior water rights along its stretch of the Rio Grande, remains an open question that no one — not Oracle, not OpenAI, and not the state — has yet answered.

Amazon is the sole data center builder that appears to uphold a minimal standard of tribal consultation. Teara Farrow Ferman, the program manager for the Department of Natural Resources’ Cultural Protection Program, says, since 2019, the company has held monthly meetings with the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation (CTUIR), signing a memorandum of understanding with the tribes in 2023, and …

author: Unknown
title: Pourquoi et comment brûler la psychiatrie ? Discussion pour des perspectives antipsy anticarcérales
content:
Le mercredi 23 septembre 2026, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs organise une discussion antipsychiatrie anticarcérale à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

, qui se trouve à la Parole Errante à Montreuil.


Mercredi 23 Septembre à 18h : Discussion antipsy anticarcérale à la

BARK

 

!


Depuis son lancement, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs s'efforce de s'organiser contre l'enfermement psychiatrique. La psychiatrie nous apparaît naturellement comme un maillon important de la domination : que ce soit par les moyens par lesquels elle enferme des personnes, par son utilisation répressive et pacificatrice dans les autres lieux d'enfermement, ou par ses dispositifs carcéraux de contrôle dans la société. Dans une optique de s'informer sur les luttes contre la psychiatrie et d'y intervenir, on veut prendre en compte le fait que nous n'avons pas toustes les mêmes expériences et connaissances sur le sujet.


L'idée de cette discussion est donc de poser des bases, ensemble, sur ce qu'est l'antipsy pour nous, que ce soit pour découvrir ses courants ou pour développer ce qui nous parle dedans. Quels sont les dispositifs d'enfermement de la psychiatrie

 

? Pourquoi viser à sa destruction

 

? Quels liens faisons-nous depuis nos perspectives anticarcérales

 

? Comment la domination psychiatrique est elle étendue ces dernières années

 

? Comment s'organiser pour la brûler

 

?


Une base d'infokiosque sera aussi proposée pour approfondir certaines questions spécifiques, mais il ne faut pas hésiter à apporter toute brochure que l'on voudrait discuter, conseiller, diffuser, etc.


La discussion commencera dès 18h à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

 (5 rue francois debergue à la Parole Errante à Montreuil, en passant par le jardin à gauche de la librairie Michèle Firk). La permanence de la bibliothèque commence elle dès 16h, et l'infokiosque y sera installé en avance

 

!

author: Rana Mamdouh
title: Future of Egypt enters healthcare: Govt, military hospitals to serve tourist dollars
content:
In its first public move into the healthcare sector, the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority

unveiled

 last week the launch of the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company.


According to reports announcing the authority’s participation in this year’s Egy Health Exhibition and Conference, the company is chaired by Major General Khaled Oweida, the physician and former director of the Air Force Specialized Hospital, and is set to provide specialized medical services, training and research, digital and technological healthcare solutions, as well as medical tourism services.


In the first phase of its operations, the reports stated, the company will incorporate the International Medical Center and the Air Force Specialized Hospital, both of which are affiliated with the Armed Forces. The two facilities provide medical services to military personnel through the Armed Forces’ health insurance system, while also treating civilians for a fee or through

contracts

 with the Universal Health Insurance system or other entities.


The company plans to expand gradually by bringing additional facilities and hospitals under its umbrella.


This year’s Egy Health Exhibition and Conference, held September 15-17. Courtesy: Menassat website


Future of Egypt

also announced

 that the company was taking part in the exhibition, which was held from September 15 to 17, in order to “showcase its integrated medical system’s components and the range of specialties, services and advanced solutions it offers.”


Coverage of the exhibition focused on what media outlets described as the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company’s vision for developing medical tourism — mapping the international patient journey that runs from pre-travel consultations and case assessment, through travel, reception, accommodation and translation, to post-treatment follow-up.


According to media

coverage

, the company intends to pursue this by building a network of medical partners and tourism operators and establishing cooperation channels with entities involved in medical tourism and target markets.


Steps to foster a state vision for medical tourism date back to at least 2017, when Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly

established

 the Supreme Committee for Medical Tourism by decree to be headed by the health minister. The decree set out several objectives, including implementing the medical tourism components of the Egypt Vision 2030, restoring the confidence of foreign patients, attracting Arab and foreign investment to establish projects serving medical tourism and involving civil society and the private sector.


During a committee meeting in December 2024, chaired by Madbuly, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar

said

 the committee’s technical secretariat had begun preparing a unified national strategy for medical tourism. According to a Cabinet

statement

, the committee had contacted all relevant entities involved in health tourism in Egypt to solicit their proposals for the strategy.


At the same meeting, Madbuly said that it was agreed to establish a national council for medical tourism, with a technical secretariat tasked with following up on all matters related to this portfolio.


The council was established by a prime ministerial decree in June 2025. In its first meeting,

chaired

by the health minister, a proposal setting out criteria for service providers to join the national health tourism platform was reviewed. The providers included healthcare, hotel and hospitality, transportation and logistics services.


A senior Health Ministry official told Mada Masr on condition of anonymity that the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company is primarily focused on providing treatment to tourists: “[The company] is targeting Gulf nationals and foreign tourists in Egypt whose treatment costs are paid in dollars by international insurance companies.”


As an example, the official said, “if we perform open heart surgery for LE200,000 for someone insured in Egypt, [Future of Egypt’s] hospitals would perform the same operation for a foreign tourist staying in, say, Sharm el-Sheikh, and their insurance company would pay US$10,000. And we benefit from the difference in the exchange rate.”


According to the official, one of the main criteria for selecting hospitals to be transferred to Future of Egypt is having a helipad equipped to receive emergency cases, as well as facilities equipped for major surgeries and subspeciality medical care …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Warren Introduces Bill to Ban Private Equity From Owning Medical Practices
content:
More than 80 percent of doctors are employed by corporate entities — a massive increase from 62 percent seven years ago.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

A group of Democrats has introduced bicameral legislation to ban private equity from owning medical practices as increasingly widespread corporate ownership continues driving up health care costs each year.

The bill was introduced Wednesday by Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts) with the support of 12 other members of the Senate and House. The legislation was based on a law in Oregon aimed at beating back the corporate takeover of health care providers that took effect this year. The law has already been successfully used by physicians in Eugene to prevent a corporate takeover.

Warren’s bill would ban for-profit corporations like private equity funds and insurance companies from owning medical practices, while also prohibiting entities known as management services organizations, which conduct business operations for practices, from controlling such offices.

Such a prohibition could help stanch the rapid rise in health care costs. Between 2000 and 2004, KFF found, costs for medical care far outpaced costs for goods and services at large, increasing by 121 percent compared to 86 percent for the rest of the consumer price index.

The growing grip of private equity on health care, like in other sectors, has played a major role in this rise in costs. In 2000, private equity invested $5 billion in health care; by 2024, this had risen to $104 billion. Since private equity firms are focused not on patient care, but on maximizing profits, research has found that private equity ownership is associated with worse outcomes for patients as well as higher costs, particularly in nursing homes.

In large part due to rising costs for care, health coverage costs are slated to rise precipitously next year. A recent survey found that employers expect health care plan costs to rise by an average of 11 percent per worker in 2027, unless benefits are cut. This could translate to higher costs for workers and patients on job-based insurance if employers shift the burden onto them; costs for plans through the Affordable Care Act are also expected to rise significantly due to Republicans’ massive slashes via the One Big Beautiful Bill.

“Patients want to know that decisions about their health are being made by their doctors, not by Wall Street investors,” said Warren. “If we’re going to lower costs and un-rig the health care system, we need to stop the corporate takeover of medicine.”

The passage of the bill could also help allow physicians to retain control in their practices, including in their medical decisionmaking, at a time when private equity and other corporate actors are close to gobbling up almost the entire field of medical providers.

As the lawmakers point out, research has found that, as of this year, 82 percent of physicians are employed by hospitals or other corporate entities as the industry shifts away from private practices. This is a 20-point increase from 2019, when 62 percent of physicians were employed this way.

The legislation has been backed by numerous health and advocacy groups, who say that private equity must be barred from standing between patients and receiving good health care.

“A prohibition is only as strong as its enforcement, and this bill backs its corporate practice of medicine prohibition with three enforcement paths: the FTC, state attorneys general suing on behalf of residents, and physicians themselves through a private right of action with treble damages,” said Marco Fernandez, president of the Association for Independent Medicine. “That layered enforcement, paired with mandatory divestment, is what gives this bill teeth that earlier [Corporate Practice of Medicine] laws have often lacked.”
