author: Katja Diehl
title: 2,5 Milliarden. Verbrennen.
content:
Es ist leider gar nicht so schwer, DIE Stimme zur intersektionalen Mobilitätstransformation zu sein, wenn Gesellschaft und Politik bis heute bei Mobilität Auto und am liebsten auch Verbrenner denken.


2,5 Milliarden Euro für fossile Kraftstoffe – was wäre damit möglich?


Bund und Länder haben sich auf einen erneuten Tankrabatt ab dem 1. Oktober 2026 geeinigt. Es ist bereits der dritte Versuch innerhalb weniger Jahre, steigende Spritpreise durch kurzfristige Steuersenkungen zu kompensieren. Während massiv in die Subventionierung von Benzin und Diesel investiert wird, bleiben die strukturellen Defizite im öffentlichen Nahverkehr ungelöst.


Aus Sicht der Mobilitätsgerechtigkeit stellt sich mir die Frage:


Wie lange wollen wir noch mit der Gießkanne Milliarden ausschütten, während für jede Wahlfreiheit in der Mobilität durch Busse, Bahnen, Radwege angeblich kein Geld da ist?


Menschen in Armut, die auf das Auto angewiesen sind, ein geringes Einkommen haben und oft in ländlichen Regionen leben, wo Alternativen fehlen.


Mit denselben 2,5 Milliarden Euro ließen sich Hunderte Kilometer neuer Radwege bauen, On-Demand-Rufbus-Systeme im ländlichen Raum etablieren oder kindgerechte, sichere Räume schaffen. Selbst ein flächendeckendes Sozialticket wäre finanzierbar.

author: Amy Goodman
title: Trump Administration Aims to “Asphyxiate” Cuba Into Submission, Diplomat Says
content:
Meanwhile, the CIA recently formed a new secret task force as part of a widening US effort to destabilize Cuba.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

As the United Nations General Assembly opens in New York, we speak with senior Cuban diplomat Carlos Fernández de Cossío, who says the Trump administration is seeking to “asphyxiate the people of Cuba into submission.” On Friday, millions in Cuba lost power in what was at least the sixth major blackout since President Trump cut off fuel shipments to the island in January. The fuel blockade comes on top of the six-decade-long U.S. economic embargo and countless attempts to topple the communist government.

“We will do all we can to stop any nation, the U.S. or any nation, from taking over Cuba,” says Fernández de Cossío, who has served as deputy Cuban foreign minister since 2022.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman in New York. Juan González is in Chicago.

As world leaders gather for the United Nations General Assembly here in New York, we turn now to look at Cuba, which is facing a growing humanitarian crisis amidst an escalating economic war waged by the Trump administration. On Friday, millions in Cuba lost power in what was at least the sixth major blackout since President Trump cut off fuel shipments to the island in January. The fuel blockade comes on top of the six-decade-long U.S. embargo. Residents of Havana say they have no water or electricity in their homes.

VALENTIN PARRA: [translated] It’s very bad for everyone, because everyone gets desperate in a house without water and without light. It’s a phenomenon that isn’t seen anywhere else in the world, only here. And when people don’t have water — look, I myself was without water for 15 days, without water or light for 15 days. The luck is that I could bathe over here and bathe on the other side. But tell me: What does someone do who doesn’t have that possibility?

AMY GOODMAN: Meanwhile, the CIA recently formed a new secret Cuba task force as part of a widening U.S. effort to pressure Cuba. According to the Times, the CIA is adding case officers who recruit and manage spies, as well as officers who conduct cyber operations and specialize in covert influence operations.

The U.S. has made many attempts to overthrow the Cuban government over the past 65 years, hundreds of attempts. In 1960, the CIA formed a Cuba task force that oversaw the failed Bay of Pigs invasion on April 17th, 1961. The Guardian recently reported allies of President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have already begun vying for control of Cuba’s assets if the Cuban government falls under the U.S. pressure. The Wall Street Journal just published an article headlined “The Backroom Meetings in Miami Where Cuba’s Future Is Being Plotted.”

To talk about all of this, we’re joined by Cuba’s Deputy Foreign Minister Carlos Fernández de Cossío.

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: It is an honor.

AMY GOODMAN: Thanks so much for being with us. I’m glad we’re within the 25-mile zone that you’re allowed to travel in in New York. Right? Twenty-five miles from Columbus Circle?

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: Columbus Circle, yes.

AMY GOODMAN: Number one, if you can talk about what is — as the foreign minister addresses the United Nations, what’s the Cuban government’s message to the Trump administration as it tightens the economic sanctions and embargo?

CARLOS FERNÁNDEZ DE COSSÍO: We will be speaking to the international community at the U.N., not necessarily to the U.S. government, but the U.S. belongs to the international community. We live in a world which has become very dangerous, where expansionism, the ambition of domination, the attempts to take over the natural resources of developing countries has come back to the stage. The U.N. was created precisely for that not to happen, and has developed precisely for not that to happen, yet as reality today as a result of a foreign policy that is conceptualized as peace through force, which implies imposing the will of the U.S. through intimidation, aggression, coercion and so on. So, that’s one point that we need to talk.

We need to talk about the plight of the people of Cuba, because the aggression of the United States against Cuba today has a very serious human face …

title: İki gündür kayıp olarak aranıyordu: Ormanda cansız bedeni bulundu
content:
Kütahya - Tavşanlı ilçesinde 2 gündür kayıp olarak aranan gece bekçisi Hikmet Uzuncan (42), ormanda otomobilinin içinde ölü olarak bulundu.

Devekayası mevkiindeki özel bir şirkette gece bekçisi olarak çalışan Hikmet Uzuncan, 2 gün önce otomobiliyle evinden çıktıktan sonra kendisine haber alınamadı. Yakınları çevrede yaptığı aramalarda Uzuncan’dan bir iz bulamayınca kayıp ihbarında bulundu.

Yapılan incelemede Uzuncan’ın otomobiliyle 2 gün önce Tavşanlı-Kütahya kara yolu üzerindeki bir akaryakıt istasyondan yakıt alıp ayrıldığı belirlendi. Arama çalışmalarını akaryakıt istasyonun çevresinde yoğunlaştırılan jandarma ekipleri, Şahmelek mevkiindeki ormanda otomobili tespit edildi.

Otomobilde yapılan aramada ise Uzuncan'ın cansız bedeni bulundu. Jandarma ve savcılık incelemesinin ardından Uzuncan’ın cansız bedeni, hastane morguna kaldırıldı. Uzuncan’ın ölüm nedeni, yapılacak olan otopsinin ardından netlik kazanacak.

Olayla ilgili soruşturma sürüyor.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Senator Says European Nations Must Sanction Trump, Rubio Before US Wrecks ICC
content:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen said that Trump and Rubio’s attacks on the ICC seek to obstruct investigations into Netanyahu.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A U.S. senator has called on foreign leaders to impose sanctions on top U.S. officials as the Trump administration wages a campaign to dismantle the International Criminal Court (ICC).

Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) said that, if they “have any self-respect,” nations party to the ICC would take steps to stop the Trump administration’s meddling. It is extraordinary for such a call to come from a sitting member of congress.

“If European countries & other signatories to the International Criminal Court have any self-respect, they’d sanction Rubio & Trump for obstructing investigations of [Israel Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu’s war crimes,” the senator said in a post on social media on Monday.

When the Trump administration first announced sanctions against the court last year, a group of 79 countries, including major European powers like the U.K., France, and Germany, signed a statement opposing the move. “Such measures increase the risk of impunity for the most serious crimes and threaten to erode the international rule of law, which is crucial for promoting global order and security,” they wrote.

But, despite such statements, many of those nations have not taken decisive action to rein in the Trump administration — and, even further, have continued to capitulate to the administration on many repressive requests throughout Trump’s second term.

Van Hollen’s post came in response to a Wall Street Journal report that the administration is preparing yet more sweeping sanctions against the ICC. These sanctions, which have not been finalized, “forbid most transactions with the ICC after a grace period of six to seven months,” the Journal reports. Such sanctions could have wide-ranging consequences due to the U.S.’s vast control over global financial systems.

The sanctions sought by the Trump administration mark an escalation in its campaign against the ICC, the end goal of which, as Rubio has stated, is to “dismantle” the court. The U.S. has previously sanctioned individual members of the court, including the current president of the ICC, Tomoko Akane, as well as the lead prosecutor in the case against Netanyahu for crimes against humanity in Gaza.

Sanctions on the entire court could make it even harder for the ICC to carry out prosecutions of Netanyahu and other global leaders accused of committing human rights violations. Adil Haque, a professor of international law at Rutgers University, also noted on Monday that “Congress could pass a law stripping presidential power to sanction international institutions and their staff.”

The Trump administration has claimed that the ICC is a threat to American sovereignty. Analysts have said that the administration’s true goal is not to protect sovereignty, but to shield the U.S. and other allies from facing consequences for past and future abuses.

In his speech before the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, President Donald Trump reiterated his attacks on the ICC. He said that the ICC is an “evil group of people,” and called on all 125 member countries to “resign” from the body.

“We will never allow U.S. service members to be investigated or anyone else to be investigated, or given show trials by an anti-American tribunal with no jurisdiction over us,” Trump said.

His remarks came days after two separate UN reports suggested that U.S. officials could be investigated and prosecuted for war crimes in Iran and military actions in central and South America.

title: İran’dan Hürmüz Boğazı açıklaması: Geçiş düzenlemelerine uymayan gemilerin yüklerinin yüzde 20'sine el konulacak
content:
Yarı resmi Tesnim Haber Ajansı'na göre, İran Meclisi Ulusal Güvenlik Komisyonu Sözcüsü Hasan Kaşkavi, Hürmüz Boğazı’na ilişkin oluşturulan “Hürmüz Boğazı'nın Güvenliğinin Sağlanmasına Dair Stratejik Eylem Planı” hakkında konuştu.

İran Meclisi Ulusal Güvenlik Komisyonu’nda Stratejik Eylem Planı’nın 13, 14 ve 15. maddelerinin onaylandığını söyleyen Kaşkavi, Ceza Kanunu’nun 5. maddesine göre, 13. madde ile Hürmüz Boğazı’nda oluşturulan geçiş düzenlemelerine uymayan gemilerin taşıdığı yükün yüzde 20’sine el konulacağını veya yüzde 20'lik yükün değeri ölçüsünde ceza kesileceğini belirterek, cezanın ödenmemesi halinde gemilere de el konulacağını kaydetti.

Kaşkavi ayrıca, 14. maddeye göre Hürmüz Boğazı ile ilgili iki ülke arasında oluşturulan belge veya çok taraflı uluslararası anlaşmaların İran Anayasası’nın 77, 125, 176 ve 57. maddeleri çerçevesinde olması gerektiğini söyledi.

Kaşkavi, İran Genelkurmay Başkanlığının ilgili kanunun uygulanmasını takip etmekle görevli olduğunu ve bu hususun 15. maddede yer aldığını hatırlattı.

İran Ceza Kanunu’nun 5. maddesinin A fıkrasına göre, İranlı olsun veya olmasın, İran’ın iç ve dış güvenliğine, toprak bütünlüğüne veya bağımsızlığına karşı girişimde bulunanlar, İran’ın egemenliği dışında kalan alanlarda olsa bile, işlediği bazı suçlardan dolayı İran kanunlarına göre yargılanabiliyor.

title: Filistin: BM toplantılarında halkımızı koruyacak kararlar alınmasını istiyoruz
content:
Filistin Devlet Başkan Yardımcısı Hüseyin eş-Şeyh, yaptığı yazılı açıklamada İsrail'in işgal altındaki Filistin topraklarında sürdürdüğü ihlal ve saldırılara dikkati çekti.

Tel Aviv yönetiminin şehir, kasaba ve mülteci kamplarını demir kapı ve kontrol noktalarıyla toplu hapishanelere çevirdiğini belirten Şeyh, İsrail'in bu ihlalleri kapsamında Filistinlilere ait yüzlerce dönümlük arazilerde bulunan zeytin ağaçlarını söktüğünü kaydetti.

Filistin Devlet Başkan Yardımcısı, sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü:

"Dünyayı, halkımızı ırkçılıktan ve etnik temizlikten korumak için müdahale etmeye çağırıyoruz. Birleşmiş Milletlerin (BM) şu andaki toplantılarında Filistin halkını koruyacak ve işgalciyi tüm bu uygulamalarından vazgeçirecek kararlar alınmasını talep ediyoruz."

Resmi açıklamaların İsrail tarafından işlenen suçları durdurmadığına dikkati çeken Şeyh, İsrail'i ırkçı uygulamalarından vazgeçirecek caydırıcı adımlar atılması talebinde bulundu.

İsrail'in Gazze Şeridi'ne saldırılarını başlattığı Ekim 2023'ten bu yana işgal altındaki Batı Şeria ve Doğu Kudüs'te de Filistinlilere yönelik gözaltı, baskın ve saldırılarda artış yaşanıyor.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Tony Blair Wants Governments to Embrace AI, Not Slow It Down
content:
Tony Blair’s think tank has called for governments to embrace AI and rebuild their states around the new technology despite the risks posed to workers, societies and security.


The former Labour prime minister, who has multiple ties to the tech sector, has backed a new paper arguing that countries risk being left behind if they do not adapt to the AI era.


Blair’s vision for AI-powered governance was set out in a

paper

 released by his think tank, the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI).


“Countries cannot protect themselves from AI by ignoring it,” the paper argues. “The only meaningful path is to engage with it, building institutions capable of operating at the speed and complexity of the world now emerging, and harness AI to transform how the state itself works.” 


The institute’s paper does not make reference to Blair’s own relationship with the tech industry, including the hundreds of millions of dollars in funding his institute has received from tech moguls. 


Larry Ellison, the billionaire founder of software company Oracle, which is heavily invested in infrastructure driving the AI boom, has given

around £257m in donations and pledges

 to Blair’s think tank since 2021.


In February, campaign group

Foxglove criticised the UK government

 for collaborating with Blair’s think tank on AI implementation, stating: “Ministers seem to be unable to spot a potential conflict of interest which is blindingly obvious to everyone else.”


Despite acknowledging the risks to labour markets, the dangers of concentrating technological power and increased exposure to biological threats, the answer is not to slow development but instead to “harness and control it”, he wrote.


“This AI revolution will be happening to you and you won’t be guiding it,”

Blair added in a video interview posted on X

.


Earlier this month, a handful of AI executives

called for a global slowdown

 in AI development in response to warnings about the existential threat posed by the new technology. However, other

tech leaders – including the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia – questioned

 if Silicon Valley bosses were motivated more by safety concerns or by their fears of increased competition.

author: The Canadian Press
title: ‘Dooming the moose’: Manitoba Cree chief calls for voluntary stop to hunting
content:
The leader of a First Nation in Manitoba is urging all moose hunters to stop hunting in the community’s traditional territory due to what she calls dwindling population numbers.


Misipawistik Cree Nation Chief Heidi Cook is advocating for a “voluntary hunting closure” of an approved game hunting area that encompasses a large part of the community along the northwestern shores of Lake Winnipeg.


Cook is appealing to all hunters, including members of Misipawistik, to prioritize the long-term health of the moose population by halting harvesting in the area beginning Monday, when the season opens.


“At this moment in time, the moose population just cannot sustain that harvest. So we’re asking all Manitobans to stand with us in protecting moose and calling on our government to do better,” Cook said in an interview.


“We need to take action, all of us collectively, to protect that moose population so that it can be there for generations of hunters to come. This is our responsibility.”


Cook said information last year from the province, based on an aerial survey, estimated 64 bull moose were in the area.


The government has made 62 bull moose tags available for the same area this year, said the chief.


That doesn’t take into account community hunters, who have treaty rights to hunt on their traditional territory and don’t require government-issued licences or tags.


A provincial spokesperson said in an email Friday that the government’s survey found the moose population remained stable since the last survey in 2013.


While 62 tags were available this year, the spokesperson said fewer hunters applied and 37 licences were allocated. The government projects a harvest of nine bull moose.


The First Nation disputes the province’s position on the moose population, saying it has observed a sharp drop in the number harvested by members.


Cook said historically the community would harvest up to 19 moose in a season but that hasn’t happened for the past 10 to 15 years.


A government report detailing the 2013 survey recorded a historic low number of moose for the area. It attributed the low numbers to fires, forestry and mineral exploration, and suggested further disturbances to the animal’s habitat over the following 10 to 20 years.


The First Nation has been raising concerns with the province for years about the moose, said Cook, but it hasn’t seen much “meaningful change.”


“What our people have been experiencing for a number of years is that it’s almost an involuntary closure. We just don’t have the moose,” she said.


“This is something that is part of our responsibility. We have a right to moose, but we also have a responsibility to protect that moose and make sure that it can survive and be healthy.


“If we continue with the hunt as is, we’re dooming the moose to not being able to be available for future generations.”


Manitoba Keewatinowi Okimakanak, an advocacy group representing some northern First Nations, supports Cook’s call for a voluntary halt to hunting.


“When First Nations’ leaders raise concerns about the health of a population and the future sustainability of a resource, those concerns must be taken seriously by Manitoba,” Grand Chief Garrison Settee said in a statement.


Cook said areas south of the First Nation have seen total hunting closures because of the way the province has managed the moose population.


In 2024, Misipawistik warned the province its members couldn’t meaningfully hunt for moose in their territory and asked the government to put licences on hold.


The government reduced the number issued and committed to working with the community to determine moose population dynamics and the First Nation’s food needs, but Cook has said that didn’t happen.


The First Nation took the province to court last year in an attempt to halt moose harvesting in its territory, arguing it infringes on the community’s right to hunt for food and that moose are important for social and ceremonial purposes.


The importance of the animals affects the community in more ways than “just an empty freezer,” added Cook.


“It’s hard, because the moose is such an important cultural species. It’s tied to our relationship with the land, the sharing that happens between families, just the seasonal rhythms of being out and having those moose camps.”


In 2018, Misipawistik developed a land guardian program to track moose in the area.

author: William Turton
title: Trump’s FBI Scrapped Bribery Investigation Linked to Sen. Susan Collins
content:
A top donor told agents his company won millions in federal contracts by bankrolling campaigns of powerful politicians.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In the final weeks of 2019, a top fundraiser for Sen. Susan Collins walked into a perilous meeting at a Corner Bakery in Washington, D.C.

For the first time in her two-decade Senate career, the Republican lawmaker from Maine was in danger of losing her seat. President Donald Trump’s dismal approval ratings were dragging her down in the polls, and she was falling behind her likely 2020 Democratic challenger in fundraising.

Scott Reed, head of the Collins super PAC, was on a mission to close that gap. Reed was meeting that day with three executives from a Hawaiian defense contractor, Navatek. A year earlier, Collins had helped their company land a multimillion-dollar Navy research contract in Maine. Now, seated at a coffee shop not far from the U.S. Capitol, Reed asked them for a $500,000 donation.

Government contractors are banned from making political contributions. More consequentially, for the company to offer donations to Collins in exchange for an official action, or for Collins to accept, would constitute criminal bribery.

But the company did have such a proposal: Navatek was hungry for more government contracts in Maine. If they cut a big check, the CEO told Reed, Navatek wanted Collins to guarantee tens of millions of dollars in additional federal funding.

To skirt campaign finance laws and conceal the source of the funds, Navatek planned to funnel the donation through a shell company. The CEO wanted assurance that Collins would know where the money came from. Reed confirmed that she would, the executive said — and that Navatek would get its government contracts.

After the Corner Bakery meeting, Navatek’s CEO, Martin Kao, sent an initial $150,000 to the Collins super PAC using the shell company. Two months later, he told Navatek executives that Collins committed to getting the company $32 million in naval contracts, according to an internal company email reviewed by ProPublica.

Three years later, Kao holed up in a conference room to recount the Corner Bakery meeting to a group of four FBI agents and federal prosecutors. The FBI had seen through his shell company ruse, and in 2022 a grand jury indicted him for making illegal campaign contributions. No one working for Collins was charged.

Facing years in prison, Kao hoped to do less time by revealing the entire scheme.

What he told them has never before become public. The Corner Bakery meeting, he asserted, was just one episode in a sprawling pay-to-play operation that embroiled some of the most powerful figures in Congress.

Over three days at the U.S. attorney’s office in Honolulu, Kao laid out in devastating detail how his operation worked. He gave agents a 50-page document naming dozens of lobbyists, congressional staffers and members of Congress who he said helped him trade cash for contracts. Kao and his close associates had donated nearly $900,000 to dozens of politicians, allowing Navatek to establish operations in half a dozen states with over $40 million a year in government funding.

Most damningly, Kao told FBI agents and prosecutors, the company’s work for the government was of no real value. Navatek’s research under his stewardship never resulted in products the military wanted to buy, ProPublica found.

Kao’s tell-all interviews with the FBI lasted into late 2024. His confessions opened up an entirely new phase of the investigation. Agents sifted through hundreds of thousands of records seized during Kao’s arrest and found that many were consistent with his account of widespread influence peddling.

Kao had credibility issues. He was now a felon trying to avoid a lengthy prison sentence. And there were other challenges. Building a corruption case against elected officials requires extraordinary proof of a quid pro quo arrangement, in part because the Supreme Court has narrowed what counts as bribery.

Even so, by the end of 2024, the agents had enough evidence to pursue a sweeping bribery probe that could ensnare top lawmakers of both political parties. They asked their supervisors to approve a new investigation and contemplated using undercover operatives to gather more evidence. Although their effort was in its early stages, and it was unclear where it would lead, FBI agents asked Kao extensive questions …

… Von dem Moment an, als Trump ins Amt zurückkehrte, hat seine zweite Regierungsmannschaft einer Reihe von rechtsextremen Einflussnehmern und Nachrichtenagenturen Zugang und Status verschafft, darunter auch Persönlichkeiten mit zweifelhafter Vergangenheit und dünnen oder nicht vorhandenen journalistischen Referenzen. Auf diese Weise hat die Regierung einen Schwall schmeichelhafter Medienberichterstattung geschaffen, eine hauchdünne Blase um jede ihrer Entscheidungen, egal wie destruktiv oder inkohärent sie auch sein mag. Diese neuen staatlichen Medien zeigen bedingungslose Loyalität, und ihre Propaganda-Pipeline ist schneller als je zuvor und stellt sicher, dass jede Durchführungsverordnung oder jeder neue Schritt des Ministeriums für Regierungseffizienz in dem Moment, in dem er bekannt gegeben wird, mit begeisterter Pseudo-Berichterstattung begrüßt wird…“

Aus dem engl.

Artikel von Anna Merlan vom 25. Februar 2025 in Mother Jones

 

 – siehe mehr Informationen, auch zum Widerstand:


Trump verbietet CNN, MS NOW und Politico den Zugang zum Weißen Haus – Klagen und Soli-Boykott großer US-Sender, dem sich sogar Fox News anschließt


Trumps Streit mit Medien eskaliert: Der US-Präsident stellt Medien als Müll dar – und verbannt sie aus seiner Regierungszentrale. Stattdessen gibt es jetzt »Trump TV«.


„

Nach dem Rauswurf des TV-Senders CNN aus dem Weißen Haus eskaliert die Fehde zwischen Präsident Donald Trump und mehreren US-Medien. Die Sender CNN und MS NOW sowie das ebenfalls vom Ausschluss betroffene Nachrichtenportal »Politico« ziehen vor Gericht, um ihre Plätze im Weißen Haus zurückzuerkämpfen. Und der Streit zieht noch weitere Kreise: Die engmaschige TV-Begleitung auf Terminen und Reisen Trumps, die über ein Rotationsprinzip großer Fernsehsender geregelt ist, wurde von diesen gestoppt – als Protestaktion, weil CNN Teil dieses sogenannten Pools ist.


Mitten in diesem Streit ging das Weiße Haus am Montagabend (Ortszeit) mit einem eigenen Online-Kanal auf Sendung. Der Stream namens »Trump TV« zeigte zunächst Reden des Präsidenten sowie Übungen der US-Streitkräfte, deren Schlagkraft gepriesen wurde. Laut dem Weißen Haus wird »Trump TV« täglich rund um die Uhr laufen – »mit den besten Momenten aus der Vergangenheit, Ankündigungen sowie den neuesten und wichtigsten Nachrichten aus der Regierung«. Eigene Produktionen oder journalistische Inhalte waren zunächst nicht zu sehen.


Selbst Trumps Lieblingssender Fox News protestiert…


In einer gemeinsamen Stellungnahme der TV-Sender hieß es, die Öffentlichkeit habe ein grundlegendes Interesse daran, unabhängige Informationen über ihre Regierung zu erhalten – und keine Regierung solle eine Nachrichtenorganisation einschränken, nur weil sie deren Berichterstattung missbillige. Bemerkenswert ist, dass das Statement von allen fünf TV-Sendern kam – und damit auch von Fox News. Das ist eigentlich Trumps Lieblingssender, der häufig wohlwollend über ihn berichtet und ihm sehr viel Platz im Programm einräumt.


Auch die »New York Times« solidarisierte sich mit den »ungerecht ins Visier genommenen« Medienhäusern. Die Zeitung war am Montag für den Pressepool eingeteilt, der für Fotos zuständig ist. Als Reaktion auf den Ausschluss von CNN und Co. kündigte sie an, die am Montag aufgenommen Bilder nicht weiterzugeben und auch selbst nicht zu veröffentlichen. Die »Washington Post« teilte ebenfalls mit, keine Fotos von Auftritten des Präsidenten am Montag zu veröffentlichen.


CNN, »Politico« und MS NOW reichten ihre Klage bei einem Gericht in der Hauptstadt Washington ein. Das Verbot sei eine »Bedrohung für die Pressefreiheit und das Recht der Öffentlichkeit auf unabhängigen Journalismus ohne Einmischung der Regierung«, erklärten die Medien in einer gemeinsamen Mitteilung. Ziel sei es, »den Grundsatz zu verteidigen, dass die Regierung nicht darüber entscheidet, worüber die Presse berichtet oder was sie veröffentlicht«.


Die Klage der Medien wurde als Eilantrag eingereicht. Das heißt, dass sich ein Gericht zügig mit dem Fall befassen muss. Beantragt wurde, das Verbot unverzüglich zu kippen

author: Rizomatica
title: Filmoteca Ufro presentará en Temuco su libro “Memorias en movimiento”
content:
Dos años en el desafío de mediar, catalogar, digitalizar y difundir más de 3 mil rollos cinematográficos, tras la adjudicación del fondo de Salvaguardia del Patrimonio Audiovisual del Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio, es lo que compiló Filmoteca Ufro en su libro “Memorias en movimiento”. La presentación será este miércoles 23 de septiembre a las 17:00 horas, en el Auditorio Selva Saavedra.


Por Morín Ortiz.


En el segundo piso de la Biblioteca Central de la Universidad de la Frontera, frente a la escalera, se encuentra la Filmoteca Ufro. Una sala pequeña donde habitan cámaras filmadoras y cintas de diversos formatos, que “posibilitaron la captura de la memoria”, como le gusta decir a Diego Olivares, periodista, tipógrafo, realizador y archivista audiovisual que coordina este proyecto.


El origen de este archivo fílmico se sitúa en el 2008, cuando Diego se encontraba realizando un documental cuyo protagonista no tenía imágenes de su infancia, por lo que juntaron cerca de cien latas de películas. ”El acuerdo era construir su historia con imágenes de otros niños, con imágenes encontradas que servirían para retratar otra época: las calles, los autos, la moda, los roles de género”, relata.


De cientos de rollos pasaron a miles, lo que comenzó a ser un problema para un coleccionista por la falta de un lugar adecuado para resguardarlos. Años después, Diego Olivares logró hacer un vínculo con la Universidad de la Frontera -donde es docente- para almacenarlos.


Uno de los principales hallazgos en este crecimiento, tiene lugar en el Persa Bío Bío de Santiago, donde Diego se encontraba vitrineando cuando llamaron su atención unas latas escasamente rotuladas en las que podía leer “Budi, Puerto Saavedra”. Volvió a Temuco con 26 latas de cine en 16 mm. filmadas entre 1926 y 1936, lo que resultó ser una sorpresa, porque el modelo de cámaras usadas para su filmación comenzó a ser vendido en el mundo tan solo tres años antes de hechos estos registros en la costa de la Araucanía, por parte de la familia ganadera Duhalde, de origen Vasco Francés. Dato de origen al que llegaron gracias a la observación del profesor Jaime Flores de la Ufro, quien identificó un tipo de ganado particular que se aprecia en algunas de estas cintas.


El 2024 Filmoteca Ufro fue el único proyecto no metropolitano en adjudicarse este fondo para la Salvaguardia del Patrimonio Audiovisual, sin embargo, Diego Olivares destaca la importancia nacional de este trabajo, ya que las imágenes que conservan son desde el norte hasta el sur más extremo de Chile: “Creemos que es un gran aporte a nivel nacional, porque hay muchos lugares que solo están filmados en estos pequeños formatos. Muchas veces el Estado, el cine nacional, propagandístico, político, el cine más comercial no llegó a todos los lugares, porque nuestro cine ha estado súper inconcluso”.


Uno de los pilares de la instalación de Filmoteca Ufro es el programa de mediación que ha relacionado a las comunidades interesadas con el acervo y la labor de este archivo. El artista y realizador audiovisual Ange Cayuman diseñó el plan de mediación de este proyecto y es el encargado de llevarlo a cabo. En estos dos años, han desarrollado actividades de vinculación con colegios a los que han ido a visitar con los elementos del cine fílmico, así como también han recibido a los establecimientos que han solicitado visitar el archivo.


En agosto del 2025, Olivares y Cayuman viajaron hasta Punta Arenas para ser parte del XVII Festival Internacional de Cine Polo Sur Latinoamericano con talleres y exhibiciones. Han realizado muestras de cine en la universidad con la presencia de personas relevantes del mundo documental y los archivos, como la antropóloga y documentalista mexicana Gabriela Zamorano y el estreno en Temuco de su documental Archivo Cordero, sobre uno de los mayores acervos visuales del siglo XX en Bolivia.


Otras de las actividades de mediación, fue Filmoteca Lab, en junio del 2026, que contó “con la presencia de investigadoras/es, cineastas y una gran cantidad de personas que se interesan por el uso de los archivos a nivel de la memoria local, de los procesos de creación artística, de los intereses disciplinares como la antropología, la geografía, y la educación”, señaló Ange Cayuman, agregando que “ha sido un proceso que ha abierto posibilidades de vinculación desde la universidad con el territorio que habita y otros, y de generación de investigación y creación, que es el fin de un …

author: Clara Saliba
title: Flávio Bolsonaro propõe ‘voucher’ para creche: a troco de quê?
content:
Uma grande novidade deste período eleitoral é a constatação por parte das campanhas – de todos os espectros políticos – de que 51,5% do eleitorado é composto de mulheres. E que, por isso, falar delas e de pautas que as interessam talvez seja uma boa ideia. 


A aproximação da direita e da extrema direita ao público feminino não é de hoje. O crescimento de figuras como a Senadora Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF) e a própria Michelle Bolsonaro (PL-DF), ex-presidente do PL Mulher, são exemplos disso. 


Claro, existem personalidades e falas misóginas também na esquerda. Mas

essa “direita pró-mulher” me é um pouco estranha porque, afinal, o projeto da direita é, em essência, machista. Afinal, o neoliberalismo é ancorado em políticas econômicas que não só prejudicam relativamente mais as mulheres como dependem de forma basilar da exploração gratuita de seu trabalho. 


Um exemplo bastante conhecido é o das creches públicas. Um projeto de Estado mínimo que se desresponsabilize do investimento na educação infantil nunca vai se preocupar em garantir vagas para todas as crianças. 


Isso, por um lado, reduz a possibilidade de autonomia econômica das mães, que têm restrita sua possibilidade de trabalhar fora porque precisam ofertar cuidado para as crianças em tempo integral – sem compensação financeira. Já que

hoje

, cerca de 30% das mulheres que não buscam trabalho remunerado afirmam não o fazer por precisarem se dedicar ao cuidado de familiares e a afazeres domésticos. 


Por outro lado, este projeto terceiriza para a figura das famílias – na prática, quase sempre só às mulheres – uma carga que deveria ser da sociedade como um todo, a de manter e reproduzir a vida. 


No caso das crianças, elas são a força de trabalho do futuro. 


Ou seja: o país só cresce, produz e prospera porque há algumas décadas uma parte das mulheres dedicou anos de suas vidas para criar gratuitamente quem hoje compõe a massa de trabalhadores. 


O benefício da educação das crianças é apropriado por todos, mas os custos são vistos como uma responsabilidade privada – e que tem gênero. 


Ou seja, a direita neoliberal prega o desmonte de um aparato de políticas públicas importantíssimas para a autonomia feminina. 


Voltando ao exemplo das creches,

uma das propostas de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) é a ampliação da vaga de creches, usando como recurso, no caso de falta das vagas públicas, a distribuição de “vouchers” para creches particulares. 


Por trás de uma aparente defesa da autonomia das mulheres (que pouco convence a quem conhece o candidato, sua família e seu entorno político, com histórico de falas bastante machistas, diga-se de passagem) há uma repetição dessa mesma lógica neoliberal que estamos discutindo.


Ofertar “vouchers” para a educação pública é, de novo, tirar a responsabilidade do Estado e da coletividade e direcionar para o mercado privado. Além disso, tem efeitos ambíguos, pois raramente conduz a uma melhoria do serviço ofertado.

 Mercantilizar um serviço que não segue a lógica operacional de mercado traz mais malefícios do que ganhos. 


Uma política de “vouchers” expande, a princípio, o número de vagas, porque gera um incentivo financeiro para a criação de equipamentos de creche particular. Mas dificilmente os valores repassados às famílias serão suficientes para custear uma educação de elite. Criam-se aparelhos voltados para o atendimento desse mercado, com pior qualidade, superlotação e outras estratégias para garantir que uma atividade que não é muito lucrativa por princípio vire um bom “negócio”.


A educação infantil vira uma máquina de fazer dinheiro, e assim há ainda menos incentivo para resolver o problema da falta de vagas na rede pública. 


Quem perde são as crianças. E as mulheres que cuidam delas. 


Num outro caminho, a Política Nacional de Cuidados, instituída em dezembro de 2023, dá um passo na garantia do direito universal às creches públicas. Sua aprovação e a subsequente criação do Plano Nacional de Cuidados Brasil que Cuida foram uma vitória importante do movimento feminista no governo atual. Meses antes fora criada a

Secretaria Nacional da Política de Cuidados e Família

, no Ministério do Desenvolvimento e Assistência Social, Família e Combate à Fome (MDS), e da

Secretaria Nacional de Autonomia Econômica e Política de Cuidados

, no Ministério das Mulheres. São dois órgãos criados para construir políticas sólidas para as mulheres. 


O Plano prevê a criação de 100 mil novas vagas em creches e pré-escolas …

title: Escuela Moderna/Ateneo Libertario (Venecia) en las Biennale Sessions 2026: «Escultura social, tecnología y ciudad»
content:
Escuela Moderna/Ateneo Libertario en las Biennale Sessions 2026: «Escultura social, tecnología y ciudad»

El 9 de mayo de 2026, Escuela Moderna/Ateneo Libertario presentó en las Biennale Sessions de la Bienal de Venecia el proyecto «Escultura social, tecnología y ciudad», dedicado a la figura y al pensamiento de Joseph Beuys.

«Azione Terza Via es el intento de afrontar la lucha por un cambio social radical en Occidente y en Oriente, por la solución de la crisis ecológica y por superar el retraso en el desarrollo del Tercer Mundo, uniendo las fuerzas y los medios de todos aquellos que han reconocido que los sistemas económicos, políticos e ideológicos existentes han llevado a la humanidad a un callejón sin salida que pone en peligro su existencia».

Así escribía Joseph Beuys en 1978, y a partir de estas palabras Escuela Moderna/Ateneo Libertario ha desarrollado el proyecto «Escultura social, tecnología y ciudad», presentado en Venecia en el marco de las Biennale Sessions.

Uno de los árboles relacionados con este proyecto se encuentra en Monte Verità, en Suiza, un lugar históricamente ligado a experiencias de libertad, vida comunitaria y pensamiento anarquista.

La jornada comenzó con la ponencia inaugural de Massimo Mazzone, que repasó los 7000 Eichen (7000 robles) de Joseph Beuys, una de las grandes obras de arte público del maestro alemán. Iniciado en Kassel en 1982, el proyecto consistió en la plantación de 7.000 robles, acompañados cada uno por una columna de basalto. Para Beuys, aquella intervención no era simplemente una acción ecológica: formaba parte de su concepto de «escultura social», según el cual el arte puede intervenir directamente en la transformación de la sociedad y de la ciudad.

A continuación intervinieron Gianluca Stasi y Alessandro Zorzetto, dos arquitectos vinculados desde hace décadas a las artes visuales y relacionados también con la Bienal desde diferentes ámbitos.

Ambos recorrieron el profundo significado de una tradición que ha marcado a generaciones de artistas, arquitectos y diseñadores. Partiendo precisamente de la «lección» de Beuys, y también de las aportaciones de Yona Friedman, Giancarlo De Carlo, Gordon Matta-Clark y Pettena, plantearon una forma diferente de entender la relación entre arte, arquitectura, tecnología, ciudad y participación social.

En este recorrido ocupa también un lugar especial José Pérez de Lama, arquitecto, investigador y profesor sevillano, cuya trayectoria estuvo estrechamente relacionada con la arquitectura, las tecnologías libres, la cultura digital, el territorio y las formas participativas de construcción de la ciudad. Su pensamiento y su trabajo se encuentran en sintonía con muchas de las cuestiones que atraviesan este proyecto.

Pérez de Lama falleció en 2025, demasiado joven. Su contribución a estos ámbitos es reivindicada ahora como parte de una tradición de pensamiento que entiende la arquitectura y el arte no como disciplinas aisladas, sino como herramientas capaces de intervenir en la sociedad y de transformar los espacios que habitamos.

De Beuys a Pérez de Lama, pasando por Friedman, De Carlo, Matta-Clark y Pettena, el proyecto «Escultura social, tecnología y ciudad» recupera así una misma preocupación: cómo utilizar el arte, la arquitectura, la tecnología y la participación colectiva para imaginar y construir otras formas de ciudad y de sociedad.

No se trata solamente de hacer arte, sino de estar presentes (como libertarios) en todos los ámbitos —social, cultural, arquitectónico, tecnológico, sindical y de lucha—, reivindicando una presencia activa y una manera diferente de intervenir en la realidad.

Lugar: Arsenale de Venecia, Sale d'Armi D

Marco: Biennale Sessions, dentro de la 61.ª Exposición Internacional de Arte de La Biennale di Venezia.

title: The enchanter of the Balkans
content:
At the beginning of the concert, when the lights in the hall were gently dimmed and the sound of a wind instrument rose from the back rows, everyone turned with curiosity toward the source of the sound. Some audience members stood up to see the musician. Just as they caught sight of him, another appeared from a different corner, and then another from the back. Positioned among the audience, the orchestra members began accompanying one another one by one as they walked toward the stage.


As they moved toward the stage playing trombone, trumpet, and saxophone, two women in traditional Bulgarian attire entered from behind and took their positions on the left. The younger, dark-haired man sat down behind a large bass drum. Once all nine were on stage, Goran Bregović arrived in white attire, with his signature disheveled hair. Sitting in the middle of the orchestra, he picked up his distinct electric guitar. As he took his seat, nearly the entire audience burst into applause and excitement. The few who remained seated looked bewildered and out of place, because this concert at the Kongresshaus in Zurich, Switzerland, was a gathering of former Yugoslavs and the "others."


Most of the Swiss audience members were bewildered because they had come simply to sit, listen, and leave. Yet here, the roles had reversed: the local had become the "other," while the "other" virtually turned into the host. Unable to make much sense of the core "others"—who had arrived separately but were now dancing as if they were a single community—the locals joined in by dryly swaying their shoulders and nodding along. This is a unifying power unique to Goran. He began making music in 1966 at just 16 years old—a 60-year legacy of artistic creation. Unsurprisingly, he has mastered the art of connecting with his audience.


The Art of a 'Cultural Yugoslav'


Born in Sarajevo to a Serbian mother and a Croatian father, he entered the world when his homeland, Yugoslavia, was at the beginning of a federal structure that peacefully united different ethnic, religious, and cultural identities. This richness of his native land influenced his musical style—which blends Balkan rhythms—and served as the primary inspiration for defining himself as a "cultural Yugoslav."


In a European continent that had caused two world wars, the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was established in 1945 under the leadership of Josip Broz Tito following World War II. Pre-war "powers" like Britain, France, Germany, and Japan suffered military and economic devastation alongside the loss of millions of lives. The resulting power vacuum was filled by the two victorious superpowers: the United States and the Soviet Union.


In the power struggle known as the "Cold War," the Western Bloc led by the US and NATO squared off against the Eastern Bloc formed by the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact. States that refused to align with either block joined under the umbrella of the "Non-Aligned Movement." Tito led this initiative. Indeed, the movement was formalized at the 1961 Belgrade Conference, with Yugoslavia, Egypt, India, Indonesia, and Ghana among its founding members.


Although Yugoslavia positioned itself among these neutral states, its socialist system meant Western nations treated it as an actor leaning toward the East. Tito made immense efforts throughout his life to preserve the country's ethnic and cultural diversity. After his death, although Yugoslavia tried to maintain its neutral stance, an empowered opposing Bloc treated it almost as "the Eastern Bloc's outpost in the West." These delicate internal differences and contradictions, stoked by external blocs, ultimately dragged the country into a conflict-ridden and bloody disintegration.


Yugoslavia Collapsed; He Reunited It Through Music…


Yugoslavia consisted of eight administrative federal entities in total: six constituent republics and two autonomous provinces within Serbia. Slovenia and Croatia declared independence on June 25, 1991. The Slovenes achieved their modern status after ten days of conflict, while the Croats did so after nearly four years of war. A few months later, on September 8, Macedonia declared independence following a referendum, separating without armed conflict. Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence after a referendum on March 1, 1992, but was plunged into a bloody war until 1995. In this conflict—the bloodiest fought on European soil since WWII—over one hundred thousand people …

title: DFG pays tribute to journalist Seyit Evran
content:
The Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) issued a written statement marking the anniversary of the death of journalist Seyit Evran (Seyit Mahmut Evran).


Evran, who was 54, passed away on 22 September 2023, at a hospital in North and East Syria where he was receiving treatment. DFG said he had devoted his journalistic career to conveying to the world the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom and democracy, events in Kurdistan, and the realities of the peoples of the region.


DFG said that Evran did not view journalism merely as a profession, but as a means of making visible the realities experienced by peoples and bearing witness to history. The statement added that through the photographs he took, his reporting, and his analyses from conflict zones, he left behind an important journalistic and historical record.


The association said: “Keeping his memory alive, preserving the journalistic legacy he left behind, and continuing to defend the truth is a responsibility for us.”


Seyit Evran


Evran was born in 1969 in the Hênê (Hani) district of Amed. He witnessed the events that unfolded following the September 12 military coup. During his studies at Çukurova University, he met journalist Gurbetelli Ersöz, an encounter that became an important turning point in his journalistic career.


Evran began working as a journalist at the Özgür Ülke newspaper in 1994, at a time when clashes, village evacuations, and unsolved killings were widespread in the Kurdish provinces.


Evran was serving as the editor responsible for Özgür Ülke’s editorial office when the newspaper’s Istanbul headquarters, as well as its Ankara and Amed offices, were bombed on December 3, 1994. He escaped the attack unharmed. Newspaper employee Ersin Yıldız was killed and 23 employees were injured in the attack.


In the following years, Evran worked as a journalist in conflict zones across Kurdistan and compiled his experiences and testimonies in his book “A Journey to the Edge of Life.”


Evran followed events in Rojava


Evran, who also worked as a journalist in Armenia and Russia, moved to northern and eastern Syria in 2012. Closely following developments in Rojava, he worked to bring developments in the region to the attention of the international public and taught journalism at press academies.


Evran moved to the Kurdistan Region in 2017 and later returned to northern and eastern Syria. He underwent two heart surgeries but continued his journalistic work despite his health problems.


Evran did not stop working as a journalist during the final period of his life. He died on 22 September 2023, leaving behind a journalistic legacy spanning many years of reporting, photographs, writing, and eyewitness testimony.

title: Iraq in talks with Ankara over withdrawal of Turkish troops
content:
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has confirmed that talks are underway with Ankara over the withdrawal of the Turkish military from Iraq and the Kurdistan Region. “Our talks with the government in Ankara are continuing in order to reach an agreement on the withdrawal of Turkish troops from Iraqi territory,” al-Zaidi said in an interview with the New York Times.


In the interview, al-Zaidi also addressed the future of non-state armed groups in Iraq. He said their disarmament was not voluntary but mandatory. “Above all, in order to build a strong economy, weapons must be exclusively under the control of the state,” the prime minister said.


Disarmament to be completed by June 2027


Following the planned complete withdrawal of the remaining US troops on September 30, the Iraqi government intends to announce the terms of an agreement on disarmament. The process will then be implemented gradually and is expected to be completed by June 30, 2027. According to al-Zaidi, some of the groups concerned are calling for the deadline to be extended until the end of 2027.


As a first step, the plan provides for a 90-day period during which the armed groups will halt their attacks and the United States, in return, will refrain from retaliatory strikes. The surrender of weapons will then begin. “These groups will not have an independent status,” al-Zaidi said. Their members could individually join the Hashd al-Shaabi forces. Once the specified deadline has passed, organizations that continue to operate as independent armed groups will be considered illegal and banned.


Billions in losses due to war against Iran


Al-Zaidi also addressed the economic consequences of the US war against Iran for Iraq. He said the country had lost 60 percent of its oil export revenues due to Tehran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The prime minister estimated the resulting financial losses at around $60 billion.

author: Unknown
title: Lawyer Binbir: İGK decisions preventing releases from prison must be abolished
content:
The release of numerous political prisoners, including İzzethan Aykut, Hicran Binici, Mehmet Sait Yıldırım, Gülşen Adet, Nuriye Adet, Aydın Altığ, Mahsum Bilem, Levent Cin, Zübeyir İdem, Ömer Okul, Nidayi Tezer, Nurettin Ataman, Ahmed Abdi İbrahim and Tuncay Doğan, has been repeatedly postponed this year by the Administrative and Observation Boards.


The Administrative and Observation Boards, which have become an obstacle to the release process in prisons, are preventing the release of prisoners who have served 30 years in particular, citing various grounds. Their decisions have invoked reasons such as “not displaying good conduct,” “showing no remorse,” “failing to develop awareness of the offense,” “failing to distance oneself from organizational ideology,” and “the assessment that the individual will maintain ties with the organization.”


Lawyer Mehmet Zeki Binbir, a member of the Prison Commission of the Lawyers for Freedom Association (ÖHD), stated that the decisions issued by the Administrative and Observation Boards, which were established by legislation passed in 2020 and came into effect in 2021, are unlawful.


Speaking to ANF, Binbir said that the boards were making decisions beyond the scope of their authority and extending the sentences of political prisoners on abstract grounds. He said, “Although it is not their duty, they effectively conduct a trial, extend sentences on abstract grounds, carry out a second trial and impose further penalties. We believe that the purpose behind this law is entirely political because it is applied only to political prisoners. We have not received a single application from ordinary prisoners regarding this issue. In fact, this law was established to increase pressure.”


Drawing attention to the composition of the boards, Binbir noted that the only legal professionals serving on them are the Chief Public Prosecutor and a prosecutor appointed by the Chief Public Prosecutor. “Apart from them, the other members consist of prison administrators, staff members, psychiatrists or teachers,” he said.


‘Courts are not responding favorably’


Binbir said that the appeals they had filed against the board decisions in the cases they were following had yielded no results. “We have filed numerous applications regarding this issue and are following many such cases. However, at this stage, we have not received any favorable response from the courts regarding them,” he said.


The consequences of the boards’ decisions can be seen in the postponement of releases. The release of İzzethan Aykut, an ill prisoner who has been incarcerated for 30 years and was due to be released on September 16, was postponed for three months on the grounds that he had “not displayed good conduct.” Aykut, who suffers from health problems including heart failure, asthma and vertigo, is scheduled to appear before the board again on December 18.


At least 1,500


ill prisoners remain behind bars


With releases being postponed, the situation of ill prisoners is also becoming increasingly urgent. There are at least 1,500 ill prisoners in Turkey and Kurdistan, 335 of whom are reported to be seriously ill.


The problems faced by ill prisoners include delays in transfers to hospital, medical examinations while handcuffed, denial of access to healthcare, and the postponement of releases.


Even the right to medical treatment becomes torture


Lawyer Binbir drew attention to the violations seriously ill prisoners face during transfers to hospitals, saying, “They are taken to the hospital in handcuffs and subjected to searches inside their mouths. We thought these practices might decrease during the current process, but the problems continue.”


Mehmet Sait Yıldırım, a seriously ill prisoner who has been imprisoned for 33 years, has recently been subjected to this treatment. The 75-year-old Yıldırım’s release was postponed for three months for the third time on August 24. Following his board hearing, Yıldırım suffered a heart attack and was taken to hospital, where two stents were inserted into his heart.


Yıldırım, who suffers from COPD, hypertension and cardiovascular disease, is among the seriously ill prisoners.


‘If the state is sincere, it should ensure releases’


Binbir said that the failure to release prisoners cannot be considered separately from the new legal regulations. Referring to the “framework law” adopted by Parliament on August 10, he said that around 4,000 prisoners are expected to benefit …

title: KNK welcomes the unification of KDP and PUK Peshmerga  in the Kurdistan Region
content:
The Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) issued a message welcoming the unification of the 80th Unit of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the 70th Unit of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) under the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs. The Peshmerga forces were brought under a unified command at a ceremony held in Hewlêr (Erbil) on September 21, 2026, attended by Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani, Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani, Deputy Prime Minister Qubad Talabani, Minister of Peshmerga Affairs Shoresh Ismail, and other Kurdistan Region officials.


The statement described the unification of the Peshmerga forces as an aspiration of the people of Kurdistan for decades and expressed hope that the move would mark the beginning of the unification of all administrative, security, economic and diplomatic institutions.


“We hope that this initiative will serve as a means of fostering unity and solidarity across Kurdistan on the basis of national and patriotic principles,” the KNK said.


The statement noted that a government has not been formed for two years following the elections held in the Kurdistan Region, describing the situation as dangerous and unacceptable and expressing hope that parliament would be formed as soon as possible.


“As the KNK, we regard the unification of the Peshmerga forces as a positive and auspicious step for Southern Kurdistan and all of Kurdistan. On this occasion, we congratulate all the people of Southern Kurdistan and all Kurds around the world. We also thank the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), and all parties and groups that supported and contributed to this significant initiative,” the statement concluded.

title: Bakırhan: No consensus without equal rights for Alevis
content:
DEM Party Co-Chairs Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan met with representatives of Alevi organizations in Ankara. The meeting focused on the Peace and Democratic Society Process, as well as the concerns, demands and proposals of the Alevi community.


Bakırhan said at the meeting on Tuesday that Turkey was going through a decisive period. He said the goal of the ongoing process could not be limited to ending violence and armed conflict. “This must be followed by a phase in which democracy, the rule of law and equal citizenship are realized.” The concerns of Alevis must also be taken into account, Bakırhan said. “For us, consensus can only be achieved on the basis of legal recognition, only within a legal framework in which Alevis feel that they are equal citizens.” The DEM Party, he added, will not support a process that does not ensure the equal participation of Alevis.


Peace is possible when all identities are free


Bakırhan said that genuine peace could only be achieved when Alevis were equal citizens, Cem houses (Alevi places of worship) were granted legal status, discrimination was ended, and all identities were free to exist. With the implementation of the framework law, he added, the process would enter a second phase. This phase, he said, must aim at the democratization of Turkey and the creation of a system in which different identities could coexist on an equal footing while preserving their distinct characteristics.


“If the Kurds are one pillar of this struggle, then another is the Alevis, the oppressed, and those whose rights are not recognized,” the DEM Party co-chair said. The goal, he added, was to advocate for a shared citizenship that includes everyone.


Democratic integration does not mean Turkification


Bakırhan also rejected an understanding of integration based on assimilation. “Democratic integration does not mean that Kurds are Turkified or Alevis are Sunnified. On the contrary, it is about building a free relationship.” He also warned against attempts to drive Kurds and Alevis apart and weaken existing social ties. “Different identities must preserve their distinct characteristics and, on that basis, build a shared democratic future,” he noted.


Bakırhan also criticized attempts to distinguish between supposedly “acceptable” Alevis and other members of the Alevi community. The painful experiences of the past must not be forgotten, he said, while at the same time the future must not be built on a repetition of those experiences.


Alevi organizations plan to meet with other parties


Mustafa Aslan, Chair of the Alevi-Bektashi Federation (ABF), described the meeting as important for directly voicing the concerns and demands of the Alevi community. Alevis must play an active role in the democratization process, Aslan said. Meetings with other political parties are therefore planned for the coming weeks.

title: Beshear Says McConnell’s Return Shows Why the Senate Is “Broken”
content:
“I still have concerns, and I think anybody who actually watches the video [of McConnell] has concerns,” Beshear said.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Gov. Andy Beshear (D-Kentucky) told the hosts of ABC’s “The View” that he still has concerns about Sen. Mitch McConnell’s (R-Kentucky) ability to serve in Congress.

McConnell returned to work at the U.S. Capitol earlier in September, after spending three months out of public view following a fall in his home in June. During that time, the Kentucky senator made some public statements, but never provided audio or video evidence of his recovery, leading to questions about his ability to remain in office for the rest of his term.

When he did return, McConnell was noticeably frail, observers noted. He did speak for a brief time to reporters, but took no questions, and his speech was much slower than usual.

Beshear took notice of McConnell’s condition and said Monday morning he was still worried about McConnell’s health — and whether he should remain in office.

“I still have concerns, and I think anybody who actually watches the video has concerns, both for him and for the position,” Beshear said.

The Kentucky governor, who joined many lawmakers and observers in demanding McConnell show proof of his recovery during the three months he was gone, also believes the situation showed a larger problem with Congress in general.

“This is what’s broken about the current Senate: they don’t think they work for anybody. I mean, Mitch McConnell was gone for three months, three months away from work, and wouldn’t tell his boss, which are the people of the Commonwealth of Kentucky,” Beshear explained.

Gov. Andy Beshear calls for term limits after Mitch McConnell abandoned his constituents. pic.twitter.com/P9VsXU81vR

Beshear also used the opportunity to call for term limits.

“None of us wish [McConnell] ill will,” Beshear insisted, “but we all deserve senators that can actually do their job. And I think it’s fair to say we can now all agree it’s time for term limits for Congress. Yeah, and I’ll throw it out for the Supreme Court, too.”

Some government reformers have maintained that, while well-intentioned, term limits are not the best way to address issues like aging lawmakers or long-term, unpopular incumbents remaining in office, as they would prevent constituents from selecting effective leaders who have been in Washington a long while but are still supported by voters. Experts also agree that term limits would be ineffective at addressing the core reasons why incumbents like McConnell stay in office so long — including issues like gerrymandering and corporate spending in elections.

But on Supreme Court justices facing tenure limits, experts say the matter is different, as those chosen for the role are not elected by the people themselves. According to a recent Marquette University Law School poll, nearly 8 in 10 Americans (79 percent) support fixed terms for Supreme Court justices, while 2 in 10 (21 percent) oppose the idea.

title: İmamoğlu: Absürt davalarla yargının yorulmasını istemiyorum
content:
Büyükçekmece 21. Asliye Ceza Mahkemesi, tutuklu cumhurbaşkanı adayı ve İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediye (İBB) Başkanı Ekrem İmamoğlu’nun Beylikdüzü Belediye Başkanlığı dönemindeki makam aracı uygulamasına ilişkin davanın ilk duruşmasını Silivri’de yaptı.


Savcılık, İmamoğlu’nun ortağı olduğu İmamoğlu İnşaat’a ait aracın makam aracı olarak kullanıldığı dönemde yakıt, lastik, bakım ve onarım giderlerini belediyenin karşılaması nedeniyle “görevi kötüye kullanma” suçunun oluştuğunu öne sürüyor. İddianamede, bu harcamalar nedeniyle 122 bin 305 lira 70 kuruş kamu zararı oluştuğu öne sürülüyor. Savcılık, İmamoğlu için altı aydan iki yıla kadar hapis cezası istiyor.


12 sanıklı davada İBB Spor Kulübü Başkanı Fatih Keleş ile YENİ Parti Beylikdüzü İlçe Başkanı Mülayim Demirtaş da yargılanıyor.


İmamoğlu, aynı gün İstanbul 33. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nin İBB davasındaki oturumuna katıldıktan sonra Silivri’deki Marmara Ceza İnfaz Kurumları Kampüsü’ndeki 4 No’lu duruşma salonuna geçti.


YENİ Parti Grup Başkanvekili Gökhan Günaydın, YENİ Parti İstanbul İl Başkanı Özgür Çelik, İBB Başkanvekili Nuri Aslan ve çok sayıda yurttaş duruşmayı izledi.


Salon dolunca jandarma girişleri kapattı. İmamoğlu’nun yanı sıra sekiz tutuksuz sanığın da bulunduğu duruşmada hakim, kimlik tespitinin ardından iddianamenin özetini okudu.


Ekrem İmamoğlu’na yeni dava


1 Mart 2026


“100’üncü duruşmaya giriyorum”


İmamoğlu, savunmasına 9 Mart 2026’dan bu yana 100’üncü kez duruşmaya çıktığını söyleyerek başladı.


ANKA Haber Ajansı

’nın aktardığına göre, davayı kendisine yönelik yargı süreçlerinin siyasi bir parçası olarak nitelendiren İmamoğlu, “Bana yönelik yürütülen yargı saldırısının sebebi olarak doğmuş siyasi davalardan bir tanesindesiniz ne yazık ki” dedi.


İmamoğlu, yargının siyasetten bağımsız olması gerektiğini savundu ve sözlerinin yalnızca kendi tutukluluğuna ilişkin olmadığını söyledi.


⚖️ ‘Makam aracı’ davası başladı

🗣️ Ekrem İmamoğlu: “Absürt davalarla yargının yorulmasını istemiyorum”

https://t.co/YAM6KwagKR


pic.twitter.com/3O0sVzNokv


— bianet (@bianet_org)

September 22, 2026


“Aracı belediyeye bedelsiz tahsis ettim”


İmamoğlu, Beylikdüzü Belediye Başkanı olduğu dönemde belediyenin kiraladığı makam aracının maliyetini yüksek bulduğunu ve bunun yerine şirketine ait aracı belediyeye bedelsiz tahsis ettiğini anlattı.


Davanın bu işlemden kaynaklandığını belirten İmamoğlu, “Benim aracım varsa milletin parasını neden makam aracına harcayayım ya da makama hizmet aracına harcayayım?” dedi.


İmamoğlu, kendi aracını kullandığı için belediyenin araç kiralama giderinden kurtulduğunu savundu. Ortağı olduğu ve şu anda Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu’nun (TMSF) yönettiğini söylediği şirketin de dava konusu yakıt ve diğer giderler için faiziyle birlikte yaklaşık 215 bin lirayı belediyeye ödediğini belirtti.


“Bir litre benzinin hesabını da veririm, bir lastiğin hesabını da veririm. Çünkü kamu görevlisine milletin tek kuruşunun dahi hesabı sorulmalıdır” diyen İmamoğlu, belediye başkanlığı görevini “zenginleşmenin, gösterişin veya ayrıcalığın adresi” olarak görmediğini söyledi.


Ekrem İmamoğlu’nun ortakları arasında yer aldığı şirkete el konuldu


20 Mart 2025

İmamoğlu, İBB Başkanlığı döneminde de kendi aracını makam aracı olarak kullandığını ve yakıt giderlerini kendisinin karşıladığını söyledi.


İBB iştirakleri KİPTAŞ ve İGDAŞ’ın 2015 ve 2017’de birer zırhlı Mercedes S 600 aldığını anlatan İmamoğlu, bu araçları çok az kullandığını ve daha sonra satılmalarını istediğini belirtti.


İmamoğlu, Beylikdüzü dönemindeki tercihini de kamu harcamalarını azaltma amacıyla yaptığını savundu:


Bir zamanlar bu sorumluluk gereği belediyeye makam aracı kiralamamak için kendi aracımı kullanıyordum, bugün o makam aracının hesabını vermek için ne yazık ki sizin karşınızda sanık kürsüsünde, Silivri’deyim.


“Bütün siyasi tutsaklar serbest kalsın”

Kendisini ‘siyasi tutsak’ olarak tanımlamayanlara da yanıt veren İmamoğlu, “Gerçi bazıları beni siyasi tutsak olarak görmüyormuş ama bununla övünen zihniyet, ancak ve ancak özgürlüğü saraya yakınlıkla ölçen zihniyettir” dedi.

Die Sonderbehörde des Industrieländerclubs OECD empfiehlt den Mitgliedstaaten darin als Reaktion auf den Iran-Konflikt zielgerichtete Hilfen für Haushalte mit niedrigem Einkommen, da diese am stärksten von den aktuellen Energiepreisschocks getroffen würden. author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: GN ready to airlift fuel to Igloolik if needed after shipment delayed 9 days
content:
The Government of Nunavut is on hand to fly diesel up to Igloolik, but officials don’t expect it will be needed.


The hamlet’s annual resupply of fuel was initially expected to arrive Sept. 17. That shipment has been

delayed

 by nine days and now is expected to arrive Saturday.


Igloolik relies on diesel fuel for generating electricity, home heating and for the trucks that provide drinking water and sewage services. With reserves dwindling, the hamlet had asked residents to conserve water, and put the water trucks on a reduced schedule.


John Ivey, Igloolik’s senior administrative officer, said the hamlet has since lifted these restrictions after the territory assured him that the community wouldn’t be left without fuel.


The territory’s Petroleum Products Division is prepared to airlift fuel to the community if necessary, said Greg Belanger, a spokesperson for Transportation and Infrastructure Nunavut.


“The [petroleum products division] is closely monitoring inventory, and while we do not currently anticipate the need to airlift fuel, the option is available if required,” Belanger said.


The hamlet had approximately 80,000 litres of diesel fuel in its tanks as of Sept. 18, he said, an amount that should be “sufficient until resupply.”


The department did not explain why the Igloolik’s fuel shipment was delayed.

title: Migrationspakt und GEAS: Neuer Anlauf in der EU-Flüchtlingspolitik (???)
content:
Dossier


„… Die EU hadert und ringt spätestens seit der Flüchtlingskrise von 2015 mit ihren Regeln für Asyl und Migration. (…) Inzwischen hat sich die Diskussion verlagert. Wichtige Akteure wie

Bundesinnenminister Horst Seehofer (CSU) richten ihr Augenmerk stärker auf die EU-Außengrenzen

. Die Idee: Die Menschen werden schon dort einem Asylverfahren beziehungsweise einer sogenannten Vorprüfung unterzogen, die Anträge würden in beschleunigter Weise bearbeitet. Abgelehnte Bewerber würden direkt abgeschoben. Mit Blick auf die Aufnahme der übrigen Menschen, also der Schutzberechtigten, sind zudem schon lang Alternativen im Gespräch, etwa dass aufnahmeunwillige Staaten wie Ungarn Geld bezahlen. Entwicklungsländer wiederum könnten auf EU-Zahlungen hoffen, damit sie ihre Bürger schneller wieder zurücknehmen und deren Perspektiven verbessern…“


Beitrag von Phillipp Saure vom 19. Juni 2020 im Migazin


, siehe dazu nachfolgend:


100 Tage GEAS: Abschreckung, Druck und Rechtsverstöße – aber „Diese Agenda hat eine lange Tradition“ (Maximilian Pichl)


100 Tage GEAS: Abschreckung, Druck und Rechtsverstöße


„

Vor 100 Tagen, am 12. Juni 2026, ist die Neuordnung des Gemeinsamen Europäischen Asylsystems (GEAS) in der EU und in allen Mitgliedstaaten in Kraft getreten. Die 100 Tage nimmt PRO ASYL zum Anlass für eine erste Einordnung. Deutlich wird: Es geht Deutschland um maximale Härte.

In einem neuen Policy Paper zieht PRO ASYL Bilanz: Der deutsche Gesetzgeber hat die vorhandenen Spielräume weitgehend zulasten der Schutzsuchenden genutzt. Einzelne Regelungen gehen über die zwingenden Vorgaben des EU-Rechts hinaus.

„Die Erkenntnisse aus den ersten 100 Tagen GEAS sind alarmierend: Schutzsuchende werden abgeschottet, komplexe Verfolgungsgeschichten im Eiltempo geprüft und besondere Schutzbedarfe übersehen. Unabhängige Beratung fehlt, während Menschen unter haftähnlichen Bedingungen festgehalten werden. So entstehen Fehlentscheidungen und Rechtsverstöße. Das ist politisch gewollte Abschreckung“, erklärt Helen Rezene, Geschäftsführerin von PRO ASYL

…“

Pressemitteilung vom 21.09.2026

 


Feindbild Migration: „Diese Agenda hat eine lange Tradition“


„

Die Demokratie ist mehr als die Herrschaft der Mehrheit, sagt Rechtsprofessor Maximilian Pichl. Er erklärt, was sie mit Flüchtlingsschutz in Europa zu tun hat. (…)


Maximilian Pichl: Weltweit beobachten wir, wie autoritäre Akteure versuchen, Demokratie neu zu definieren: als Durchsetzung des Willens der Mehrheit. Was Demokratie konkret bedeutet, wird natürlich ständig neu ausgehandelt. Aber es ist auch nicht völlig losgelöst von der Geschichte. Und in Deutschland haben wir eine spezifische, regelbasierte Form der Demokratie in Abgrenzung zum NS-Regime. Die deutsche Demokratie begünstigt eben nicht nur eine vermeintliche Mehrheit, sondern sieht strukturelle Schutzmechanismen für Minderheiten vor. Insofern ist die Verteidigung von Flüchtlingsrechten zugleich eine Verteidigung unserer Demokratie. (…)


Die Lücke zwischen Bevölkerung und Wahlberechtigten in Deutschland driftet immer weiter auseinander. Dass die Staatsbürgerschaft immer noch der Schlüssel zur demokratischen Teilhabe ist, passt nicht in eine postmigrantische Gesellschaft. Es gibt also tatsächliche Defizite unseres demokratischen Modells – die extreme Rechte aber deutet diese völlig um. (…)


In Rostock-Lichtenhagen hat die deutsche Gesellschaft den angegriffenen Geflüchteten die Solidarität entzogen. Michel Friedman aber und Ignatz Bubis, damals Präsident des Zentralrats der Juden, fuhren an den Ort des Pogroms. Das konnten viele gar nicht begreifen. Die beiden wurden gefragt: Was habt ihr da gemacht, es waren doch gar keine Juden betroffen, sondern Geflüchtete und vietnamesische Vertragsarbeiter. Aber ihnen ging es um Solidarität. Friedman und Bubis hatten verstanden, was viele andere bis heute nicht verstehen: dass ein Angriff auf das Recht auf Schutz ein fundamentaler Angriff auf die Demokratie und die Menschenrechte aller ist. (…)


Diese populistische Debatte über Migration hat weitreichende Folgen. Auch auf Gerichte zum Beispiel. Der Europäische Gerichtshof für Menschenrechte etwa hat noch im Jahr 2012 Pushbacks von Italien nach Libyen in einer Leitentscheidung verboten. Aber seit 2015 hat sich die Rechtsprechung verändert, die Interessen der Nationalstaaten haben gegenüber den Menschenrechten Geflüchteter mehr Gewicht bekommen. Man kann aber Menschenrechte nicht einfach für eine bestimmte Gruppe relativieren …

This week on Talk World Radio we’re talking about U.S.-Iranian relations with two guests who recently visited Iran from the United States, Nuri Ronaghy and Alan Shorb.


Nuri Ronaghy was born in Iran in 1940, and has been an activist for peace for over 70 years. She came to the United States nearly 60 years ago, and got her Masters degree in Economics from the University of Wisconsin while teaching Farsi there. She has been a member of Women’s International League for Peace and Freedom, and was active in the Iranian Student Association during her student days. On a visit to Iran in the waning days of the Shah’s regime she was put into solitary confinement in the infamous Evin Prison of the Shah’s secret police, SAVAK. Nuri has been an organizing member of peace delegations to Iran both in the Fall of 2024 as well as in the Spring/Summer of 2026. During those delegations she has been a strong supporter of a school for Afghani children, refugees from the U.S. war on Afghanistan.


Alan Shorb, Nuri’s husband, was born in Baltimore in 1938. He participated in the 1963 March on Washington and peace demonstrations over the years, and in recent years has been a full-time peace activist, including being an anchor of the weekly Peace Vigil in Ojai, California for the last 11 years, and participating in the peace delegations to Iran.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: French-only election materials draw criticism from Inuit rights group
content:
An Inuit cultural organization in Nunavik is criticizing Quebec’s decision to conduct its Oct. 5 provincial election entirely in French.


On Sept.1, Élections Québec announced that election information documents, which include the guide and reminder card that will be mailed to voters, would be French-only.


The move abides with Quebec’s language law, which

became more strict

 in 2022 with the passage of Bill 96.


“Yesterday, I went to go get some mail and all I saw was French. I have no idea what it’s saying,” said William Tagoona, president of Avataq Cultural Institute.


His organization says Inuit voters will be disenfranchised if they have to navigate the provincial election in a language they don’t understand.


According to data collected in Nunavk in 2021, 8,770 out of 13,985 Indigenous respondents, or 62 per cent, reported they speak English only. A total of 1,550 respondents, or 11 per cent, reported they don’t speak English or French.


Tagoona said the decision is particularly troubling because Inuit have an exemption from certain Quebec language laws under the James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement, signed in 1975.


“Ever since elections were ever created, in provincial elections and federal elections, the ballots are not in a language that the majority of the Inuit understand,” Tagoona said. “They know very well that the majority of the Inuit don’t speak French.”


Élections Québec has asked since 2023 to be exempt from the law that forces government institutions to communication in French only. Last week, a Quebec Superior Court judge approved an emergency order for Élections Québec to mail out voter information in both English and French.


Tagoona said those materials haven’t reached his mailbox yet.


His riding, Ungava, is Quebec’s largest electoral district by geography and covers more than 855,000 square kilometres, encompassing much of northern Quebec and Nunavik. Five candidates

are running

.


“Right now if you were in Kuujjuaq, you would never know there was a provincial election,” he said. “You come to Kuujjuaq or any of our 14 villages, you won’t see one poster about any election at all.”


Tagoona would like future elections to be held in English as well as French, but seeing an Inuktitut option would be even better, he said.


Nunatsiaq News contacted Quebec’s ministry responsible for the protection of the French language for comment but has not received a response. Nunatsiaq News also reached out to Élections Québec but did not receive a response.


The Parti Québecois is leading in the polls against the Coalition Avenir Quebec, the current government. A recent Radio-Canada poll placed Parti Québecois in the lead at 29 per cent, with the Coalition Avenir Quebec at 22 per cent.


The Quebec Liberal Party is tied with the Parti conservateur du Québec, at about 19 per cent. About 12 per cent of those polled said they intend to vote for Québec solidaire, in last place.


— With files from Dominique Gené
