author: Julius Gavroche
title: Opening essay/An effort at an openning: The State, the people, the strategist
content:
from

lundimatin

 #533, 15/09/2026


This is often the case during election campaigns, and it is probably even more so given the rise of fascist tendencies: everything is put on hold – common sense, reality, boldness, autonomy, determination. Instead, people sound out the situation, calculate their moves, whisper little secrets in each other’s ears and spout posturing that rings hollow. Everyone thinks they are manipulating everyone else, but it is always reality that we are scheming with. The author of this text sets out to examine what this appetite for political manoeuvring entails. Spoiler: the very logic of a world it purports to criticise.


Every political strategy, whatever its political persuasion, is based on two key concepts: the sovereign subject and the state apparatus. Whichever side it takes, it implies intervention from the outside into the structures. Whether they aim to prevent the decline of the white race or ward off the coming of fascism, political strategies rest on the same hackneyed fiction: the political –

subject

. The fact that their aims are opposite changes nothing of their form. One hates what the other defends, but both call upon a subject to rise up, a people to count themselves, a mass to allow itself to be led. Yet there is no subject, any more than there is an object. There are compositions, decompositions, recompositions, speeds. Strategy, for its part, imposes this grammar: a subject that aims, that calculates, that stands at the forefront; an object that it names, that it fixes, that it promises. The reality is that there is no political subject standing there, before the structures it claims to be able to alter. There is a singular production of a particular context: the political subject is a fable of the modern state just as much as the modern state is an effect of this fable – each needs the other as the riverbank needs the river.


So the strategists suggest that the situation is grave, more so than before, more so than ever. That, in the name of all those whose livelihoods are under threat, we must get our hands dirty, campaign for the century-old structures of a republic that massacred our parents, grandparents and great-grandparents. “In the name of”, means that these voices have never been raised in the wake of the massacres; but from university lecterns, from lucrative chatter on Twitch, from parliamentary delegations, from publishing houses: from very specific interests whose voices are clearly heard. In this respect, whatever the objectives of the various strategies, their architectures are analogous. They share the same blind spots and perpetuate the same structures. They suggest the same modes of action, the same relationships to the world and to the masses – What should be done about those who abstain from voting? How can neighbourhoods be mobilised? Should we abandon rural areas? Thus caught up in the same fallacious representations of the State, the People and Power, strategists share the same obsession with the administration of the masses, using levers that are more or less ridiculous, increasingly paternalistic, and still far too didactic. For the State is a mode of governmentality whose fundamental axiom is separation: between subject and object, the individual and the collective, the public and the private, the political and the everyday. This separation, however fictional it may be, produces relationships and exists through them. On this basis, anything that strategically aims to take control of the state apparatus cannot claim to be anything other than a product arising from the relationships codified and distributed by the state apparatus itself, and cannot therefore bring about anything other than the continuation of those very relationships. However revolutionary the strategy may be, it delays the revolution.


What causes the normal course of events to vary is not so much the objectives we set ourselves to bring about that variation as the practice of variation itself. Adopting a mode of action characterised by procrastination, waiting for macro-political mechanisms to take effect, and faith in institutions—this

stabilises

, this

institutes

. And what establishes necessarily wards off variation: the position and those who covet it are made of the same code. That which truly varies has no position; that which has a position does not truly vary. In form, then, nothing changes from the enemy: the rally, the programme, the leader, the fervour. And …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Peregrination: Foreignness/Strangeness/Otherness as a counterpower
content:
Jörg Breu the Elder,

St. Bernard Altar: Scenes from the Life of Saint Bernard

, 1500


from

Ficcíon de la rázon

, 10/09/2026


Peregrinatio. La extrañeza como contrapoder


Federico Ferrari


We have been taken in by the hypnotic fable of the apocalypse. Public discourse, intoxicated by the spectacle of imminent ruin and by the narcissism of catastrophe, continues to tell us that we are living through the end of time. An end that drags on indefinitely, like a well-structured Netflix series in which the epilogue is always postponed to the next episode. In reality, the mass apocalyptic narrative is nothing more than a form of anaesthetic: it serves to mask the only true tragedy of the present, namely that

nothing changes

 in the great continuum of the history of oppression and that things continue to slide, without the slightest disruption, along the tracks of their political and social collapse.


However, beneath the ashes of this spectacle of ruin, something profoundly new has taken root. What we must come to terms with today, in Italy and at the heart of Europe, is not merely the continuation of the ruthless violence of classical liberalism, nor even a straightforward reproduction of the historical fascisms of the twentieth century. We have entered the era of a new authoritarian and xenophobic mindset—the principle of authority and fear of the stranger, the unfamiliar, the alien—: a post-ideological mechanism that finds its most striking global embodiment in export-oriented Trumpism.


In the face of the entrenchment of this new authoritarianism, we are witnessing, as a counterpoint, a further metamorphosis of the “aestheticisation of politics” theorised by Walter Benjamin. Whilst in the 1930s this took the form of the imposing stage-set-like displays of mass rallies, designed to sublimate the masses into a mystical body, today it manifests itself in the digital aestheticisation of the world: an uninterrupted production of images and narratives saturated with a fictional and hallucinogenic excess in which the dividing line between reality and virtuality, between truth and falsehood, becomes blurred. The masses no longer need to take to the streets to feel part of the ritual; rather, they are incorporated into a continuous virtual flow, where reality blurs into fiction and anaesthetic seduction replaces the gathering of bodies. Social anaesthesia is complete, the alienation of bodies within an empty and, above all, paralysing hyper-signifying sphere.


This defensive, possessive and identity-based authoritarianism therefore has no need for the traditional ethical state. It thrives on fragmentation, exploits the loneliness of individuals, transforms resentment into a political agenda and the fear of the “other” into a social glue. It promises false protection by fortifying borders — not only physical ones, but also psychological and identity-based ones — whilst, on a material level, it dismantles the welfare state, employment and essential rights; it thus renounces any prospect of redemption or social regeneration and is content to govern the fear of an impoverished and precarious humanity.


Faced with this stranglehold, the Leninist question re-emerges with uncompromising ferocity:

what is to be done?


The answer is dramatised by an inescapable historical fact: the political subject is missing. There exists no collective subject, no organisation, no class force on today’s political stage capable of taking the lead amongst the oppressed, of gathering the scattered suffering and transforming it into a project of rupture. The forces of the institutional left, now reduced to mere agencies for managing the status quo or to accounting guardians of the

status quo

, have lost even the basics of opposition, let alone revolutionary discourse, which is now a dead language incomprehensible to the majority.


When the subject is absent and history seems at a standstill, the greatest danger is to succumb to impotent protest, to a futile head-on collision with an adversary who draws strength precisely from direct conflict. The other danger, naturally, is a comforting retreat into the private sphere. Today, given the balance of power within society, it is not a question of opposing a blind force with a mirror-image reaction, but of understanding the need for a lateral shift: to defuse the logic of the clash endured through that austere stance which—as the late Tronti reminded us—is conveyed to us by the memory of …

content:
24/09 - 8h30 Rassemblement au parvis du stade Vélodrome


Ces 24 et 25 septembre 2026, le sommet de l'IA, sobrement titré :

The Great SHIFT – the Great Acceleration aura lieu au stade Vélodrome, à Marseille.


Ce sommet est naturellement organisé par notre petit Bolloré local – Rodolphe Saadé, et sera donc couvert par le média Brut ( racheté pour mémoire par la CMA CGM en septembre 2025 ).


Pendant deux jours, Présidents-directeurs-généraux, chef.fes de projet technophiles et penseur.euses complaisantes se succéderont sur la pelouse pour débiter la grande messe de l'IA.


Il faudrait pourtant commencer par souligner qu'« Intelligence artificielle », ça ne veut rien dire : c'est un terme marketing creux, qui désigne un ensemble de technologies disparates.


Pourtant, on croise l'Intelligence artificielle partout où on regarde, et quoi que l'on écoute.


Les entrepreneurs de la tech, quand ils ne s'attellent pas à concevoir des systèmes pour nous crever plus efficacement les yeux, ont visiblement à cœur de nous éblouir.


Pourquoi faire un sommet de l'IA et pourquoi l'ouvrir au public, tant les contournements démocratiques que s'aménage les entrepreneurs de la tech sont nombreux ?


Malgré l'indiscutable avancée majeure que constituerait l'IA, désignée comme vecteur révolutionnaire de l'humanité, il faut encore s'embarrasser d'acceptabilité sociale.


Bon sang, les gens sont cons ou quoi ?


En effet, si la France ( ce kidnapping linguistique qui désigne la classe capitaliste entrepreneuriale ) a besoin de l'IA pour faire fleurir son économie, les habitant.es de la France, elleux, ont semble-t-il besoin, pour commencer, de manger décemment, de se loger, de se soigner, d'avoir du temps, de ne pas vivre d'apocalypse climatique, et ainsi de suite. Les cons !


Ainsi, il va falloir urgemment convaincre ces rétifves de monter à bord du train de l'IA.


À ce sujet, nous, ( les rétifves ) n'avons de toute façon pas de billet.


Les agent conversationnels tiennent nos solitude en embuscade, les nourrissent et les encadrent ;


Les outils opérationnels vident le travail de sa substance ( déjà peu reluisante à maints égards ), et capturent les savoirs-faire,


Et les entrepreneurs de la tech, quand ils s'expriment par la bouche des décideurs publics, ont remplacé


Nous allons autoritairement imposer massivement ces usages


par

Il faut que les gens comprennent, il faut absolument travailler sur l'acceptabilité sociale.


Chacun, chacune, portant religieusement sa petite pierre à l'édifice de mystification générale.


Ceux qui vont pontifier au Vélodrome sont rompus à la prestidigitation :


 Tout mettre en œuvre pour faire advenir ce qu'on nous présentera comme étant déjà là

 Effrayer le quidam par la puissance du progrès ( doit-on craindre un cyber-armaggedon ? ) tout en affirmant être à la pointe de l'innovation dudit progrès

 Masquer l'avancée réelle de nouvelles technologies de guerre, de surveillance, de gestion des frontières.

 Marteler la nécessité d'une souveraineté numérique de la France, tout en ne signalant pas que ses infrastructures – des datacenters en folle expansion – sont la propriété de multinationales états-uniennes, qui fonctionnent avec des puces produites à Taiwan, lesquelles sont construites avec des métaux extraits au prix du sang en RDC, qui compilent des données annotées par des travailleureuses exploitées à Madagascar, au Kenya, et dont les serveurs, qui jouissent d'une durée de fonctionnement approximative de 3 à 4 ans, finissent illégalement dans les immenses décharges à ciel ouvert au Ghana.


L'IA n'a rien de souverain – le néocolonialisme, lui, l'est bel et bien. Cocori- splash.

title: Guerrilla commander Dîlan Şirnex laid to rest in Qandil
content:
Earlier today, the Party of Free Women of Kurdistan (PAJK) announced the death of guerrilla commander Dîlan Şirnex. According to the statement, Şirnex died on September 17 while undergoing cancer treatment. She joined the PKK in 1994 and, according to PAJK, was one of the leading commanders involved in building the autonomous women’s organization.


Masses bid farewell to the female commander at the Mehmet Karasungur Martyrs’ Cemetery in Binarê Qandil. Local residents and many patriots attended the ceremony.


Addressing the crowd on behalf of PJAK, Sozdar Dilsoz said that Dîlan Şirnex became acquainted with the struggle and joined the Freedom Movement as a guerrilla fighter at a young age.


Dilsoz said that Şirnex joined the struggle without hesitation and with great enthusiasm, adding: “Martyr Dîlan served both as a commander of the women’s forces and as a representative of the women’s movement, struggling in all parts of Kurdistan and across every inch of the country. That is why she fought with great passion until her last breath.”


Stating that the martyrs raised awareness among the people, educated them, and organized them through their struggle, Dilsoz added: “She fought continuously until the day she fell as a martyr. To defend the Rojava Revolution, she fought in Tabqa and Raqqa until the end of the war in Rojava.”


Dîlan Şirnex’s brother, Selîm Ebdulrehman, also spoke at the ceremony. Stating that the path of the martyrs was also their path, Ebdulrehman said: “We express our condolences to Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan) and our patriotic people. We hope that these lands will be liberated and Leader Apo will gain his freedom.”


Following speeches, Dîlan Şirnex was laid to rest amid chants of “Şehîd Namirin” (Martyrs are immortal).

author: Unknown
title: Tanrısı savaş olan bir dünya: Kan Meridyeni
content:
Cormac McCarthy’nin 1985 tarihli romanı “Kan Meridyeni’’, geçtiğimiz ağustos ayında ilk defa Türkçeye çevrildi. Yazarın “İhtiyarlara Yer Yok’’ ve “Yol’’ gibi romanları daha önce yayınlanmış ama en az onlar kadar çok tartışılan ve pek çokları için Amerikan edebiyatının en iyi romanlarından olan Kan Meridyeni ise okurla buluşmamıştı. Bahsi geçen diğer romanlarının çok başarılı klasikleşmiş filmleri bulunmakta ancak Kan Meridyeni birkaç defa niyetlenilmesine rağmen hiçbir zaman beyaz perdeye taşınmamış. Kitabın şimdi Türkçeye çevrilmesinin sebebi olarak son yıllarda internette bir tartışma konusu haline gelmesi ve hakkında sayısız içerik üretilmesi dolayısıyla Türkiyeli okurlar tarafından da talep edilmesini gösterebiliriz. Şimdiye kadar yayınlanmama sebeplerinden biri çevirisinin zorluğu olabilir. McCarthy noktalama işaretlerini çok az kullanmasıyla meşhur bir yazar. Parantez ve tırnak işaretleri romanda yok; virgülü de mecbur değilse kullanmıyor, onun yerine “ve’’ bağlacıyla cümleyi uzatıyor. Daha olası bir sebep ise kitabın içerdiği şiddet oranı. Peşinen söyleyeyim, bu kitabı çoğu arkadaşıma tavsiye edemem. Belli bir yaşın altındaki arkadaşlarımızın ise asla okumamaları gerekiyor. Kitapta neredeyse her sayfadasında ayrı bir şiddet olayı yaşanıyor. Tek sorun şiddet de değil, bu romanda ‘iyi karakter’ yok. İyilik diye tarif edebileceğimiz tek eylem kitabın başlarında bir kere isimsiz karakterler tarafından yapılıyor, o da toplamda eserin yüzde birini bile oluşturmuyor. Ne zaman bir cinayet işlense bütün görgü tanıkları olayı izlemekle yetiniyorlar. Okur da tıpkı onlar gibi, sayfalar ilerledikçe artık bu şiddete ve gaddarlığa karşı hassasiyetini yitiriyor.

Birbirleriyle çatışsalar da yerli halka soykırım ortak fikirleri

Bu eserin türünü tanımlamak için eleştirmenler tarafından “Amerikan batısına karşıt” anlamına gelen “anti-western’’ terimi kullanılıyor. (Bu doğu taraftarı oldukları anlamına gelmiyor) Roman, “antisi’’ olduğu türün yaygın olduğu dönemde ve o coğrafyada geçmesine rağmen klasik ‘western’lerde bulunan kahramanlık, dindarlık, medeniyet gibi bütün değerleri tersyüz ediyor. Roman boyunca takip ettiğimiz isimsiz ‘çocuk’; evinden kaçıp ABD’nin çeşitli yerlerinde kısa süreli işlerde çalışıp birkaç şiddet olayına karışmasının ardından, kısa süreliğine bir paralı asker bölüğüne dahil olur ve sonrasında kendini Glanton Çetesiyle bulur. 1840’larda gerçekten ABD-Meksika sınırında terör estirmiş olan John Glanton ve Çetesi, başta Amerikan yerlileri olmak üzere bütün sivil halka karşı uyguladıkları vahşetle; Komancheler, Apacheler gibi yerli kabilelerle olan çatışmalarıyla bilinirler. Geçimlerini olabilecek en aşağılık şekilde sağlarlar: İnsanların kafa derilerini ABD ve Meksika hükümetlerine satarak. (1837 yılında Meksika’nın Chihuahua eyaleti, her Apache kafa derisi başına ödül koydu. Her erkek kafa derisi için 100 peso, her kadın için 50, her çocuk için 25 peso. Bulduğum örneklerin sadece biri.) Görüyoruz ki, 1846-1848 yılları arasında savaşmış ve kitabın geçtiği dönemde ise hem birbiriyle hem kendi içlerinde çatışma halinde olan bu iki devlet; bölgenin gerçek halkının soykırımı konusunda birbirleriyle aynı politikayı izliyorlardı.

Yazar üzerinde oturduğu mirasın özeleştirisini veriyor

Glanton Çetesi’ni incelediğimizde ise saçtıkları vahşeti saf sadistik ve ırkçı güdülerle uygulamadıklarını görüyoruz, bunlar ne kadar önemli bir rol oynasalar da. Haydutluk yoluyla biriktirdikleri metayı daha yüksek fiyata satabilmek için sürekli yer değiştiriyorlar, rekabetin daha az olduğu alanlara gidiyorlar, muhasebe ve iş bölümü yapıyorlar, işverenlerinin kendilerinden istediği kafa derisi kotasını dolduramadılarsa yerli olmayan insanları da öldürüyorlar. Bütün bu şiddetin iktisadi sebepleri kitap boyunca ayrıntılarıyla veriliyor.

Cormac McCarthy, romanı yazdığı yaklaşık 10 yıllık süreçte tarihi belgelerden ve çetenin gerçek üyelerinden biri olan Samuel Chamberlain’in otobiyografisinden yararlanmış, bahsettiği bölgelerde uzun zaman geçirmiş. Bunlara dayanarak emperyalist yayılmacılığın, ulus mitinin ve soykırımcılığın çirkin gerçek yüzünü kitabında ortaya koyuyor. Yani, beyaz bir adam olarak üstüne oturduğu mirasın ve geçmişin özeleştirisini veriyor.

Kan Meridyeni, Marksist bir okuma için bol bol malzeme verdiği halde, romanın sosyalist bir mesaj verdiğini iddia etmek imkânsız. Yazar, “İhtiyarlara Yer Yok” kitabında da yaptığı gibi, ‘kötülük’, ‘iktidar’, ‘şiddet’ gibi kavramları metafizik ve mutlak unsurlar olarak ele …

author: Unknown
title: Ailenin ve çocukların korunmasına yönelik politikalar gerçekte kimi kimden koruyor?
content:
Ailenin ve çocukların korunması söylemiyle hayata geçirilen politikalar; masum bir sosyal refah iddiasının çok ötesinde, bireyleri korumaktan ziyade toplumsal yaşam üzerindeki denetimi meşrulaştıran ve özellikle genç kadınların yaşam alanlarını daraltan birer araç olarak karşımıza çıkıyor. Mevcut sisteme hizmet eden gelenekselleşmiş aile yapısı; kadınları eve kapatan, onları ev içi hizmetlere mahkûm eden, çocuk bakımı sorumluluğunu büyük ölçüde kadınların omuzlarına yükleyen ve kız çocuklarının üniversitelere giderek yeterli donanıma ulaşıp bu yapıyı bozmasını engellemeye çalışan baskıcı bir mekanizma üretmektedir. Gelenekselleşmiş yapılar; kız çocuklarının özgürleşmesine ve kendi ayakları üzerinde durmasına karşı çıkmaktadır. Bu baskıcı iklim yalnızca aile içinde kalmamakta, devlet politikaları aracılığıyla günlük yaşamın her alanına yayılmaktadır. Gençlerin dinlediği müzik gruplarından sosyal medyada izledikleri videolara, sanat üretiminden kişilerin kendini ve kimliklerini kamusal alanda ifade etme biçimlerine kadar pek çok alan denetim altına alınmaya çalışılmaktadır. Son dönemde “müstehcenlik” suçu ve “ahlak” maskesi altında yürütülen gözaltı ve tutuklama dalgaları da bu politikaların önemli bir parçasıdır. Sanatçıların ve influencerların hedef gösterilmesi, özellikle kadınların görünürlüğünün kriminalize edilmesi ve farklı yaşam biçimlerinin “ahlaka aykırı” olarak sunulması, ahlakın nasıl bir siyasal denetim aracına dönüştürüldüğünü göstermektedir. Bu durumun güncel örneklerinden biri Manifest grubuna açılan davaydı. Grubun sahne performansındaki danslar ve sahne hareketleri gündem olmuş, bunun hakkında “müstehcenlik” ve “hayasızca hareketler” kapsamında soruşturma başlatılmıştı. Bu olaydan bir süre sonra Manifest grubunun kurucusu ve menajeri Tolga Akış gözaltına alınmış, “müstehcen yayınların yayımlanmasına aracılık etmek” suçlamasıyla tutuklama talebiyle mahkemeye sevk edilerek tutuklanmıştı. Aynı dönemde “müstehcen içerik” gerekçesiyle sosyal medya kullanıcılarına ve kamuoyunca tanınan isimlere yönelik operasyonların gündeme gelmesi, yaşananların münferit birkaç olaydan ibaret olmadığını göstermektedir. Bu nedenle “müstehcenlik” üzerinden kurulan cezalandırma mekanizmasını yalnızca hukuki bir kategori olarak değerlendirmek yetersizdir. Bedenlerin, arzuların ve sanatsal ifadelerin “genel ahlak” kavramına uymadığı gerekçesiyle cezalandırılması; iktidarın toplumsal yaşamı kendi ideolojik ihtiyaçları doğrultusunda yeniden biçimlendirme araçlarından biridir.

Burada mesele yalnızca belli içeriklerin “müstehcen” ilan edilmesi ya da belirli kişilerin cezalandırılması değildir. Asıl mesele; insanların nasıl giyineceğine, kimle ilişki kurabileceğine, hangi yaşam biçimini tercih edebileceğine ve kamusal alanda nasıl var olabileceğine ilişkin sınırların iktidar tarafından yeniden çizilmesidir. Sosyal medyanın milyonlarca insanın kendi bedenini, yaşamını ve kimliğini görünür kıldığı bir alan haline gelmesiyle birlikte bu denetim ihtiyacı dijital alana da taşınmaktadır. Böylece kamusal görünürlük yalnızca politik düşüncelerin ifade edilmesi üzerinden değil; kadının nasıl giyindiği, hangi davranışların “uygun” bulunduğu ve hangi cinsellik biçimlerinin görünür olabileceği üzerinden de düzenlenmektedir.

Ahlak politikaları ve makbul kadınlığın inşası

Bir kadın ne zaman iyi, doğru veya makbul kabul edilir? Kendi hayatı hakkında karar verdiğinde mi, yoksa ona biçilen rolü kabul ettiğinde mi? Yıllarca bize “İyi bir kız ailesini üzmez, çok iddialı giyinmez, saçını rengârenk boyamaz, geç saatte dışarıda durmaz ve gerekli yaşa geldiğinde evlenip yuvasını kurar, çocuklarına annelik yapar” sözleriyle bir kalıp dayatıldı. Artık bugün genç kadınların bu kalıpları reddetmeye başladığını söyleyebiliriz. Olmak istedikleri kişinin başkasının dayattığı kalıplarla sınırlı olmadığını; aksine kendi ayakları üzerinde durabilen, kararlarını kendi veren, üzerindeki baskıyı kabul etmeyen ve bu düzene karşı duran bütün kadınlar olduğunu biliyorlar. Eğer sistem onları bu tanımla kabul etmiyorsa, genç kadınlar makbul kadın tanımını kendileri yeniden yazmalıdır.

Manifest örneğinde olduğu gibi bir kadının dans etmesi veya geleneksel kadınlık normlarına uymayan bir görünüm sergilemesi; “topluma kötü örnek olmak”, “gençleri bozmak” ya da “ahlaka aykırı davranmak” gibi suçlamalarla karşılaşabilmektedir. Mabel Matiz’in sanatsal üretiminin hedef alınması ve LGBTİ+’ların kamusal görünürlüğü üzerinden yürütülen tartışmalar da bu açıdan tesadüfi değildir …

author: Unknown
title: 34 years ago, the killing of Musa Anter
content:
Musa Anter, affectionately known as “Apê Musa” (Uncle Musa), was a prominent Kurdish writer who contributed columns to the daily Özgür Gündem and the weekly Yeni Ülke. He was shot and killed in Diyarbakır on 20 September 1992.


Lured from his hotel by a telephone caller who asked him to help settle a property dispute, Anter and a friend set off in a taxi with an unknown man, described as between 25 and 30 years old. When they began to suspect that a trap was being set, they demanded to get out of the taxi. The man accompanying them also got out and, having walked in front of them, began shooting at them with a gun.


Anter was struck by four bullets and died soon afterward. The friend, hit by two bullets, was seriously injured. Amnesty International reported that a 14-shot 9 mm gun was used in the attack, which the group says occurred on the outskirts of the city near a police station and a manned traffic control point.


Anter, who did not live in Diyarbakır, was visiting the city to sign books during a cultural festival. A previously unknown group, Boz-Ok, claimed responsibility for the killing, but editors at Yeni Ülke and Özgür Gündem discounted the claim, blaming the state and counter-guerrillas.


Born in 1920 in the village of Zivingê in Nusaybin, Anter experienced many things during his lifetime that others knew only by hearsay. He experienced the founding years of the Turkish Republic, the uprising of Sheikh Said and the genocide in Dersim as a schoolboy, and the Second World War as a student.


He was one of the protagonists of the short spring of the Kurdish national movement at the end of the 1950s; in the "Trial of 49" he was accused of Kurdish propaganda and separatism. The background was his poem Qimil (Weevil), which he had published in Kurdish in the magazine Ileri Yurt in August 1959. The magazine, based in Diyarbakir, was again the first magazine in decades to deal with the Kurdish question. Musa Anter was the editor.


Abdülkadir Aygan, a former PKK militant turned informant and recruited by JITEM (the Turkish Gendarmerie's Intelligence and Counter-terrorism Service), said he had been part of a JITEM unit, along with a "Hamit" from Şırnak, who had assassinated Musa Anter.


Turkey was found guilty of Anter's murder in 2006 by the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) and sentenced to a fine of 28,500 euros.


In 2009, 17 years after the murder, Turkish prosecutors reopened the case following Aygan’s 2004 interview in which he confessed to being involved in Anter’s killing. In 2010, the case was merged with two other trials

 

involving

 

several alleged JİTEM members, including Aygan, as defendants. The merged trial started to be known as the “main JİTEM trial” (as there were others). Turkey’s military confirmed the unofficial existence of the JİTEM as a temporary intelligence unit from 1988 to 1990 that was made official before being disbanded in 2001, a trial memo said. 


Hamit Yıldırım, whom Aygan accused of being the gunman, was arrested in Turkey in 2012 but released in 2017, when the legal limit for a person to be held without conviction

 

was reached.


The trial was transferred from Diyarbakır to Ankara in 2015 for security reasons.


Anter’s murder case, or the “main JİTEM trial,” was dropped by the sixth Ankara Court of Serious Crimes on September 21, 2022, due to the statute of limitations.


Nearly four years after the case was dismissed due to the statute of limitations, the family of Musa Anter has filed a request to reopen the case in August 2026.


Rahşan Yorozlu, Anter’s daughter, submitted the application through her lawyer Bişar Abdi Alinak to the Department for the Investigation of Unsolved Crimes at the Turkish Ministry of Justice. The aim is to reopen the proceedings, which were dismissed in 2022 due to the statute of limitations. The application calls for a comprehensive reassessment of the case and further investigations to ensure that all those responsible for the killing are held criminally accountable.


In the application, the family requests that previously omitted investigative measures be carried out and that all evidence collected in the case be reexamined using current forensic and criminal investigation techniques. The applicants also demand a full clarification of the crime and investigations into everyone involved throughout the chain of command. The stated objective is to fully establish the circumstances of the murder and determine the criminal …

title: PAJK announces the death of guerrilla commander Dîlan Şirnex
content:
The Party of Free Women of Kurdistan (PAJK) has announced the death of guerrilla commander Dîlan Şirnex. Born in 1977 in the province of Şırnak in Northern Kurdistan (Bakur), she died on September 17 while undergoing cancer treatment. She joined the PKK in 1994 and, according to PAJK, was one of the leading commanders involved in building the autonomous women’s organization.


The PAJK obituary on Sunday reads as follows:


“In the Kurdish people’s and women’s struggle for their existence, the stance of our fallen comrades for a free life and their struggle have left indelible marks on historical memory. The courageous children of Kurdistan stood against the policies of denial, assimilation and genocide directed against our people and joined the freedom movement. Convinced that the path to a dignified and sincere life lay in taking part in the struggle within the ranks of the guerrilla, they continued their journey toward freedom.


As Kurdish women became increasingly aware of the effects of colonialism and the patriarchal system of domination, they joined the ranks of the freedom struggle in ever greater numbers. They felt the spirit of freedom created by Rêber Apo [Abdullah Öcalan], developed their consciousness, and became the driving force behind a powerful awakening. Rêber Apo became a light and a source of hope for every woman seeking freedom and equality.


Like Kurdish women from all parts of Kurdistan, the women of Botan joined the freedom struggle with great courage, commitment, self-sacrifice, and a deep attachment to their homeland. Botan is a historical center of patriotism and resistance. The struggle, resistance, and devotion to their homeland that the women of Botan brought into the ranks of the freedom movement played a pioneering role in reviving national consciousness throughout Kurdistan and in the development of the uprisings.


The struggle of the women of Botan has thus made a decisive contribution to keeping the tradition of freedom and resistance alive in Kurdistan. Our comrade Dîlan Şirnex, who carried within her the spirit of resistance of Botan and devoted her life to the freedom struggle, continued this resistance for 32 years with great dedication and self-sacrifice and fell as a martyr. As comrades of Dîlan, who was among the leading commanders in the establishment of our women’s army, we extend our condolences to her esteemed family, our entire people, and especially the patriotic people of Botan. At the same time, we renew our pledge to achieve our goal and reunite with Rêber Apo.


Personal details of our fallen comrade Dîlan Şirnex:


Nom de Guerre: Dîlan Şirnex


First and last name: Rabia Barınç


Year and place of birth: 1977, Şırnak


Parents’ names: Zeliha – Abdurrahman


Date of participation: 1994, Zakho


Date of death: September 17, 2026


Our comrade Dîlan was born in Botan in 1977 and grew up there. She embraced the pioneering role and the resistant and combative character of the people of Botan and remained deeply connected to her roots. Every Kurdish woman felt profound anger and conviction in the face of the attacks of the capitalist system, which enslaves women, strips them of meaning, and confines them within four walls. Dîlan, too, learned from the women of Botan, and especially from her mother, that she could achieve anything through her own strength. She therefore insisted on a free life and deepened her search for it day by day.


Although she was still very young, she had a strong sense of responsibility and a profound desire to seek a different life. Even as a child, she was confronted with attacks aimed at destroying the Kurdish people, who were struggling for their existence on their ancestral lands. In the 1990s, the Kurdish freedom struggle developed under the leadership of Rêber Apo raised hopes for freedom in Botan, as it did throughout Kurdistan. With the PKK, a kind of rebirth began. Rêber Apo and the PKK became a place of freedom where the Kurdish people and women sought guidance.


The Turkish state therefore intensified its policies of denial and destruction, burning villages and attempting to extinguish hopes for freedom through massacres. Dîlan’s family was among those forced to flee to Zakho in Southern Kurdistan in 1992 as a result of these attacks. title: Eva Maria Michelmann: Solidarity freed me, and we will free Ahmet too
content:
German journalist Eva Maria Michelmann spoke in Zurich about her abduction in Raqqa and her subsequent five-month detention in prisons run by the Syrian transitional government. At an event held at the Autonomous School, she also described the final days she spent with her colleague and partner Ahmet Polad and their forcible separation. Polad, whose legal name is Mehmet Nizam Aslan, was transferred to Turkey on September 9 after nearly eight months of detention in Syria. Following his transfer, the Kurdish journalist was placed in pre-trial detention and taken to Metris Prison in Istanbul.


The event was organized by the “Freedom for Eva and Ahmet” initiative, which initially campaigned for the release of both journalists and has continued its work on behalf of Polad since Michelmann’s release in June.


Trapped in a youth center


Michelmann and Polad were in Raqqa in January to report on developments during the Syrian transitional government’s offensive against the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (DAANES). They had also anticipated possible attacks by sleeper cells of the “Islamic State” (ISIS) and had therefore remained in the city. As the military situation escalated, Michelmann said that a neighborhood predominantly inhabited by displaced people from Afrin was surrounded. Between 30 and 70 people sought shelter in a youth center, including Michelmann and Polad.


The people were trapped there for several days, while their calls for help went unanswered. After a diesel tank on the roof was hit, two floors of the building could no longer be used. The ground floor also repeatedly came under attack, leaving those inside eventually trapped on the first floor. Armed men ultimately entered the building and separated Michelmann and Polad. More than 30 people were then taken to the rear of the building. However, when a bus later arrived, Michelmann said she saw only 14 people board it. “I counted them one by one. I asked then, and I ask again today: What happened to these people?”


Separated from Polad and taken to Aleppo


Michelmann said that she did not see Polad again after their arrest. She was initially taken to the building of the so-called Internal Security in Aleppo, where she was repeatedly interrogated and tortured. Over the following months, she was transferred between several prisons and cells in Aleppo, Idlib, and Damascus. Michelmann repeatedly pointed out that she was a German citizen and demanded that the German diplomatic mission be notified. Her guards responded: “No one is asking about you.”


“I was freed through solidarity”


Michelmann was released on June 19 after 152 days in detention and returned to Germany. The journalist attributes her release largely to public pressure and solidarity efforts outside the prisons. “If I am here today, it is because of the struggle that was waged outside. I am free now, but many people are still being held in those places of torture. Solidarity is important. That is why I will continue to fight.”


Baki Selçuk of the initiative recalled that during the months when there was no reliable information about Michelmann and Polad, protests and other actions were organized outside institutions including the German Foreign Office, Syrian diplomatic missions, and the United Nations. Following Michelmann’s release, the initiative announced that it would continue its work as long as Polad remained in Syrian custody. At the time, his family and legal representatives had explicitly warned against a possible transfer to Turkey. That transfer ultimately took place on September 9. “Our task now will be to secure his freedom,” Selçuk said in Zurich. “For that, it is very important that the solidarity continues.”


“Why didn’t we defend the women’s struggle in Rojava?”


During the discussion that followed, Michelmann was also asked about political developments in Rojava and the agreement between the Autonomous Administration and the Syrian central government. Michelmann placed the women’s revolution at the center of her response: “There is a unique women’s struggle in Rojava. Even if you bomb this place, women around the world know about it. Women will never forget it.” Before discussing the decisions of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), she said, the question should instead be asked why the international public had largely remained silent in the face of the attacks on Rojava. “Rojava is unprecedented in the world. There is no other example like …

title: Burial site containing remains of ISIS genocide victims opened in Shengal
content:
In Shengal, Iraqi forensic experts have opened a burial site containing the remains of victims of the ISIS genocide. The exhumation near the Şerfedîn Shrine began in the presence of relatives with a religious ceremony conducted according to Yazidi rites and has been ongoing for around ten days. According to Iraqi authorities, the remains of 76 people are believed to be buried in the area. However, earlier figures regarding the number of people buried at the site differ.


Buried before identification was completed


The remains were recovered from mass graves discovered in the Xanesor (Khanasor) area after Shengal was liberated from the “Islamic State” (ISIS). In 2016, KDP authorities in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq had the remains exhumed and subsequently reburied in the Şerfedîn area, even though the necessary DNA testing had not yet been completed.


Relatives who still had no certainty about the fate of their missing family members subsequently called for the burial site to be reopened. After years of efforts, Iraq’s Directorate for Mass Graves and Missing Persons and the forensic authorities began the exhumation work.


The bones now being recovered will be taken for forensic examination. DNA samples will be collected and compared with those of relatives in order to identify the victims.


Numerous mass graves still unopened


So far, 96 mass graves containing victims of the ISIS genocide have been registered in Shengal. According to the Autonomous Council of Shengal, 77 of them have been opened, while another 19 have yet to be examined. The identification of the recovered remains is progressing slowly. Hundreds of sets of human remains are still awaiting identification, while numerous Yazidi families, even twelve years after the genocide, still have no certainty about the fate of their relatives.


Background


In the summer of 2014, ISIS overran large parts of Iraq. On August 3 of that year, the jihadist militia committed genocide and femicide in the Yazidi main settlement area of Shengal (Sinjar), west of Mosul. Through systematic massacres, rape, torture, expulsion, enslavement of girls and women, and the forced recruitment of boys as child soldiers, the Yazidi community experienced the 74th genocide in its history.


According to recent estimates, around 10,000 people fell victim to the ISIS massacres, and more than 400,000 others were driven from their homes. Over 7,000 women and children were abducted, and around 2,500 of them are still missing today.


Only with the help of a dozen guerrilla fighters from the PKK were hundreds of thousands of people saved from certain death or enslavement. Reinforcements from the HPG (People’s Defense Forces) and YJA Star (Free Women’s Troops) then moved out of the Kurdistan mountains. Together with the YPG (People’s Defense Units) and YPJ (Women’s Defense Units), a corridor of escape to Rojava was created. Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and Shengal Women's Units (YJŞ) were formed, and the region was liberated step by step. In January 2015, an autonomous council was proclaimed. On 31 October 2015, an offensive began to liberate the villages in the west of the city of Shengal, and on 13 November 2015, ISIS was completely driven out of the region.


After the liberation of the city, the HPG and YPG/YPJ subsequently withdrew in 2017. People who returned to their land after Shengal's independence reformed, established defensive units and built their institutions.


The fate of thousands of Yazidis, especially women, remains unknown. Many were sold in slave markets established by ISIS in cities such as Raqqa, Mosul, Deir ez-Zor, and Al-Bukamal. SDF forces have successfully liberated thousands of them, reuniting them to their families in Shengal.


Countless victims of the ISIS massacres in the city were buried in mass graves. Although the Iraqi government began opening mass graves in 2019, many have yet to be opened. Several families are still waiting for the work to begin so they can get back the remains of their loved ones.


According to a recent statement by Iraq’s Ministry of Migration and Displacement, more than 30,000 people have returned to Shengal so far. Around 19,000 families, the majority of them Yazidi citizens, are still living in a total of 16 camps in Hewlêr (Erbil) and Duhok.

title: Musa Anter commemorated on the 34th anniversary of his murder in Amed
content:
Kurdish writer and journalist Musa Anter was commemorated in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) on Sunday. The commemoration took place at the site in the Seyrantepe district where the intellectual, known as Apê (Uncle) Musa, was shot dead on September 20, 1992. The memorial event, organized by the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG), was attended by Anter’s relatives, media workers, and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations.


Anter’s murder is among the most widely known political crimes of the 1990s. The Susurluk Report, later prepared on behalf of the Turkish prime minister, contained extensive information about the activities of state-backed structures and linked Anter’s murder to Mahmut Yıldırım, alias “Yeşil,” and the military intelligence organization JITEM. A full judicial reckoning with the case has yet to take place.


“For peace, the political murders must be solved”


DFG member Fexredin Kılıç stated that even 34 years after Anter’s death, the structures behind the murder have still not been fully exposed. Referring to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, he called for the political murders of the 1990s to be investigated. “In these days when we are talking about peace, we say it once again at the place where Apê Musa was murdered: For there to be peace, the unresolved political murders must be solved.”


Anter’s murder, he said, was not directed solely against a journalist but against bringing the social reality of the Kurdish people to the public. Even after his death, Kılıç noted, members of the free Kurdish press were killed, imprisoned, detained, and threatened; newsrooms were bombed and media outlets banned. In this context, Kılıç commemorated the slain journalists Nagihan Akarsel, Gulistan Tara, Cihan Bilgin, and Nazım Daştan, saying: “The free press has not bowed down and will not bow down. We will continue to write the truth, defend the truth, and carry the voices of the peoples to the world.”


From Apê Musa to Hüseyin Aykol


DFG Co-Chair Selman Çiçek commemorated journalist Hüseyin Aykol, a longtime companion of the Kurdish press, who died on January 1 this year. Despite his age and health problems, Çiçek said, Aykol regularly attended the commemoration in recent years. “Perhaps we did not have the chance to know Apê Musa ourselves. But today we are here as students of Hüseyin, who was shaped by Apê Musa. We learned a great deal from Hüseyin. From Apê Musa to Hüseyin, from Hüseyin to us, and from us to the next generations, we will carry this tradition forward.”


Musa Anter’s son, Dicle Anter, pledged to continue keeping his father’s memory alive at the site where he was killed: “Thirty-four years have passed since Apê Musa was murdered. But we will come here every year and commemorate him.”


Mızraklı: Truth and accountability are indispensable


Former Amed Co-Mayor Adnan Selçuk Mızraklı recalled that Anter’s significance extended far beyond his role as a pioneer of the Kurdish press. “Apê Musa was not only a founding figure and guiding force of the Kurdish press. He left behind a great legacy for all Kurds and all people.” Mızraklı pointed to the many young journalists who continue Anter’s work today. At the same time, he linked Anter’s legacy to the issue of confronting and addressing state crimes.


“Especially in the context of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, uncovering the truth and confronting it are indispensable if peace is to be deepened and a dignified peace established. If those who murdered Apê Musa are still walking free somewhere today, then justice remains incomplete. Without justice, there can be no genuine peace.”


“Today there are thousands of Musa Anters”


Mızraklı also recalled a meeting of the Human Rights Association (IHD) in the early 1990s, where politician Vedat Aydın, who was also killed by JITEM in 1991, delivered a speech in Kurdish. Musa Anter had been sitting behind him. “I remember Apê Musa’s proud stance during that speech—a stance that said: We exist through our language, our culture, and what we have created.” Today, he said, this legacy has long since been embraced by a new generation: “Today there are thousands of Musa Anters. We have thousands of young people who write fearlessly with the pen he left behind and pick up their cameras even in the most difficult moments.”


The necessary process of reckoning, he added, extends far beyond Anter’s murder. Mızraklı drew a line from the state crimes of the 1990s …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Estados Unidos: la centralidad de la tasa de interés
content:
La incertidumbre domina el escenario, nadie sabe cuándo terminará la guerra ya perdida, ¿la suba de la tasa de interés devendrá en una crisis económica o será expresión de que la economía irá al alza?


El presidente de la Reserva Federal, Jerome Powell. Foto: Anna Moneymaker, Getty Images


Finalmente la Reserva Federal de EEUU resolvió subir la tasa de interés de referencia, algo que no sucedía desde 2023. Desoye así las exigencias de Donald Trump que pedía bajarlas. Es una expresión de las complejidades económicas que atraviesa el imperio estadounidense. Complica la toma de deuda en nuestro país.


En una entrega anterior me preguntaba si la Reserva Federal subiría las tasas de referencia, cuando Trump presionaba para que las baje y así estimular el crecimiento económico, la incógnita se reveló este miércoles. La FED (el banco central estadounidense) resolvió por unanimidad una suba de 25 puntos básicos llevándola al rango de 3.75 – 4.0, con lo que afirma una política monetaria más restrictiva, que según el comunicado oficial sería duradera. Hasta ahora la tasa se encontraba en un rango de 3,50% a 3,75% y no se movía desde hace tres años. Sin embargo en las proyecciones de la FED esta decisión no afectaría las tasas de empleo ni del crecimiento del PBI.


Para varios analistas el aumento de las tasas de interés, que es un fenómeno global que está afectando a casi todos los países, tiene que ver con el aumento de la inflación mundial, las necesidades de endeudamiento (que compiten con el aumento de la inversión del capital privado en IA), y la incertidumbre electoral. En estos días debiera agregarse el debate por la regulación de la IA y la desaceleración de la inversión en ese campo.


La inflación


La semana anterior se informó que el índice de inflación de agosto arrojó un incremento del 0.4 mensual, lo que acumulado significa una suba interanual del 3.4%, muy alejada del 2% considerado normal.


La inflación viene en ascenso en el mundo desde los días posteriores a la pandemia, impulsada por los aumentos en los costos de las materias primas y el transporte. Sin embargo en la coyuntura inmediata el alza en EEUU es un resultado directo de la aventura militar en Medio Oriente, a la que Trump fue arrastrado por Netanyahu y a la que no le encuentra salida.


Donald Trump y Benjamin Netanyahu en el aeropuerto Ben Gurion en Tel Aviv. Foto: Chip Somodevilla


La guerra provocó la suba de las cotizaciones del petróleo, que impactó fuerte en el precio de los combustibles, subieron más de un 40% desde fines de febrero pasado cuando EEUU e Israel iniciaron los ataques a Irán. Estas cotizaciones volvieron a tensionarse en estos días cuando se conoció que el paso naval de Bad el Mandeb, una ruta alternativa al Estrecho de Ormuz bajo control iraní, quedó bajo control de los hutíes, aliados de los persas. Además Arabia Saudita informó que por ataques de drones desde Irak, cerró preventivamente el oleoducto Este-Oeste. que va desde los principales yacimientos petroleros hasta el Mar Rojo. El barril cotiza ahora por arriba de los 100 dólares.


La deuda


Hace un par de semanas se conoció que la deuda pública de EEUU alcanzó el nivel histórico de 40 billones de dólares (más del 120% del PBI). El grueso de esta deuda está originado en el extraordinario déficit del comercio exterior, especialmente con China, que el Tesoro de EEUU financia con la emisión de bonos. La carga de los intereses de estos bonos va al presupuesto y alimenta el déficit fiscal, a lo que hay que adicionar los recortes impositivos y el aumento de los gastos militares que de conjunto pudieron más que los mayores ingresos por los nuevos aranceles y los recortes en la administración pública. El resultado es que el déficit fiscal trepó al 5.8% del PBI, lejos del objetivo inicial del 3%. que obviamente se financia con más deuda, que así crece a razón de 7.000 millones diarios y se torna casi inmanejable. Sumados al déficit federal, el de los estados más la seguridad social, el déficit general supera el 7.6% del producto.


Donald Trump habla con Jerome Powell durante un recorrido en la Reserva Federal en Washington el 24 de julio de 2025. Foto oficial de la Casa Blanca por Daniel Torok


En este contexto la cotización de los bonos (tanto de corto como de largo plazo) están en baja mientras que los rendimientos, que ya venían en ascenso desde fines de la pandemia, han pegado un nuevo salto y están en niveles similares a los de 2008-2009 cuando la crisis de las …

author: anred
title: Elecciones en Berlin
content:
17 partidos se han candidateado para las elecciones de la 20 ͣ Cámara de Diputados de Berlín y de las asambleas de Consejales de distrito este Domingo 20 de Septiembre. Las elecciones se celebran en un escenario bastante crítico: La crisis de la vivienda, como uno de los principales problemas, un candidato se baja de su candidatura por duras críticas a su gestión, otro candidato está envuelto en una acusación de soborno. Esto sucede en un contexto de falta de credibilidad en la política, debido a que los gobiernos anteriores no han cumplido con sus promesas y porque el Estado de Bienestar empieza lentamente a desaparecer y se empiezan a visibilizar un menor poder adquisitivo por parte de sus habitantes. Por un lado el gobierno multiplica los subsidios para la seguridad y la armamentística, pero por el lado recorta en educación, salud y cultura. Están llamados a las urnas 2,5 millones de berlineses. Muchos habitantes migrantes están excluídos del derecho a votar. Sólo los ciudadanos de la Comunidad europea, pueden votar, pero solamente, en una de las doce asambleas de consejales de distrito. Estas son algunas de las problemáticas que definirán dondé pondrán su voto las y los habitantes de Berlín.

Por Ana Muro, corresponsal de ANRed en Alemania


Las elecciones se celebran en un escenario bastante crítico:

La crisis de la vivienda

, como uno de los principales problemas, un candidato se baja de su candidatura por duras críticas a su gestión, otro candidato está envuelto en una acusación de soborno.


Con el gran apagón de enero, quedó evidenciado que el alcalde y ex candidato principal de la CDU, Kai Wegner, había mentido y dado datos erróneos sobre su gestión de la crisis. El 10 de Julio, a raiz de las fuertes críticas, Wegner se retiró como candidato principal de su partido CDU. Esto no solo había debilitado gravemente a Wegner a título personal, sino también a su partido.

Varios apagones y sabotages sucedieron en los últimos años, como expresión de disconformidad de la política alemana en relación a su apoyo incondicional al gobierno de Israel.


El grupo anarquista Vulkan y la campaña Switch Off se adjudicaron la autoría de ellos: «Switch off contra la codicia por la energía, Switch off contra la gestión digital de la vida, Switch off contra el progreso de la destrucción». No es la primera vez que los «Grupos Vulcano» y «Switch Off» se citan mutuamente.

El complejo de la megafábrica Tesla también sufrió daños.


Otro hecho que toma parte para la campaña electoral: El 25 de julio, una mujer fallece y muchas otras personas resultan gravemente heridas en la marcha del orgullo Christopher Street Day en pleno centro de Berlín. Una persona devota del Islam es acusada de embestir con un coche a la gente que estaba marchando. El atentado hace que, a corto plazo, el tema de la seguridad interior cobre mayor protagonismo en la campaña electoral.


Las personas candidatas


El Partido CDU cambió a su candidato muy sobre la fecha, luego de que Wagner se retirase de su candidatura, y propuso al senador de Hacienda y Cultura Stefan Evers, que mostró su política antimigrantes sin tapujos. Stefan Evers concedió una entrevista televisiva y realizó polémicas declaraciones sobre el atentado en la marcha del orgullo al acusar a La Izquierda de “negación de la realidad” en lo que respecta al islamismo y también mostró preocupación por el “creciente odio hacia los judíos”. Evers ha encontrado su tema principal para la campaña electoral: su política antimigrantes, la advertencia sobre La Izquierda como “riesgo para la seguridad de la capital del país” y la criminalización a la solidaridad con Palestina.


La candidata principal del partido de izquierda Die Linke, Elif Eralp, puede convertirse en la primera mujer jefa de gobierno de la ciudad autónoma de Berlin de origen migrante. Ella acusó a la CDU de “dividir a la ciudad y preferir mimar a los propietarios codiciosos en lugar de hacer algo para combatir la crisis del mercado inmobiliario”. El partido de izquierda-Die Linke- desde las últimas dos elecciones -defiende el tema que más importa a los votantes de la ciudad: la vivienda y los alquileres y es el partido de los que tienen más chances, según las encuestas. En las elecciones pasadas tuvieron un resultado exitoso e inesperado de más del 9%.


Cada vez se perfila con mayor claridad una pugna por el primer puesto. La CDU y La Izquierda llevan semanas codo con codo, y últimamente La Izquierda lleva una ligera ventaja.

title: Απάντηση Νίκου Μαζιώτη στην πρέσβειρα των ΗΠΑ Κίμπερλι Γκίλφοϊλ
content:
ΑΠΑΝΤΗΣΗ ΤΟΥ ΝΙΚΟΥ ΜΑΖΙΩΤΗ ΣΤΙΣ ΔΗΛΩΣΕΙΣ ΓΚΙΛΦΟΪΛ


Επ’ ευκαιρίας των δηλώσεων της πρέσβειρας των ΗΠΑ, Κίμπερλι Γκίλφοϊλ, για την αποφυλάκισή μου, θέλω να πω τα εξής: όταν ο εχθρός κάνει τέτοιες δηλώσεις, τότε σημαίνει ότι είμαι στον σωστό δρόμο! Θα άρχιζα να ανησυχούσα αν έκανε επαινετικές δηλώσεις για το άτομό μου!


Πράγματι, δεν έχω θέση σε μια κοινωνία και σε ένα σύστημα που μέσα από την ορολογία του «πολιτισμο» εννοούν την υποταγή, την καταπίεση, την δουλεία, τον ρατσισμό, την ανισότητα, τους πολέμους, τις γενοκτονίες λαών, την καταστροφή της φύσης και της γης. Άτομα όπως η Κίμπερλι Γκίλφοϊλ, αυτά  θεωρούν ως «πολιτισμό» και «δημοκρατία».


Από την άλλη μεριά, είναι υποκρισία να με χαρακτηρίζει «τρομοκράτη» η εκπρόσωπος των πραγματικών αρχιτρομοκρατών, των σφαγέων των λαών, των ιμπεριαλιστών, αυτών που βομβαρδίζουν και δολοφονούν αμάχους στο Ιράν, παλιότερα στο Ιράκ και το Αφγανιστάν, αυτών που εξοπλίζουν το Ισραήλ για να δολοφονεί δεκάδες χιλιάδες αμάχους Παλαιστίνιους στη Λωρίδα της Γάζας.


Είναι οι ίδιοι που παλιότερα βομβάρδιζαν το Βιετνάμ και βρίσκονταν πίσω από κάθε φασιστικό-δικτατορικό καθεστώς, στην Λατινική Αμερική, την Ασία, και την Αφρική, αυτοί που εκπαίδευαν τους βασανιστές και στήριζαν τα τάγματα θανάτου. Είναι οι ίδιοι που βασάνιζαν κρατούμενους στο Γκουαντάναμο και στο Αμπού Γκράιμπ μετά την επίθεση της 11/9/2001 και την κήρυξη του πολέμου κατά της «τρομοκρατίας».


Έχει θράσος η εκπρόσωπος της Αυτοκρατορίας να μιλάει, όταν το κράτος της μέσω του ΔΝΤ επέβαλε στον ελληνικό λαό το απεχθές καθεστώς δουλοπαροικίας μέσα από τα μνημόνια που εξόντωσαν χιλιάδες πολίτες, την ίδια στιγμή που η ίδια έκανε αισχρές δηλώσεις για τον ελληνικό λαό, όπως ότι είμαστε τεμπέληδες.


Η πρέσβειρα των ΗΠΑ θα πρέπει να ξέρει ότι πολλοί σ’ αυτήν τη χώρα δεν ξεχνούν τον βρώμικο ρόλο που έπαιξε το κράτος της στην ιστορία αυτού του τόπου όπως στον εμφύλιο του 1947-’49 και τη δικτατορία του 1967-’74. Και θα πρέπει να λάβει υπόψη ότι παρά πολλοί σ’ αυτόν τον τόπο αλλά και διεθνώς χάρηκαν και επικρότησαν την επίθεση του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα με αντιαρματική ρουκέτα RPG στην πρεσβεία των ΗΠΑ το 2007. Με την επίθεση αυτή είχαμε απαντήσει στον τότε πρόεδρο των ΗΠΑ, Τζώρτζ Μπους τζούνιορ –που στο πλαίσιο του «πολέμου κατά της ‘‘τρομοκρατίας’’» είχε πει ότι «όποιος δεν είναι μαζί μας, είναι εναντίον μας» –ότι ΔΕΝ ΕΙΜΑΣΤΕ ΜΑΖΙ ΣΑΣ, ΕΙΜΑΣΤΕ ΕΝΑΝΤΙΟΝ ΣΑΣ! Όπως και πάρα πολλοί σ’ αυτόν τον τόπο!


Νίκος Μαζιώτης


20/9/2026

Απάντηση Νίκου Μαζιώτη στην πρέσβειρα των ΗΠΑ Κίμπερλι Γκίλφοϊλ

infolibre

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Remembering John Coltrane (1926-1967)
content:
Little of beauty has America given the world save the rude grandeur God himself stamped on her bosom; the human spirit in this new world has expressed itself in vigor and ingenuity rather than in beauty. And so by fateful chance the Negro folk-song—the rhythmic cry of the slave—stands to-day not simply as the sole American music, but as the most beautiful expression of human experience born this side the seas. It has been neglected, it has been, and is, half despised, and above all it has been persistently mistaken and misunderstood; but notwithstanding, it still remains as the singular spiritual heritage of the nation and the greatest gift of the Negro people.


W.E.B. Du Bois,

The Souls of Black Folk

, 1903


Whenever I make a change, I’m a little worried that it may puzzle people. And sometimes I deliberately delay things for this reason. But after a while I find there is nothing else I can do but go ahead.


John Coltrane (from J.C. Thomas,

Coltrane: Chasin’ the Trane,

 1975)


John Coltrane was born on the 23rd of September, 1926. The centenary of his birth serves as the occasion – though such an occasion should not be necessary – to remember and celebrate his music, and more. For this, humbly, we cite the writing and artistry of others.


We begin with a selection from writer Fred Moten and his work,

In the Break: The Aesthetics of the Black Radical Tradition

 (University of Minnesota Press, 2003). We follow with Amiri Baraka’s poem “I Love Music (For John Coltrane)”. We then turn to Cornell West and his reflections on a jazz-soaked philosophy and James Baldwin on the radicalness of love, from

The Fire Next Time

 (1962) and Toni Morrison on the immanence of love and grace, from

Beloved

 (1987) . And we close with a link to Coltrane’s album,

A Love Supreme

 (1965).


Fred Moten, from

In the Break: The Aesthetics of the Black Radical Tradition

 (2003)


Here, then, is one such disclosure, famously and infamously made by Frederick Douglass in his 1845

Narrative

. By way of a set of resonant nodal points along the massive trajectory it extends, I want to think about this disclosure as an unavoidable anticipation, the prefigurative response to an epochal counterfactual, the always already belated origin of the music that ought to be understood as the rigorously sounded critique of the theory of value.


I have often been awakened at the dawn of day by the most heart-rending shrieks of an own aunt of mine, whom he used to tie up to a joist, and whip upon her naked back till she was literally covered with blood. No words, no tears, no prayers, from his gory victim, seemed to move his iron heart from its bloody purpose. The louder she screamed, the harder he whipped; and where the blood ran fastest, there he whipped the longest. He would whip her to make her scream, and whip her to make her hush; and not until overcome by fatigue, would he cease to swing the blood clotted cowskin. I remember the first time I ever witnessed this horrible exhibition. I was quite a child, but I well remember it. I shall never forget it whilst I remember anything. It was the first of a long series of such out rages, of which I was doomed to be a witness and a participant. It struck me with awful force. It was the blood-stained gate, the entrance to the hell of slavery, through which I was about to pass. It was a most terrible spectacle. I wish I could commit to paper the feelings with which I beheld it. . . .


Aunt Hester had not only disobeyed his orders in going out, but had been found in company with Lloyd’s Ned; which circumstance, I found, from what he said while whipping her, was the chief offense. Had he been a man of pure morals himself, he might have been thought interested in protecting the innocence of my aunt; but those who know him will not suspect him of any such virtue. Before he commenced whipping Aunt Hester he took her into the kitchen, and stripped her from neck to waist, leaving her neck, shoulders, and back entirely naked. He then told her to cross her hands, calling her at the same time a d——d b——h. After crossing her hands, he tied them with strong rope, and led her to a stool under a large hook in the joist, put in for the purpose. He made her get upon the stool, and tied her hands to the hook. She now stood fair for the infernal purpose. Her arms were stretched up at their full length, so that she stood upon the ends of her toes. He then said to her, “Now, you d——d b——h, I’ll learn you how to …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Isaac Deutscher: Message of the Non-Jewish Jew
content:
The following article by the biographer of Stalin and Trotsky, whose writings on Russia and Eastern Europe appear regularly in periodicals throughout the world, is based on a lecture delivered in London last February during Jewish Book Week to the World Jewish Congress. This text, revised and extended by the author, appeared in 

Universities and Left Review

, and is reprinted here with the author’s permission. A summary of the lecture had previously appeared in the British 

Jewish Observer and Middle East Review.


I REMEMBER that when as a child I read the 

Midrash

 I came across a story and a description of a scene which gripped my imagination. It was the story of Rabbi Meir, the great saint, sage, and the pillar of Mosaic orthodoxy and co-author of the 

Mishna

, who took lessons in theology from a heretic Elisha ben Abiyuh, nicknamed Akher (The Stranger). Once on a Sabbath, Rabbi Meir went out on a trip with his teacher, and as usual they became engaged in deep argument. The heretic was riding a donkey, and Rabbi Meir, as he could not ride on a Sabbath, walked by his side and listened so intently to the words of wisdom falling from heretical lips, that he failed to notice that he and his teacher had reached the ritual boundary which Jews were not allowed to cross on a Sabbath. At that moment the great heretic turned to his pupil and said: “Look, we have reached the boundary—we must part now: you must not accompany me any further—go back!” Rabbi Meir went back to the Jewish community while the heretic rode on—beyond the boundaries of Jewry.


There was enough in this scene to puzzle an orthodox Jewish child. Why, I wondered, did Rabbi Meir take his lessons from the heretic? Why did he show him so much affection? Why did he defend him against other rabbis? My heart, it seems, was with the heretic. Who was he?,


I asked. He appeared to be in Jewry and yet out of it. He showed a curious respect for his pupil’s orthodoxy when he sent him back to the Jews on the holy Sabbath; but he himself, disregarding canon and ritual, rode beyond the boundaries. When I was thirteen or perhaps fourteen I began to write a drama on Akher and Rabbi Meir and tried to find out more about Akher’s character. What made him transcend Judaism? Was he a Gnostic? Was he the adherent of some other school of Greek or Roman philosophy? I could not find the answers, and I did not manage to go beyond the first act of my drama.


The Jewish heretic who transcends Jewry belongs to a Jewish tradition. You may, if you like, view Akher as a prototype of those great revolutionaries of modern thought about whom I am going to speak this evening—you may do so, if you necessarily wish to place them within any Jewish tradition. They all went beyond the boundaries of Jewry. They all—Spinoza, Heine, Marx, Rosa Luxemburg, Trotsky, and Freud—found Jewry too narrow, too archaic, and too constricting. They all looked for ideals and fulfilment beyond it, and they represent the sum and substance of much that is greatest in modern thought, the sum and substance of the most profound upheavals that have taken place in philosophy, sociology, economics, and politics in the last three centuries.


HAVE they anything in common with one another? Have they perhaps impressed mankind’s thought so greatly because of their special “Jewish genius”? I do not believe in the exclusive genius of any race. Yet I think that in some ways they were very Jewish indeed. They had in themselves something of the quintessence of Jewish life and of the Jewish intellect. They were 

a priori

 exceptional in that as Jews they dwelt on the borderlines of various civilizations, religions, and national cultures. They were born and brought up on the borderlines of various epochs. Their minds matured where the most diverse cultural influences crossed and fertilized each other. They lived on the margins or in the nooks and crannies of their respective nations. They were each in society and yet not in it, of it and yet not of it. It was this that enabled them to rise in thought above their societies, above their nations, above their times and generations, and to strike out mentally into wide new horizons and far into the future.


It was, I think, an English Protestant biographer of Spinoza who said that only a Jew could carry out that upheaval in the philosophy of his age that Spinoza carried out—a Jew who was not bound by the dogmas of the Christian churches, Catholic and Protestant, nor by …

author: Unknown
title: Musa Anter öldürüldüğü sokakta anıldı: “Yüzleşme kaçınılmaz”
content:
Gazeteci, yazar ve aydın Musa Anter, öldürülmesinin 34. yılında Diyarbakır’da anıldı.


Mezopotamya Ajansı’nın (MA) aktardığına göre Dicle Fırat Gazeteciler Derneği’nin (DFG) düzenlediği anma, Anter’in 20 Eylül 1992’de vurulduğu Yenişehir ilçesine bağlı Seyrantepe semtindeki Cumhuriyet Mahallesi’nde yapıldı.


Anmaya Anter’in ailesinin yanı sıra gazeteciler, siyasi parti ve sivil toplum örgütlerinin temsilcileri katıldı.


“Faili meçhul cinayetler aydınlatılmalı”


Anmada konuşan DFG üyesi Fexredin Kılıç, Anter’in öldürülmesinin üzerinden 34 yıl geçmesine rağmen cinayetin arkasındaki yapıların bütünüyle ortaya çıkarılmadığını söyledi.


Devam eden barış sürecine değinen Kılıç, geçmişteki faili meçhul cinayetlerle yüzleşilmesi gerektiğini belirtti:


Barışı konuştuğumuz bugünlerde, Apê Musa’nın katledildiği yerden bir kez daha ifade ediyoruz; barış için faili meçhul cinayetler aydınlatılmalıdır.


Kılıç, Anter’in ölümünün ardından Kürt basınında çalışan gazetecilerin öldürülme, gözaltı, tutuklama, tehdit ve yayın yasaklarıyla karşı karşıya kaldığını söyledi.


Anter’den Aykol’a


DFG Eşbaşkanı Selman Çiçek de 1 Ocak’ta hayatını kaybeden gazeteci ve yazar Hüseyin Aykol’u andı.


Aykol’un geçmiş yıllarda Anter için düzenlenen anmalara katıldığını belirten Çiçek, gazetecilik geleneğinin kuşaktan kuşağa aktarıldığını söyledi:


“Apê Musa’dan Hüseyin hocaya, Hüseyin hocadan bize, bizden diğer nesillere aktararak bu geleneği sürdüreceğiz.”


Anter’in oğlu Dicle Anter de babasını her yıl öldürüldüğü yerde anmaya devam edeceklerini söyledi.


Mızraklı: Adalet olmadan barış tesis edilemez


8 Eylül’de Edirne Cezaevi’nden tahliye edilen eski Diyarbakır Büyükşehir Belediyesi Eşbaşkanı Selçuk Mızraklı da anmaya katıldı. Mızraklı’nın tahliyesi farklı haber kaynaklarınca da doğrulandı.


Mızraklı, Anter’in Kürt basını ve toplumu açısından bıraktığı mirasa değinerek devam eden barış sürecinde geçmişle yüzleşmenin önemine dikkat çekti.


“Özellikle Barış ve Demokratik Toplum Süreci’yle birlikte barışın derinleşmesi, onurlu bir barışın tesisi için hakikatlerin ortaya çıkarılması ve yüzleşme kaçınılmazdır” diyen Mızraklı, adalet sağlanmadan kalıcı bir barışın kurulamayacağını söyledi.


Mızraklı, Kürtçe üzerindeki baskılara karşı yürütülen mücadeleyi hatırlatarak, “Artık binlerce Musa Anter var. Onun bıraktığı kalemle korkusuzca yazan, fotoğraf makinesini en zor anlarda kullanan binlerce gencimiz var” dedi.


Eren: “Özgür basın susmadı”


DEM Parti Diyarbakır Milletvekili Serhat Eren de Anter’in Kürt dili ve kültürü için verdiği mücadeleye değindi.


Anter’in öldürülmesinin ardından Kürt basınının çalışmalarını sürdürdüğünü söyleyen Eren, gazetecilerin gözaltı, tutuklama ve çeşitli baskılarla karşılaştığını belirtti.


Anma, Musa Anter’in öldürüldüğü yere fotoğrafının ve karanfillerin bırakılmasıyla sona erdi.


Musa Anter cinayeti


Musa Anter, 20 Eylül 1992 gecesi Diyarbakır’da silahlı saldırıya uğradı. Saldırıda Anter hayatını kaybetti, yanında bulunan Orhan Miroğlu ise yaralandı. Amnesty International, cinayetten iki gün sonra yayımladığı açıklamada Anter’in 20 Eylül’de öldürüldüğünü ve olayın koşullarının araştırılması gerektiğini bildirdi.


Cinayete ilişkin daha sonra açılan dava, JİTEM ana davasıyla birleştirildi.


Ankara 6. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi, 21 Eylül 2022’de Musa Anter’in öldürülmesi ve Orhan Miroğlu’nun yaralanmasına ilişkin davanın 30 yıllık zamanaşımı süresinin dolduğu gerekçesiyle düşürülmesine karar verdi. Mahkeme, JİTEM ana davasının ise ayrı bir dosya üzerinden sürmesine hükmetti.


Anter ailesinin avukatı, düşme kararının ardından yaşam hakkının ihlal edildiği gerekçesiyle Anayasa Mahkemesi’ne bireysel başvuruda bulundu.


(NÖ)

title: Iraq begins trial of six French ISIS members
content:
The trial of six French nationals accused of membership in the “Islamic State” (ISIS) began on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad. The defendants were transferred from northeastern Syria to Iraq earlier this year. Under tight security, armored military vehicles transported the six men to the Karkh Court of Appeal building. Vehicles carrying French diplomats arrived there later. Journalists were barred from attending the proceedings.


The identities of the six defendants have not yet been made public. They are part of a group of 47 French nationals transferred to Iraq from prisons run by the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria. The group also includes Adrien Guihal, who claimed responsibility on behalf of ISIS for the July 14, 2016 attack in Nice, in which 86 people were killed.


Proceedings against thousands of ISIS members


The trials of the French ISIS members are part of a much larger series of legal proceedings. By mid-February, more than 5,700 suspected ISIS members had been transferred from northeastern Syria to Iraq. According to Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, they represent 67 different nationalities, including 474 Iraqis and 3,497 Syrians. In early September, the Iraqi judiciary announced that the interrogations and investigations involving all 5,704 defendants had been completed. Their cases are now being referred individually to the competent courts based on the evidence available in each case.


According to the judiciary, the defendants also include individuals who held leadership positions as well as military, security-related, or media roles within ISIS. In at least six cases, the investigations also uncovered links to the capture, enslavement, abduction, or sale of Yazidi women who were abducted from Shengal during the ISIS genocide in August 2014.

author: Jeremy Ray Jewell
title: A Singapore Contract, Beijing’s Red Lines
content:
APPLY TO TEACH for Polly English and, before entering a classroom, the platform presents a screen titled “Sensitive Content Compliance Agreement.” Under “DO NOT Talk about,” it prohibits discussion of “Political issues, including Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macao, Xizang (Tibet), and Xinjiang.”

The next section is harder to dismiss as ordinary classroom etiquette. Under “Consequences of Violation,” the screen lists “Immediate termination of my Service Agreement,” “Potential legal action,” and “Responsibility for any resulting damages.” It does not say what kind of legal action, which damages might qualify, or how far those consequences reach. A teacher working outside the PRC is asked to accept an open-ended legal and financial warning for discussing some of Beijing’s most sensitive political questions.

Nothing on that screen is presented as PRC law. Polly English describes itself as an online English teaching company based in Singapore, and its teacher terms name Little Moon Pte. Ltd. as the contracting party and place the agreement under Singapore law and Singapore courts. That makes the arrangement more revealing, not less: recognizable PRC political red lines appear inside a private contract governed somewhere else.

The ambiguity lands in a context in which Beijing has increasingly asserted that politically defined conduct can be punished even when the accused is outside territory under its effective control. In June 2024, five PRC authorities issued guidelines allowing trials in absentia for alleged separatist offenses related to Taiwan independence. In 2026, Article 63 of the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress turned to organizations and individuals outside the PRC. They may be held legally liable for acts against the PRC that are deemed to undermine ethnic unity and progress or to create ethnic division. Amnesty International calls its core prohibitions broad and undefined; the European Parliament reads its extraterritorial reach as allowing prosecution abroad.

There is no publicly available evidence that Polly is enforcing those laws, or that any Chinese authority instructed the company to write this agreement. The mechanism is what matters. A platform can absorb political pressure originating in one market, convert it into a private contractual rule, and place the risk on workers in another jurisdiction. This is not only a story about Beijing’s reach, but about how platform work is built: nominal independence for the worker, centralized rule-making for the company. Political restrictions are the conspicuous cargo. The machinery that carries them already governs labor, and it does not stop at borders. That makes what Nick Srnicek and others have called “platform capitalism” more than a labor question. It is a question of political sovereignty.

Polly recruits English-speaking teachers, largely from North America and the Philippines, for one-to-one classes. Its recruitment portal runs on a Chinese country-code domain, and the apps are distributed through app stores in the PRC. The consumer site is in Simplified Chinese, selling lessons with American and Canadian schoolteachers to parents who sign a course subscription agreement on the same domain.

Plenty of employers tell staff to keep politics out of the classroom, and in a service for children that would be unremarkable. But Polly’s list names five specific places, and those five are the territorial, sovereignty and ethnic-political questions Beijing treats as core red lines. Four turned up in the 2018 Marriott episode, when a customer survey listing Tibet, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan as countries prompted Shanghai’s cyberspace regulator to order Marriott’s Chinese website and app shut for a week, the same year the civil aviation regulator instructed 44 foreign airlines to relabel Taiwan.

One of those names is written “Xizang (Tibet).” Since a State Council white paper in November 2023, PRC state media have systematically substituted “Xizang” for “Tibet” in English, a shift Tibetan groups read as displacing an internationally established name. Terminology alone proves nothing about who drafted the clause, but the ordering is worth noticing: the PRC’s preferred term leads, the internationally recognized one trails in brackets. A company that presents itself to recruits as Singapore-based has adopted Beijing’s sequence.

Corporate self-censorship to preserve Chinese market access is old news: a boycott, an apology, a firing. Roy Jones, the Marriott …

title: Fon soruşturması: 4 şirket için MASAK'a yeni inceleme talebi
content:
İstanbul Başsavcılığı tarafından yürütülen fon soruşturmasında mali incelemenin kapsamı genişletildi. Terörizmin Finansmanı ve Aklama Suçları Soruşturma Bürosu, Mali Suçları Araştırma Kurulu Başkanlığına (MASAK) resmi yazı göndererek dört aracı kurum ve holding ile alt şirketlerinin yöneticilerine ilişkin ayrıntılı mali verilerin iletilmesini talep etti.

Savcılık talimatında, Pusula Finans Holding AŞ, Tera Yatırım Menkul Değerler AŞ, Hedef Holding AŞ ve Bulls Yatırım Menkul Değerler AŞ ile bağlı şirketlerinin yöneticilerinin kimlik bilgilerinin çıkarılması istendi. İnceleme kapsamında, söz konusu yöneticilerin 2024 yılından bugüne kadar yurt dışına yaptıkları tüm para ve kripto varlık transferleri ile hesaplarındaki nakit akışlarının ham veri olarak dosyaya sunulması talep edildi.

Mali inceleme yalnızca şirket yöneticileriyle sınırlı tutulmadı, yöneticilerin birinci derece yakınlarının para ve kripto hareketleri de kapsama alındı. Soruşturmayla, şüphelilerin doğrudan ya da aile üyeleri üzerinden yurt dışına kaynak aktarıp aktarmadıklarının tespiti amaçlanıyor.

Gizlilik kararı bulunan dosya kapsamında son olarak Pusula Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Serdar Turhan, Tera Yatırım Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Emre Tezmen ile Alper Öztürk, Emre Alkin ve Kerem Alkin gözaltına alınmıştı.

Daha önce Pusula Portföy Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Muhammed Yarız ve Destek Yatırım Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Altunç Kumova’nın da aralarında bulunduğu dört şüpheli tutuklanmış, 51 kişi hakkında ise adli kontrol kapsamında yurt dışına çıkış yasağı getirilmişti.

Öte yandan Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), soruşturmayla bağlantılı yedi portföy yönetim şirketine ait 131 yatırım fonunu TEFAS işlemlerine kapatarak tasfiye sürecini başlatmıştı.
